name: FloodRoot
description: An explicit scope for the neutral dark foundations profile.
code:
<FloodRoot>
  <Text>Your workspace starts here.</Text>
</FloodRoot>
notes: Import @flood-md/react/styles.css once at the application entry.
This root selects neutral/dark locally. Legacy controls outside it keep their earlier theme behavior.

name: Text
description: Role-based interface text, from introductory copy to small supporting details.
code:
<Stack gap="3">
  <Text as="p" size="lead">Quarterly revenue</Text>
  <Text as="p" size="compact">Revenue increased by 8% this quarter.</Text>
</Stack>
notes: Use Text for readable copy and DescriptionList for labeled facts about one record. In a set of peer labels and values, keep each role consistent. Use weight to separate roles without turning every value into a heading.
Use as="p" for paragraphs. The label size does not create a form association.
Use wrap=pretty on short blocks of supporting prose when ordinary wrapping leaves an awkward last line. Keep labels, table cells and long editing content on their normal wrapping behavior.
Subtle is a supplementary tone; evaluate small required instructions against the actual background and font size.

name: Timestamp
description: A semantic date or time with consistent metadata typography.
code: <Timestamp dateTime="2026-11-14T09:30:00Z" format="date-time" lang="en-GB" />
notes: Provide YYYY-MM-DD for a civil date, or an ISO timestamp with an explicit offset for a moment in time. Civil dates retain their day. Instants display in timeZone, which defaults to UTC. lang defaults to English for generated text.

Pass relativeTo for elapsed time against an explicit zoned instant. After four elapsed weeks, the component uses the requested absolute format. Update the reference in the host if the readout needs to change while the page is open.
Set showExactTime with relativeTo to disclose the exact instant on hover or keyboard focus. Keep exact time visible by default when readers have to compare precise event times.
Pass explicit text as children for a host-owned presentation, such as a short schedule time. The component preserves the native dateTime.

name: NumericValue
description: Format a number with tabular figures and optional space for its expected width.
code: <NumericValue value={999} reserveFor={-9999} lang="en" />
notes: Use in measurements, counters and numerical columns. Supply a finite number or a bigint for an exact large integer. Native NumberFormat options control separators, rounding, units and currency. The data element preserves the underlying value.
Use reserveFor only where changing width moves neighboring content. Choose a representative widest value in the same notation, including signs, grouping, fractions or currency where they may appear.

The value can grow beyond the reserve. Align end for comparable values or start when the figure is read from a shared leading edge. When values could outgrow the available width, define the wrapping or overflow behavior in the enclosing composition.
Use Duration when elapsed time needs a fixed unit and MoneyField when the user edits an exact monetary amount.

name: Duration
description: A localized elapsed measurement with a fixed unit and machine-readable milliseconds.
code: <Duration milliseconds={2107.797} unit="millisecond" maximumFractionDigits={3} />
notes: Use for measured latency, execution time or another elapsed interval. Keep one display unit and precision across comparable values. Sort using the original milliseconds, not the displayed label.

Supply finite nonnegative milliseconds, including zero when it was measured. Omit the component for an unknown duration. A positive measurement that would round to zero displays below the smallest visible increment.
Use lang to localize decimal separators and units. Styling inherits from the surrounding text, and the data element keeps the original milliseconds. Use Timestamp for a civil date or event time.

name: TimestampLink
description: A date or time that opens the specific comment, event or record it describes.
code:
<Comment id="export-review" tabIndex={-1} author={{
  name: "Maya Chen",
  metadata: <TimestampLink href="#export-review" dateTime="2026-11-14T09:30:00Z" aria-label="9:30 AM, link to Maya Chen’s comment" format="time" />,
}}>
  The original export is attached to the review.
</Comment>
notes: Use in secondary metadata when people need a stable link to this entry. Use Timestamp for a date or time that only provides context.
Supply the record URL or a fragment pointing to a document-unique ID. For a same-page target such as a comment, use tabIndex={-1} on the target so native fragment navigation can focus it.
When repeated times give links the same name, provide a localized aria-label containing the visible timestamp and identifying the destination. Use absolute time when exact timing is part of the task.

name: HighlightText
description: Inline highlights that show why a plain-text result matches a search.
code: <HighlightText query="export">Export settings are included in the monthly export.</HighlightText>
notes: Pass plain text as children and the literal query. Matching is case-insensitive by default. Empty queries leave the text unmarked.
Use for visible matches in a result title or excerpt. The host owns filtering, ranking and any tokenization. Highlighting preserves the original text and does not add focus targets.

name: TruncatedText
description: One line of text that discloses the full value only when clipped.
code: Workspace activity export for October 2026.csv
notes: Give it plain text and a bounded parent width. It inherits the typography of the row or field around it.
The full value remains in the DOM. Hover or focus reveals the same value in a Tooltip only when it is clipped. Text that fits does not add a Tab stop.
Set preserveEnd to a small character count when nearby identifiers differ at the end. Check that the whole distinguishing suffix fits at the intended width.
Use tooltipSide to place the full value away from nearby metadata or controls. The tooltip centers along that edge. The default is bottom, and viewport edges can shift or flip the overlay.
Keep enough of the label visible to distinguish it from nearby values. Use wrapping or ExpandableText for passages and values which need their full text in the normal reading flow.

name: ExpandableText
description: A plain-text excerpt that expands in place when it exceeds a line limit.
code: <ExpandableText lines={3}>The export covers the full billing period. The original file contains the individual entries and payment reference for each invoice.</ExpandableText>
notes: Use in card previews, comments, and activity feeds where a longer plain-text passage is optional to scan. Keep required instructions and decision-making details visible.
The button appears only when text exceeds the line limit at the actual rendered width. The default is three lines. Localize moreLabel and lessLabel.
Use expanded and onExpandedChange for host-owned state, or defaultExpanded for an initially open excerpt. The same paragraph stays mounted throughout.
The disclosure action follows the ellipsis in the last visible line. If a wider layout fits the full text and the focused action disappears, focus moves to the passage.
Links, lists and rich content belong in a disclosure such as Collapsible. The browser retains the full plain text for assistive technologies.

name: Heading
description: Semantic heading levels with an independent visual scale.
code:
<Stack gap="4">
  <Heading level={2} size="page">Workspace settings</Heading>
  <Heading level={3} size="section">Notifications</Heading>
</Stack>
notes: Use the surface title for the task and a consistent section heading size for peer groups. Use Section to compose a named group with body content.
Choose level for document structure and size for appearance.
Use wrap=balance when a short multiline title reads better with similar line lengths. Choose the right heading size and width first. Avoid inserting manual line breaks to balance translated text.
Display is a large marketing role. Keep page and section sizes for ordinary product interfaces.

name: Stack
description: Vertical composition with spacing from the shared token scale.
code:
<Stack gap="4">
  <Heading size="section">Project</Heading>
  <Text as="p">One place for your work.</Text>
</Stack>
notes: The parent owns the gap between its children.
Spacing keys are strings and use rem. Flood does not reset the host root font size.

name: Inline
description: A wrapping horizontal group for related content and actions.
code:
<Inline gap="2" align="center">
  <Button>Save changes</Button>
  <Button variant="subtle">Cancel</Button>
</Inline>
notes: Inline wraps when its children need more space.
Use the same control size for neighboring actions of the same level.
Rows center items by default. Use gap="4" between independent choices; gap="2" remains available for tightly related content.

name: Surface
description: A quiet container with semantic elevation and token-based padding.
code:
<Surface elevation="raised" padding="6">
  <Text>Everything in its place.</Text>
</Surface>
notes: Elevation describes appearance. Overlay does not create a dialog, portal or focus trap.
Prefer grouping and spacing before adding more nested containers.

name: Divider
description: A semantic separator with a low-emphasis visual line.
code:
<Stack gap="4">
  <Text>Workspace</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text>Account</Text>
</Stack>
notes: The line is decorative in contrast terms: content grouping must remain understandable without seeing it.
Divider renders a native hr; it has no orientation prop.

name: Button
description: Native actions with a clear prominence, size and interaction state.
code:
<Inline gap="2">
  <Button>Save changes</Button>
  <Button variant="subtle">Cancel</Button>
  <Button loading>Saving</Button>
</Inline>
notes: Button defaults to type="button". Set submit or reset deliberately inside forms.
Loading blocks activation and sets aria-busy. Use loading="retain-focus" for an in-place operation that should keep keyboard focus and button dimensions. The host owns completion announcements.
Prefer subtle for standalone secondary actions; ghost belongs in a clear parent context.
Buttons use content width, including inside Stack. Opt into a full-width action with style={{ inlineSize: "100%" }} only when the composition calls for it.

name: IconButton
description: An icon-only action with a required accessible name.
code:
<IconButton label="Add idea">
  <Plus />
</IconButton>
notes: Provide a meaningful action label, rather than the name of the glyph.
Supply a licensed SVG. IconButton wraps it in a decorative IconSlot sized to the control.
Connect onClick to your host action. The interactive preview adds a local count; the basic usage snippet only shows composition.

name: IconLink
description: An icon-only link for navigation and downloads.
code:
<IconLink href="/docs/installation" label="Read the installation guide">
  <ArrowRight />
</IconLink>
notes: Provide a destination or outcome in label and use a recognizable decorative icon. Use a text Link when the glyph alone would be ambiguous.
IconLink keeps native anchor behavior and shares target and glyph sizing with IconButton. Use IconButton for commands and IconLink for navigation or downloads.

name: Link
description: A native anchor for navigation.
code: <Link href="/docs/installation">Install Flood</Link>
notes: Use a button for state-changing actions and a link for navigation.
Link forwards native anchor attributes. Its optional solid/subtle/outline/ghost variants share Flood Button geometry; text is the unchanged default. No asChild API.

name: ProfileLinks
description: A compact list of destinations attached to a public profile.
code: <ProfileLinks items={[{id:"website",label:"Website",href:"https://example.com"},{id:"newsletter",label:"Newsletter",href:"https://example.com/newsletter"}]} featuredId="website" />
notes: Use below a profile identity or bio when people can go directly to the listed resources. Supply short, distinct destination labels with stable IDs. Icons are optional and decorative.

Use featuredId for one deliberate primary destination. Keep the item order meaningful on desktop and narrow screens. The links wrap rather than hiding destinations behind a menu, and an empty list renders nothing.
The host validates user-submitted destinations. Use LinkPreview when a reader needs a source and excerpt to decide whether to visit.

name: LinkPreview
description: A single linked resource with its title, source and optional excerpt and thumbnail.
code:
<LinkPreview
  href="https://flood.md/components/line-chart"
  title="Line charts in Flood"
  source="flood.md"
  description="Compare series and inspect exact values across a shared time axis."
  thumbnailSrc="/charts-share.png"
/>
notes: Use LinkPreview in a conversation, activity feed or curated list when a source and short plain-text excerpt help readers decide whether to visit. Use inline Link when context already identifies the resource, or FileCard for a file with its own preview and actions.

The whole preview is one native anchor. Give the destination a recognizable title and identify the publisher or domain in source. Native anchor attributes and the forwarded ref belong to this anchor. Place save or menu commands beside the preview.

The host supplies the destination and metadata. Optional thumbnailSrc displays decorative art and preserves its frame when loading or when the image fails. Omit it for a text-only preview. The title, excerpt and source wrap to fit the available width.

name: PublicationPreview
description: Preview an article and subscribe to its publication through separate actions.
code: <PublicationPreview publication="Flood release notes" title="What's new in charts" href="https://flood.md/docs/charts" excerpt="How to compare related series and inspect exact values." subscription={{subscribed, onSubscribedChange: setSubscribed}} />
notes: Use for an article shared in a feed or curated list when readers can follow the publication from there. Use LinkPreview for a single linked resource without a publication action.
The title links to the article. The independent button changes the subscription for the publication named beside it. Omit subscription when that action is unavailable in context.

Set pending while the host processes a change, keep the last accepted subscribed value until the host confirms the result, and handle failures outside the card. Localize visible action labels and the accessible name with labels and formatActionLabel.

name: FilteredImage
description: Show, blur or omit an image according to a viewer’s media preference.
code: <FilteredImage image={{src:"/gallery/still-life.jpg",alt:"A ceramic vase in blue light"}} ratio={1.5} visibility="blur" blurredLabel="AI-generated image blurred" />
notes: Use for display preferences on classified images. Show and Blur keep the same aspect ratio. Blur shows a display-safe label and gives it to assistive technology in place of the original alternative text.
Hide renders no image. When galleries wrap tiles in links or list items, filter the whole record before rendering so hidden items leave no empty focus targets.
Blur is a presentation treatment. The image remains loaded. Use host authorization and omit restricted sources. Use ContentAdvisory when an individual item should offer deliberate reveal.

name: ContentAdvisory
description: A warning with deliberate, reversible reveal of sensitive content.
code:
<ContentAdvisory
  title="Story spoiler"
  description="This paragraph describes the ending."
  showLabel="Show ending"
  hideLabel="Hide ending"
>
  <Text as="p">The missing notebook was in the train station locker.</Text>
</ContentAdvisory>
notes: Use for content the reader may choose to see after a specific warning. Use Collapsible for ordinary optional sections or Alert when all information should remain immediately visible.

Children mount only while revealed and unmount again when hidden. Keep persistent child state in the host and key the advisory to the subject if the same view changes records. The host applies moderation preferences, access checks and any prefetch decisions.

Pass mediaRatio for a single inline image or video with a known width-to-height ratio. The concealed frame becomes the media frame, and the action above keeps its position. Keep ordinary paragraphs and multi-item content in the default presentation.
The warning and native Show or Hide button stay in place. Use revealed and onRevealedChange together for controlled state. Provide localized action labels when needed.

name: Citation
description: An inline marker that reveals the evidence behind a nearby claim.
code:
<Text as="p">Damaged returns require a photo.{' '}<Citation
  label="1"
  title="Returns inspection policy"
  source="Operations handbook · § 4.2"
  excerpt="Attach a photo of the damage before marking the item as unsellable."
  href="/handbook/returns#inspection"
/></Text>
notes: Place Citation immediately after the claim it supports. Keep the visible label short and give the evidence a recognizable title. Use LinkPreview when the destination is presented as a separate resource card.
Click, tap, Enter or Space opens the evidence and focuses its native link. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the marker. className and the forwarded ref belong to the trigger.
Supply the evidence title, source identifier, destination and an optional short excerpt. The host owns source retrieval, permissions and the destination.

name: SearchResultItem
description: A result link with an optional excerpt that shows where the record matches.
code: <DataList aria-label="Search results"><SearchResultItem title="Resolve duplicate invoices" context="BIL-204" href="/issues/bil-204#comment-18" query="export" excerpt={{source:"Comment",text:"We can reproduce the duplicate rows in the monthly export."}} /></DataList>
notes: Use inside DataList for linked workspace search results. Keep the record title as the link and pass the specific matched location when available.
Give each result one short, complete excerpt around its relevant match. Pass a field label when a match in a comment or other secondary field would be surprising.

Pass query for literal highlighting, or excerpt.query if the service identifies a different literal term in the excerpt. Omit a term for a semantic match without a literal one. The host owns filtering, ranking and snippet selection.

name: SourceList
description: An evidence list with optional citation markers, publisher context and excerpts.
code: <SourceList label="Sources" sources={[{id:"policy",marker:"1",title:"Returns inspection policy",source:"Operations handbook · § 4.2",href:"/handbook/returns#inspection"}]} />
notes: Use to scan the supporting evidence for a response or document. Keep Citation near the specific claim and use the same visible marker in the list when they refer to the same source.

Supply the publisher or document location and a short excerpt when it helps identify the evidence. Omit href when there is no authorized destination. The host supplies safe links and evidence, and decides source order.
An empty list renders no surface. The surrounding article, Drawer or panel supplies its own heading and handles the no-source state when it matters.

name: FormActions
description: A form footer with grouped actions and space for operation feedback.
code: <FormActions primary={<Button type="submit">Save</Button>} secondary={<Button type="reset" variant="subtle">Discard changes</Button>} />
notes: Use at the end of a native form. Pass existing Button components with explicit submit, reset or button types. The host owns validation, submission and reset.
Keep the primary action at the end of its action group. Feedback can sit alongside it on wide layouts and move to a separate line when space runs out.

Use layout=status-below to keep action and feedback alignment while reserving one line for the status slot. Use layout=stacked for full-width buttons in a narrow form. The action order stays the same.
Use the status slot for brief operation feedback such as SaveStatus. Keep field errors attached to their fields and put longer errors above the action row.

name: SaveBar
description: A persistent save and discard panel for forms with an unsaved draft.
code: <SaveBar form="project-settings" state="dirty" />
notes: Use the default viewport placement when the end of a long form may be out of view. Place the bar near the view root, outside transformed or clipped containers. Reserve enough bottom clearance in the scroll owner for the last field. Use inline placement within an overlay or a constrained panel.
Pass the target form ID when rendering outside that form. Save and Discard use native submit and reset, so the form owns validation, persistence, controlled field reset and navigation guards.

Drive state from the real draft and request. Change to clean after successful save or reset. Keep the draft on error, supply a useful state label and allow retry. If saving or resetting hides the focused bar, return focus to a persistent form control.

name: SaveStatus
description: Compact feedback for unsaved, saving, saved and failed changes.
code: <SaveStatus state="saving" />
notes: Set state from the actual draft or save operation. Show saved only after the host accepts the change. Idle has no default message.
Place near the form actions or in a document header when work saves automatically. Supply label to localize the message or describe the specific outcome.
Disable announce when another owner already announces the same state. Keep recovery instructions or field errors in their existing feedback components.

name: Field
description: The association between a visible label, its input and supporting messages.
code:
<Field label="Project name" required hint="Visible to your team.">
  {(control) => <Input {...control} name="project" />}
</Field>
notes: Spread the supplied control props onto one Input, Textarea, Select or compatible control.
Field merges describedBy with hint/error IDs and forwards native required through its function child.
Use labelAside for an optional action beside the label, such as HelpTip. Required instructions and errors belong in the field's visible descriptions.

Use layout=adaptive for an editable preference in an inspector or SettingGroup. The label and hint share one column, the control and feedback another. The same control stacks below the label when space is limited.
The host owns validation rules. Compose Field in a client component in Next.js.
Field is not a generic native div wrapper and does not forward a ref.

name: Input
description: A native input with semantic styling and independent visual sizing.
code:
<Field label="Workspace name">
  {(control) => <Input {...control} defaultValue="My project" />}
</Field>
notes: Use Field or a native associated label; placeholder text is not a label.
controlSize changes appearance. The native numeric size attribute keeps its HTML meaning.
Default outlines use the quiet field.border role. field.boundary is a stronger opt-in; preserve the independent focus indicator when customizing colors.

name: Select
description: A Flood choice field with its own popup and native form integration.
code:
<Field label="Visibility">
  {(control) => (
    <Select {...control} name="visibility" defaultValue="private">
      <option value="private">Private</option>
      <option value="team">Team</option>
    </Select>
  )}
</Field>
notes: Single selection uses a Flood trigger and listbox, including the popup. Native options and optgroups supply the choices; disabled choices cannot be selected.
Use arrows, Home/End and typing to navigate; Enter or Space confirms, Escape cancels. The popup scrolls active choices into view.
Select fills its Field; constrain the form or field wrapper. Multiple and numeric size greater than one use a native inline listbox rather than a popup.
A native form bridge preserves name, value/defaultValue, required, disabled, onChange and HTMLSelectElement ref. Inspect the matching guide for the visible focus contract.

name: Textarea
description: Native multiline input for notes and longer text.
code:
<Field label="Project note" hint="Keep it short and useful.">
  {(control) => <Textarea {...control} rows={3} maxLength={500} />}
</Field>
notes: Rows, maxLength, value/defaultValue and form props remain native.
Use autoGrow for short notes that can grow as people type. Rows sets the starting line count; maxRows bounds automatic growth.
The default has no resize grip. Long text scrolls inside the field; a host can opt into native resizing with style={{ resize: "vertical" }}.

name: MessageComposer
description: A chat draft with send, file attachments and a stop action in the same control.
code: <MessageComposer label="Message" placeholder="Write a message…" value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft} onSend={() => setDraft("")} />
notes: Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. IME confirmation stays in the editor. A blank draft can send when it has attachments.
Supply onFilesSelect to enable a multiple-file picker. Validate and store the files in the host, and pass accepted names with stable IDs to attachments.

Use maxVisibleAttachments to collapse longer lists in a constrained composer. The count reveals the remaining files, which stay attached when collapsed. Localize the list and disclosure with attachmentsLabel, moreAttachmentsLabel and fewerAttachmentsLabel.
Keep the draft controlled. While streaming, provide onStop to replace Send with Stop in the same slot. After a failed send, keep the draft and files available for retry.

Use layout=compact when the editor and send action usually fit side by side. Actions move below the editor when their labels and the available width call for more room. Pass replyContext for a compact context header above the same input surface. CommentComposer uses this composer with compact comment defaults.
Mount MessageComposer outside other forms. The composer renders its own form.
Use leadingActions for controls that affect this draft before sending, such as ReplyAudience. Make those controls non-submit actions and pass their disabled state from the host.
Pass suggestions to offer @ mentions and / commands at the caret without replacing the composer.

name: Checkbox
description: A labeled native checkbox for independent choices.
code: <Checkbox label="Send project updates" name="updates" defaultChecked />
notes: Use checked/onChange for controlled state or defaultChecked for native state.

Keep labels visible in forms. Use hideLabel when the record or column supplies the context, and pass a specific accessible label. Disabled does not mean read-only; explain unavailable choices outside the disabled control when needed.

The control and visible label form one content-width unit with an 8px-at-16px-root internal gap. Use an explicit parent gap="4" (16px at that root) between units; the glyph keeps its token-defined size.
indeterminate sets the native mixed state after hydration; checked still controls form submission. The host owns select-all aggregation and updates. Radio and Switch do not expose this prop.

name: Radio
description: A labeled native radio for one choice within a group.
code:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Visibility</legend>
  <Radio label="Private" name="visibility" value="private" defaultChecked />
  <Radio label="Public" name="visibility" value="public" />
</fieldset>
notes: Radios in one group share a name. The host supplies fieldset and legend.
Native browser keyboard and form behavior remain available.

The control and visible label form one content-width unit with an 8px-at-16px-root internal gap. Use an explicit parent gap="4" (16px at that root) between units; the glyph keeps its token-defined size.

name: Switch
description: A labeled on/off setting with native checkbox form behavior.
code: <Switch label="Email notifications" name="notifications" defaultChecked />
notes: Switch uses a native checkbox with role="switch".
checked/defaultChecked, name/value, reset and disabled remain native. The component does not persist settings.
Use readOnly for a locked value that should remain focusable and submit with the form. Space and pointer activation cannot change it.
Use layout=row for a settings list with a shared trailing switch axis. An optional description is announced separately from the switch name. The native label remains clickable.

The control and visible label form one content-width unit with an 8px-at-16px-root internal gap. Use an explicit parent gap="4" (16px at that root) between units; the glyph keeps its token-defined size.

name: SwitchGroup
description: A native form group for related on/off preferences.
code:
<SwitchGroup legend="Notifications">
  <Switch layout="row" label="New assignments" name="assignmentAlerts" defaultChecked />
  <Switch layout="row" label="Weekly summary" name="weeklyDigest" />
</SwitchGroup>
notes: Compose row switches inside one native fieldset. Each switch has its own state, name and optional description. The host owns persistence and when changes are saved.
Set disabled on the whole group when it is unavailable. A child Switch can be readOnly when only its value is locked and the rest of the group remains editable.
Choose compact or comfortable density. Dividers default to off. Use SettingGroup for a mix of switches, values and independent actions.

name: SettingGroup
description: A named section of settings with shared row spacing.
code: <SettingGroup title="Notifications"><Switch layout="row" label="Weekly summary" /><SettingRow label="Delivery history" action={<Link href="/notifications">View history</Link>} /></SettingGroup>
notes: Compose SettingRow for actions, row-layout Switch for on/off values, and Field layout=adaptive for editable scalar settings. Use Fieldset when controls share a form legend or validation boundary.

Choose layout=aligned in a mixed settings panel when direct adaptive Fields and SettingRows should share the same columns and stack at the same group width. Row-layout switches keep their trailing position.
Choose headingLevel for the surrounding page. Use spacing to separate rows by default. Enable dividers when dense adjacent items are hard to distinguish.

name: SettingRow
description: A setting label and optional explanation with an independent trailing action.
code: <SettingRow label="Account access" description="Control who can sign in." action={<Link href="/settings/access" variant="subtle" size="sm">Manage access</Link>} />
notes: Use SettingRow for one setting that opens a detail view, runs an independently named action, or shows a current value. Name the action for what it does.

The adaptive layout puts value and action together beneath the description when there is too little room. Long values wrap within their share of the row. Use inline only where the label and action still fit. Use stacked for a consistently narrow surface.
Opt into valueOverflow=truncate for a plain secondary value whose visible prefix is meaningful. It reveals the full text when clipped. Rich values keep their original layout.
Use Switch layout=row for an on/off preference and Field for a labeled editable value. Use the same trailing axis across related settings.
Give the row a description only if it explains a consequence, scope or constraint. The action owns focus and activation.

name: CodeSnippet
description: Selectable, wrapping code with an optional host-owned action.
code: <CodeSnippet prompt="$" code="git status --short" />
notes: CodeSnippet escapes code content and uses the semantic system monospace font stack.
Use prompt for a decorative shell marker. Pass the original code to the copy action.
The host implements copy behavior, failure handling and feedback. No clipboard or network API runs inside the component.
Code text defaults to LTR independently of parent layout. codeDirection can be ltr/rtl/auto; native dir still controls the wrapper and action layout.

name: IconSlot
description: Consistent geometry for a host-supplied SVG icon.
code: <IconSlot size="md"><ArrowRight /></IconSlot>
notes: No glyph pack ships in the React package. Keep the license of the host's icon artwork.
Without label the slot is decorative. With label it exposes role="img" and an accessible name.
Use an SVG rather than a text character. Avoid inline SVG sizing styles that override the slot.

name: IconSwap
description: Swap decorative glyphs in the same icon slot when an action changes state.
code:
<IconButton label="Mute notifications" aria-pressed={muted} onClick={() => setMuted(!muted)}>
  <IconSwap state={muted ? "muted" : "on"} icons={{
    on: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><path d="M18 8a6 6 0 0 0-12 0c0 7-3 7-3 9h18c0-2-3-2-3-9M10 21h4" /></svg>,
    muted: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><path d="M18 8a6 6 0 0 0-12 0c0 7-3 7-3 9h18c0-2-3-2-3-9M10 21h4M3 3l18 18" /></svg>,
  }} />
</IconButton>
notes: Place IconSwap inside IconButton or IconSlot, which owns the glyph box. Provide decorative glyphs with stable keys for a small set of known states.
The active key changes immediately. Glyphs fade and scale in the same box, without queued callbacks. Reduced motion switches immediately.
The containing control supplies its name, selected state or result announcement. Do not place interactive or independently named content inside the glyphs.

name: ScrollArea
description: Native scrolling with inset overlay scrollbars that preserve content width.
code:
<ScrollArea aria-label="Recent activity" style={{ maxHeight: "12rem" }}>
  <Stack gap="4">
    <Text>Project created.</Text>
    <Text>Workspace updated.</Text>
  </Stack>
</ScrollArea>
notes: Scrollbars overlay the viewport with an inset; they do not reserve a content gutter. Give the viewport an explicit height or maxHeight to produce vertical overflow.
The forwarded ref, className, style and native div props belong to the scrollable viewport. Supply a visible context or accessible label for keyboard users.

Wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling remain native. Default contentInset="scrollbar" keeps text and full-width rows clear of rails with inner padding, without shrinking the viewport. Explicit none allows edge-to-edge content when the host already provides safe padding. Rails automatically avoid rounded clipping corners.
Forced colors restores native scrollbars as an accessibility fallback. Verify horizontal and RTL content, resizing and zoom in the host composition.

name: Label
description: A native label that connects a visible name to a control.
code:
<Stack gap="2">
  <Label htmlFor="project-label">Project name</Label>
  <Input id="project-label" defaultValue="My project" />
</Stack>
notes: htmlFor connects the label to a matching control ID; implicit nested controls also retain native behavior.
required adds a decorative marker only. Set required on the actual control as well. Field already composes Label.

name: Fieldset
description: A native group with a legend, shared descriptions and disabled form behavior.
code:
<Fieldset legend="Notifications" hint="Choose the updates you want.">
  <Checkbox label="Product updates" name="updates" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Release notes" name="releases" />
</Fieldset>
notes: Uses a real fieldset and legend, with a ref to HTMLFieldSetElement. Disabled descendants retain native form semantics.
The browser exempts controls in the first legend from inherited disabling. Avoid interactive legend contents unless this is intentional.
hint, message, error and external aria-describedby IDs are merged without duplicates. Error takes precedence over an advisory status.
Group status describes the group; it does not mark every child invalid, manage selected values or implement a RadioGroup/CheckboxGroup.

legendSize="section" gives an independent form section a 1rem semibold title and a 1rem body inset. The default "label" remains a compact choice caption; neither option changes native group semantics.
Use layout=aligned for direct Field children with short controls and a shared label and value axis. Groups narrower than 21rem place labels above the fields.

name: RadioGroup
description: A named single-choice group with native radio keyboard and form behavior.
code: <RadioGroup name="visibility" legend="Visibility" options={[{ value: "private", label: "Private" }, { value: "team", label: "Team" }]} defaultValue="private" />
notes: Composes Fieldset and existing native choice controls. The ref targets HTMLFieldSetElement; options need unique values and visible labels.

value/onValueChange is controlled; defaultValue initializes an uncontrolled group. Native form reset restores uncontrolled defaults without firing onValueChange; controlled values remain owned by the host.
name belongs to the inputs. The form prop associates every input with an external form. Disabled options and groups follow native submission rules.
RadioGroup supports native required. CheckboxGroup returns repeated name/value entries; validate minimum/maximum selections in the host and explain errors through status/message.

name: CheckboxGroup
description: A named multiple-choice group with a shared array value and native form behavior.
code: <CheckboxGroup name="notifications" legend="Notifications" options={[{ value: "updates", label: "Product updates" }, { value: "releases", label: "Release notes" }]} defaultValue={["updates"]} />
notes: Composes Fieldset and existing native choice controls. The ref targets HTMLFieldSetElement; options need unique values and visible labels.

value/onValueChange is controlled; defaultValue initializes an uncontrolled group. Native form reset restores uncontrolled defaults without firing onValueChange; controlled values remain owned by the host.
name belongs to the inputs. The form prop associates every input with an external form. Disabled options and groups follow native submission rules.
CheckboxGroup has no required/min/max shortcut: a required checkbox means that specific checkbox. Validate the selected array in the host and use group status/message.

name: ButtonGroup
description: Connected actions with shared edges and ordinary keyboard focus.
code:
<ButtonGroup label="Editing actions">
  <Button variant="subtle">Undo</Button>
  <Button variant="subtle">Redo</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
notes: Use direct Button/IconButton children with compatible sizes. The group owns connected radii and single separators; actions keep their props and handlers.
label names the group. Tab follows normal button order; this is not a toolbar, menu or selection group.
Horizontal is default; vertical stacks actions. Content can wrap within a button. Conditional/hidden actions preserve the visible end corners. No clipping masks focus.

name: SaveToCollection
description: A split action for a quick personal save and independent collection membership.
code: <SaveToCollection label="Save lighting reference" saved={false} collections={[{id:"lighting",label:"Lighting",selected:false},{id:"studio",label:"Studio",selected:true}]} onSavedChange={(saved) => console.log(saved)} onCollectionChange={(id, selected) => console.log(id, selected)} />
notes: Use when someone can keep a resource with one press and optionally organize it in named collections. The primary action toggles its accepted personal save state.

Supply accepted membership for each collection. Its checkbox stays in the same menu so several memberships can change during one visit. Use stable IDs and disable collections that the viewer cannot edit. An empty list disables only the collection trigger.

The host owns all persistence and decides when personal saves and collection memberships affect each other. pending retains focus on the primary action during a save request. Report a failed request through host feedback.
Give each action group a contextual label and localize the action names. Prefer a searchable collection picker for a large or paged collection library.

name: SplitButton
description: A connected default action and menu of related alternatives.
code:
<SplitButton label="Export report" menuLabel="Export formats" items={[{id: "csv", label: "Export CSV"}, {id: "json", label: "Export JSON"}]} primaryButtonProps={{ onClick: exportPdf }} onAction={exportFormat}>
  Export PDF
</SplitButton>
notes: Use when one command is an established default and the adjacent menu offers alternatives for the same task. Use Menu alone when the user needs to choose before any command runs.
Give the group and the chevron localized names. Tab reaches both controls independently, arrow keys enter the menu, and Escape returns focus to the chevron.
primaryButtonProps applies only to the main action, including type, disabled and loading. Use disabled on SplitButton to disable both controls. An empty items array disables the menu trigger.

name: InputGroup
description: One native text input with logical start/end content inside a shared perimeter.
code:
<Field label="Website">
  {control => <InputGroup {...control} start="https://" placeholder="example.com" />}
</Field>
notes: Ref, id, name, value, events and ARIA attributes target the real input. className/style customize the outer layout wrapper.
start/end are logical content slots. Adornments do not become the submitted value or an accessible label; use Field or Label and explain prefixes when needed.
The input has one shared field perimeter and accent focus. Interactive adornments keep their own focus indication and accessible names.
disabled/readOnly affect the input; host-owned addon actions need their own disabled policy. Use compatible action sizes. Text-like input types are supported; Textarea/Select are separate constructs.

name: Toggle
description: A native button with a persistent pressed state.
code: <Toggle defaultPressed>Bold</Toggle>
notes: Keep the accessible name stable; Enter/Space toggle pressed. Supports controlled pressed/onPressedChange or defaultPressed.

name: ToggleGroup
description: Optional single or multiple selections exposed as pressed buttons.
code: <ToggleGroup label="Text formatting" defaultValue={["bold"]} options={[{value: "bold", label: "Bold"}, {value: "italic", label: "Italic"}]} />
notes: Tab reaches each enabled action. Arrows/Home/End move focus without selecting. Single selection can be cleared.
Use RadioGroup for form choices and tabs for switching panels. ToggleGroup does not submit form values.

name: SegmentedControl
description: A compact single-value choice or collection view switcher with native radio semantics.
code: <SegmentedControl label="Claims view" name="claims-view" defaultValue="pending" options={[{value: "pending", label: "Pending", count: 2}, {value: "reviewed", label: "Reviewed"}]} />
notes: Uses original RadioGroup behavior and native inputs.
Arrow keys move focus and select; Home/End select endpoints, skipping disabled segments. Selecting the current value does not clear it.
Use SegmentedControl to switch a shared collection between mutually exclusive views. Use Tabs for associated content panels and ToggleGroup for optional pressed actions.

An option count can communicate workload without a nested badge or a second control. Counts are read with visible labels, preserve zero, and are omitted in icon-only mode. Format localized counts before passing them.
Native name/form/required, reset and controlled values are preserved.

name: Collapsible
description: A named disclosure button and retained show/hide panel.
code: <Collapsible title="Advanced settings">Additional project settings.</Collapsible>
notes: Use open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen. The panel stays mounted and hidden when closed; hidden form controls keep native form semantics.
Title is plain text for a stable button name. Content may be interactive. Disabled prevents trigger activation, not interaction inside an open panel.
Use headerMeta for noninteractive context or status in the trigger. Put separately focusable controls in headerAction.
Use variant=flush for a disclosure nested in a Drawer or activity feed. Hover emphasizes the title without introducing a filled rectangle. The panel expands and collapses in place.
Use triggerWidth=fit for a short disclosure label in a wide feed. The chevron stays beside the label while the panel uses the available width.

name: Accordion
description: Related disclosure sections with optional single or multiple expansion.
code: <Accordion label="Questions" items={[{value:"install",title:"How do I install Flood?",content:"Install the packages and import the stylesheet."}]} />
notes: Headings contain native disclosure buttons. Set headingLevel for the surrounding document.
Enter/Space toggle. Tab visits available triggers and open panel contents. ArrowUp/Down and Home/End move among enabled top-level triggers without opening panels.
Use variant=flush for collapsible inspector sections on a shared surface. The section separators stay visible. Use Section with headingSize=group for content that should stay visible.

name: Tooltip
description: Brief text help on hover or focus, with collision-aware placement.
code: <Tooltip content="Additional context" trigger={trigger => <Button {...trigger}>Hover or focus</Button>} />
notes: Requires native Popover API.
Forward trigger props and ref to one actual button. Tooltip is text-only; interactive content belongs in Popover.
Use positionReference to place the tooltip beside a containing row while the original target still owns hover and focus.
Escape dismisses. Hover can move onto the tooltip; focus stays on the trigger. Do not use it as the only accessible name or essential instruction.

name: Popover
description: A nonmodal contextual dialog in the native top layer.
code: <Popover title="Project settings" trigger={trigger => <Button {...trigger}>Settings</Button>}>Project details.</Popover>
notes: Forward all trigger props and ref.
Escape, outside pointer and focus leaving dismiss. Focus enters content and returns when appropriate; Tab is not trapped.
Closed content unmounts; keep persistent data in the host. Uses native Popover API within the existing DOM/theme scope.

name: HelpTip
description: An inline help action that reveals brief, optional context on demand.
code:
<Field label="Project prefix" labelAside={<HelpTip label="About project prefixes" content="The prefix appears at the start of issue IDs, like SN-42." />}>
  {control => <Input {...control} name="prefix" />}
</Field>
notes: Use for optional definitions and examples. Keep instructions needed to fill a field in its visible hint, and keep validation visible beside the field.
Choose a label that names the subject of the help. The icon opens on click, touch and keyboard activation. Escape returns focus to the opener.
Place it beside a native label through Field labelAside. A label click still focuses its input. Use the full Popover component for content with actions.

name: Dialog
description: A named native modal dialog with inert background and managed focus.
code: <Dialog title="Create a project" trigger={trigger => <Button {...trigger}>Open dialog</Button>}>Project details.</Dialog>
notes: Uses native showModal, not a simulated modal div.
Escape closes the top layer; outside closing can be disabled independently. Tab remains inside the dialog.
Use getFallbackFocus to resolve a surviving focus target when the opener disappears or becomes unavailable on close.
Closed content unmounts. Forward trigger props/ref; initialFocusRef can select a safe initial control. Modern native dialog support is required.

name: Tabs
description: Connected tab buttons and retained content panels with roving keyboard focus.
code: <Tabs label="Project sections" items={[{value:"overview",label:"Overview",content:"Project context."},{value:"activity",label:"Activity",content:"Recent updates."}]} />
notes: Use variant="line" for page-level sections with an active marker beside the panel. The default contained variant joins tabs and content in one surface.
Arrow keys navigate enabled tabs; automatic activation is default, manual needs Enter/Space. Tab leaves the tablist. Horizontal direction follows RTL.

Enable overflowControls on a horizontal tablist to show named scroll arrows when tabs overflow. The arrows reveal the next or previous hidden tab without changing selection. Partial tabs at the edges are hidden, and long tab names truncate within their buttons.

Supply count for a passive panel total. The badge caps the display and assistive technology receives the exact value. Localize that description with formatCountLabel. Icon-only tabs use a dot when the count is positive.
Inactive panels remain mounted but hidden. Keep form validation and persistent selection under host control. Invalid, missing or disabled selected values fall back to the first available item.

name: TableOfContents
description: In-page navigation that marks the section currently being read.
code: <TableOfContents items={[{id:"setup",label:"Setup",children:[{id:"tokens",label:"Import tokens"}]},{id:"verify",label:"Verify"}]} />
notes: List stable heading IDs in document order. Nest child items to reflect the actual heading hierarchy. Native fragment links preserve deep links.
Automatic tracking follows the document by default. Pass scrollRootRef to track the viewport of a ScrollArea. Use activationOffset to set a minimum inset in CSS pixels.
Pass activeId to control the current location, or null to suppress the current marker. Use NavigationList for links between pages.

name: Breadcrumb
description: A path of native links and an explicit current page, with an optional compact layout.
code: <Breadcrumb items={[{label:"Workspace",href:"/"},{label:"Projects",href:"/projects"},{label:"Flood"}]} />
notes: The last item is current, with or without an href. Separators are decorative and not focusable.
Use layout=compact in a narrow header. It keeps the root and current page visible, and lets people open earlier pages through a named popover. maxVisibleItems counts path labels, with two by default.
Compact labels fit a single line and reveal the full text when clipped. The earlier pages keep native links and original order. Localize overflowLabel.
Links keep browser navigation semantics. The host owns actual routes and client routing.

name: EnvironmentSwitcher
description: A compact context switcher that keeps the accepted environment and its scope visible.
code: <EnvironmentSwitcher label="Environment" environments={[{id:"primary",label:"Primary",scope:{label:"Production",tone:"warning"}},{id:"checkout",label:"Checkout rewrite",scope:{label:"Preview"}}]} value="primary" onValueChange={id => console.log(id)} />
notes: Place EnvironmentSwitcher in persistent workspace chrome when the selected environment changes the scope of subsequent actions. Use Select for an ordinary form field and CollectionViewSwitcher for saved collection views.
Use a visible scope label when the environment name is ambiguous. Keep text available for production identification and use tint as a secondary cue.

The value reflects the host-accepted environment. onValueChange requests a switch. The host owns navigation, permission checks, unsaved work and errors. Disabled rows stay visible for context; an empty set leaves the trigger disabled.

name: Pagination
description: Controlled page navigation with bounded page windows, buttons or native links.
code: <Pagination page={1} pageCount={20} getHref={page => `?page=${page}`} />
notes: Use getHref for native route links, onPageChange for local controlled data, or both for a navigation notification. Modifier clicks retain browser behavior.
Page and pageCount must be positive safe integers within range. Empty datasets can omit Pagination. siblingCount 0/1/2 controls the numbered window; endpoints are noninteractive when unavailable.

Use presentation=compact to show position between arrows. Use presentation=arrows when a nearby range already provides visible context. Localize digits with formatPage and position text with positionLabel.

name: CursorPagination
description: Previous and next controls for collections with an unknown total.
code: <CursorPagination label="Activity pages" position="26–50" previous={{href:"?before=event-26"}} next={{href:"?after=event-50"}} />
notes: Provide a previous or next target only when the corresponding cursor is available. Pass href for route navigation or onSelect for a host-owned request.

Use position for the actual loaded range, when known. The host owns cursors, requests and errors. Pass pending while a callback request runs and keep the active target present so its button keeps focus.

name: CardDeck
description: Step through a small stack of related cards with visible controls.
code: <CardDeck label="Chart examples" selectedId={selectedId} onSelectedChange={setSelectedId} items={[{id:"line",label:"Line chart",content:"Compare trends over time."},{id:"bar",label:"Bar chart",content:"Compare named categories."}]} />
notes: Use when related cards are browsed sequentially and one at a time. Keep a valid selected ID, supply distinct card names and preserve the meaningful reading order.
Only the current card is mounted. Keep drafts or values that must survive navigation in the host. Use loop to wrap at the first and last card. The controls keep focus when activated.
Use Grid when readers need to compare cards side by side and ImageGallery for opening media in a dedicated viewer. The deck’s position is user-controlled.

name: RecordNavigator
description: Previous and next record destinations drawn from the current ordered results.
code: <RecordNavigator label="Adjacent requests" previous={{title:"Review access logs",href:"/requests/41"}} next={{title:"Audit export retention",href:"/requests/43"}} />
notes: Use for neighbors of the open record in the actual filter and sort order. Pass previous and next only when those records are reachable. The navigator disappears when neither exists.
Compact arrows fit a detail header. Use presentation="labeled" when people should see destination titles before navigating. Longer titles can truncate visually while remaining in the accessible name.

Use href for a real route and onSelect for host-owned in-place navigation. Move focus to the new detail heading after a host transition when the original control becomes unavailable. Use CursorPagination for collection pages and ResponseVariants for versions of one response.

name: ResponseVariants
description: Switch between existing versions of one response with compact controls.
code: <ResponseVariants label="Response versions" value={versionId} onValueChange={setVersionId} variants={[{id:"short",content:"Retain exports for 30 days."},{id:"detailed",content:"Delete exported copies 30 days after creation."}]} />
notes: Use for alternate versions of one reply or generated result. Supply stable version IDs in host order and keep the selected ID valid whenever at least one version exists.
The controls disappear with a single version. Reaching an endpoint keeps focus on the unavailable arrow and suppresses repeat activation. Localize previousLabel, nextLabel and formatPosition.
Only the selected version is mounted. Keep drafts, branch history, generated data and any per-version state that needs to survive in the host. Composition of message actions belongs to the parent.

name: Badge
description: A compact, noninteractive label for status and metadata.
code: <Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
notes: Use Badge for a category, qualifier or priority. Keep the size and variant consistent for every value in the same priority column, including the ordinary value. Use StatusIndicator for lifecycle state and Tag for removable values.
Place a badge beside the name it qualifies. Use a quiet tone unless color conveys meaning, and check the longest label next to its neighbors at the intended width.
Use text to communicate status; color is supplementary.
Tone, size and visual variant are independent. This is not a selectable or removable chip.
Available in 0.2.4. Use FloodRoot for the neutral dark recipe.

name: CountBadge
description: A compact count with an optional cap or unread dot.
code: <Inline gap="2"><Text size="compact">Inbox</Text><CountBadge count={137} formatLabel={count => `${count} unread messages`} /></Inline>
notes: Use CountBadge for a passive count beside the destination or label it qualifies. It adds no focus stop. Use formatLabel for a localized accessible description.
The default visual cap is 99. Counts above max display the cap with a plus sign while assistive technology receives the exact count. Use locale to format the digits.
Zero is hidden by default. Set showZero when an explicit zero is useful. Dot presentation signals a nonzero count in tight spaces and always hides zero.
Use NavigationItem compactBadge to put an unread dot on a compact navigation control without moving its icon.

name: Spinner
description: A sized loading indicator with an optional accessible status label.
code: <Spinner label="Loading workspace" />
notes: Standalone indicators expose a status with a localizable label. Decorative indicators are hidden from assistive technology.
Button loading uses this indicator decoratively and keeps the button name. Do not announce every spinner in a busy area.
Use Progress when completion is measurable. Reduced motion stops rotation. Available in 0.2.4.

name: LoadingState
description: A visible loading message that shares spacing and layouts with empty and error states.
code: <LoadingState label="Loading project activity…" layout="row" density="compact" />
notes: Use when a region has no accepted content to display and a visible label explains what is being loaded. Use Skeleton when the future content structure is known and a matching placeholder preserves its layout.

Match the layout and density to the adjacent empty or failed states. Use actions for an actual available choice, such as cancelling an interruptible operation. The host owns cancellation and accepted data.

The spinner is decorative. Keep announce off inside a region that already announces loading. Set announce when the visible message is the sole status region. The host marks the content region busy and owns focus throughout the request.

name: CardSkeleton
description: A loading placeholder with the same layout and density as Card.
code: <CardSkeleton description headerAction footerAction />
notes: Match density, elevation, description, header action, footer action and the expected number of short body lines to the real Card. Use bodyLines={0} for a card without a body.
Use descriptionLines to reserve the expected number of lines in a wrapping description. It overrides the single-line description flag.
Pass mediaRatio when the loaded card has a top media slot. Use the same ratio in the real card to preserve the image frame.
Pass reserveSelectionSpace when the loaded Card has selection. It uses the same header track with a decorative placeholder and no focusable checkbox during loading.
The placeholder is decorative. Announce loading once for the surrounding region, including when loading multiple cards. Keep populated cards visible during a background refresh.

name: FileCardSkeleton
description: A first-load placeholder for a file card, with the same thumbnail, selection and footer tracks.
code: <FileCardSkeleton thumbnailRatio={4 / 3} reserveSelectionSpace footerActions={2} />
notes: Match thumbnailRatio, thumbnailPlacement, density and headingSize to the loaded FileCard. Set reserveSelectionSpace when that card will be selectable.
Use descriptionLines to reserve the expected number of lines in a wrapping description at the gallery's card width.

Set metadata according to whether a format or size is expected. Count preview, download and remove in footerActions only when they appear in the footer. Use previewOnThumbnail when preview belongs on the artwork.
Action placeholders reserve the same target size as file commands on fine and coarse pointers.

The placeholder has no interactive controls. Announce the first load once for the gallery. If file details are already available while only the artwork loads, render FileCard with its stable thumbnail fallback.

name: FileListSkeleton
description: Loading placeholders that follow file-row thumbnails, metadata and commands.
code: <FileListSkeleton label="Loading attachments…" appearance="plain" rows={3} row={{metadata:"plain",actions:1}} />
notes: Use while a panel or plain FileList first loads, such as the attachments in a review drawer. Pass the same appearance, density and dividers as the ready list.
Use a row count and repeated row shape for a uniform list. Use an array of shapes to vary metadata, secondary text and action count.
One announcement identifies the pending list. The thumbnails and command slots are decorative and inherit the file family's responsive layout and touch dimensions.

name: ListSkeleton
description: Loading rows that share the spacing and tracks of a data list.
code: <ListSkeleton label="Loading activity…" rows={3} media description metadata dividers={false} />
notes: Use during the initial load of a DataList. Match the number of expected rows, density, media, descriptions, metadata and dividers to the destination list.
Set reserveSelectionSpace when the loaded DataList has a checkbox track. The skeleton keeps the title aligned without exposing an interactive checkbox.
The placeholder list is decorative. Localize the loading announcement through label. Keep that message outside any ancestor marked aria-busy.
Leave the current results in place during a background refresh. For a DataTable body, use loadingAppearance=skeleton on DataTable.

name: TableSkeleton
description: Loading rows with real table headings and matching column widths.
code:
<TableSkeleton caption="Workspace projects" rows={4} columns={[
  {id:"project",label:"Project",width:"70%",placeholderLines:2},
  {id:"members",label:"Members",width:"30%",align:"end"}
]} />
notes: Use during initial loading of a plain Table. Keep the expected column widths, caption, density and row count. Use placeholderLines=2 where the eventual cell has a title and secondary line.
Body placeholders are decorative. TableSkeleton marks its table busy and announces loading once by default. Use announce=false when the host already owns that message.
For DataTable, use its skeleton loading appearance and column placeholderLines so selection, resize and other column tracks keep their geometry.

name: Skeleton
description: A decorative placeholder that reserves space for loading content.
code:
<Stack gap="2">
  <Skeleton width="65%" />
  <Skeleton />
  <Skeleton width="80%" />
</Stack>
notes: Always hidden from assistive technology. The host owns loading announcements and aria-busy on the relevant region.
Width and height accept CSS dimensions; style overrides them. Match the final content geometry.
Animation can be disabled; reduced motion and forced colors disable the pulse. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Avatar
description: A stable identity image with initials or an explicit text fallback.
code: <Avatar name="Alex Morgan" />
notes: In an authored row, keep the visible author, timestamp and message together. Use decorative when the author name is already visible. Place any per-message action in that item.
Name supplies the accessible image name; decorative suppresses duplicate naming next to an equivalent visible name.
Fallback remains visible until the image loads and after a load error. Changing src starts a fresh load lifecycle.

Pass presence with an online, away, busy or offline state and a localized label. Omit it for unknown availability. A decorative Avatar needs the label supplied by its surrounding composition. Use visible status text when availability affects an action.
Native span props and ref target the root. Size and shape do not change during loading. Available in 0.2.4.
Use xs in dense choice rows and 2xs inside tags.

name: Progress
description: Completion of a task, with a determinate or unknown value.
code: <Progress label="Uploading files" value={60} valueText="60%" />
notes: Omit value for indeterminate progress. The accessible progressbar omits aria-valuenow in that state.
Max defaults to 100; values must be finite and inside 0..max. Invalid ranges throw instead of silently inventing a percentage.
hideLabel removes the caption visually while keeping the accessible name. valueText supplies human-readable units.
Use layout=inline in compact panels and rows. The track moves below the caption when it cannot retain a readable length. The default layout is stacked.
This is not a live region or a task manager. Native div props, className/style and ref target the wrapper. Available in 0.2.4.

name: ProgressRing
description: Circular task progress for compact rows, cards and panels.
code: <ProgressRing label="Exporting files" value={60} valueText="6 of 10 files" />
notes: Use ProgressRing for a single task with a compact circular track. Use Progress when a horizontal track can use the available width, and DonutChart for categories as parts of a whole.
The ring shares Progress range semantics. Max defaults to 100. Omit value for indeterminate progress; 0 and max represent empty and complete tracks.
Supply localized valueText for a visible amount or an indeterminate state. hideLabel hides the caption and keeps its accessible name and value text. Size accepts sm, md and lg.
Progress is host-owned. The ring has no tab stop or live announcement. Reduced motion keeps an indeterminate arc visible without rotation.

name: ConnectionDetails
description: Connection methods with an exact, copyable string and the matching parameters.
code: <ConnectionDetails title="Connect to Postgres" profiles={[{ id: "direct", label: "Direct connection", connection: "postgresql://postgres:[PASSWORD]@db.studio.example:5432/studio" }]} />
notes: Supply display-safe strings with credential placeholders and stable, unique profile IDs. The host owns authorization, provisioning, and secret retrieval.

Give each method a short description when the choice depends on the client environment. Pass unavailableReason for a blocked method so users can inspect the reason without seeing or copying an endpoint.

Switching methods updates the exact clipboard value and parameters together. Supply value and onValueChange for host-controlled selection, or defaultValue for a starting method. If the selected profile is removed, the selector prompts for another method and withholds connection data.
A single method has no selector when already selected. With no methods, the panel shows its empty label.
Use parameters for individual facts people need to enter in a client. Use CopyableValue for a standalone endpoint or identifier.

name: ServiceEndpointList
description: Read and copy a service’s public and private network addresses in one list.
code: <ServiceEndpointList label="Network addresses" endpoints={[{id:"web",label:"Web",scope:"public",protocol:"HTTPS",address:"https://sync.example.com"},{id:"proxy",label:"TCP proxy",scope:"public",protocol:"TCP",address:"edge-gateway.example.net:14386"},{id:"internal",label:"Service discovery",scope:"private",protocol:"DNS",address:"warehouse-sync.production.internal"}]} />
notes: Use when operators need to compare several addresses for one service. Give each row a distinct purpose and supply its actual visibility and protocol.
Pass a credential-free address with its exact hostname and port. An endpoint can have a status before an address is available. It exposes a copy action only once the host supplies an address.
The host owns provisioning, access scope, connectivity and ordering. Use ConnectionDetails for a selected connection method and its parameters.

name: ReplicationStatus
description: Compare database roles, reported health and observed read-replica lag.
code: <ReplicationStatus label="Database nodes" nodes={[{id:"fra",label:"Frankfurt",role:"primary",status:{label:"Available",tone:"success"}},{id:"sin",label:"Singapore",role:"replica",status:{label:"Behind",tone:"warning"},lagMilliseconds:8400}]} />
notes: Use for one primary and its read replicas, or a replica-only view. Keep node IDs stable and pass the reported status independently from the lag measurement.
Omit lagMilliseconds for an unavailable measurement. Zero is a measured value. Choose one lagUnit for the list and use lang and labels to localize the display.
Use ServiceEndpointList when the task is to read or copy addresses. The host owns polling, stale-data policy, lag thresholds and routing or failover decisions.

name: DomainVerification
description: A custom domain setup panel with exact, independently copyable DNS names and values.
code: <DomainVerification domain="api.example.com" status={{label:"Waiting for DNS",tone:"warning"}} records={[{id:"cname",type:"CNAME",name:"api",value:"service.example.net",status:{label:"Found",tone:"success"}},{id:"txt",type:"TXT",name:"_verify.api",value:"project-verification=example",status:{label:"Pending",tone:"neutral"}}]} />
notes: Supply record names and values in the form the user should paste into their DNS provider. Exact values wrap and copy individually. Localize the field and copy labels if needed.

Per-record states diagnose the expected DNS entries. Use the section status for the overall domain outcome and action for a host-owned check or activation. The host owns DNS resolution, asynchronous checking, errors and persistence.
Use this panel when someone needs the exact DNS configuration and verification state. Use DescriptionList to display ordinary domain metadata.

name: MilestoneProgress
description: A compact readout for a named milestone, its completed work and an optional target date.
code: <MilestoneProgress name="Public beta" completed={6} total={10} dueDate={{label:"Nov 24",dateTime:"2026-11-24"}} />
notes: Use beside other milestones in project summaries, sidebars and details panels. Use Progress or ProgressRing for progress of a single task such as an upload.

Supply counts from the same snapshot: completed and total are nonnegative whole numbers, with completed no larger than total. An empty scope uses emptyLabel. Zero completed items in a nonempty scope show the exact count.
Supply a localized dueDate label and formatProgress for the host locale. Progress is already stated in text, so the ring is decorative. Only the name becomes a link when href is supplied.

name: CycleProgress
description: Compare completed work with the changing scope of one work cycle.
code: <CycleProgress name="Cycle 42" initialScope={20} observations={[{label:"Mon",completed:2,scope:20},{label:"Tue",completed:5,scope:20},{label:"Wed",completed:8,scope:24}]} />
notes: Use in cycle details when changes to scope affect how progress should be read. Use MilestoneProgress for a compact snapshot without history.

Supply equally spaced observations in chronological order, with completed and scope from the same snapshot. Use one unit for both series and initialScope. The latest observation supplies the visible current totals.
Preserve final cycle observations as a historical snapshot. Reflect later changes to live issue records in the issue list when relevant. A cycle without observations shows the empty state.
Use formatWork for a localized unit and labels for headings and chart navigation. The shared LineChart supports exact values with pointer and keyboard.

name: Meter
description: A measured value within a meaningful, finite range.
code: <Meter label="Storage used" value={75} valueText="75 of 100 GB" />
notes: Use Meter for storage, battery or other bounded measurements; use Progress for task completion.
Value is required. Min defaults to 0 and max to 100; require min < max and min <= value <= max. Invalid values throw.
Use valueText for meaningful units; hideLabel keeps the accessible name. Tone is host-owned and does not calculate warning thresholds.
Use reference for one named point on the same scale. The mark does not change the measured value or threshold behavior. Its label describes the point and is associated with the meter.
Use layout=inline to place the caption next to the track in compact panels. The track moves below when space is limited. The default layout is stacked.
Native div props, className/style and ref target the wrapper. Available in 0.2.4.

name: CycleCapacity
description: Compare planned work with the estimated capacity of an upcoming cycle.
code: <CycleCapacity planned={42} forecast={{capacity:36,basis:"Based on the last three completed cycles."}} formatAmount={amount => `${amount} pts`} />
notes: Use before a cycle starts to compare its plan with a host estimate. Express planned work and capacity in the same unit. Supply the basis when it helps readers decide how much to trust the estimate.
Zero is a known capacity value. Omit forecast when unavailable. Work above the estimate remains visible on the same scale and is reported as a difference.
The host calculates estimates and decides how to change the plan. Use CycleProgress for work observed over time and CapacityMeter for a fixed quota.

name: CapacityMeter
description: Usage against a fixed quota, with an exact readout when usage exceeds the limit.
code: <CapacityMeter label="Storage used" used={112} capacity={100} warningAt={85} unit="GB" />
notes: Use for a fixed service, memory or storage quota. Supply usage, capacity and warningAt in the same units. Omit warningAt when the product has no policy for a warning.
The fill and accessible numeric range end at capacity. The visible and accessible value text reports the actual amount, including overages.
Supply locale for number formatting and unit for a localized unit. Supply valueText when the amount needs different precision or phrasing. Include both amounts so exceeding the limit stays explicit.
Use the same units and a comparable scope across peer rows. Use Meter for a bounded measurement and Progress for an operation.

name: UsageLimit
description: Current usage, an optional notification threshold, and the consequence of crossing a policy boundary.
code: <UsageLimit label="Compute spend" used={84} limit={100} policy="hard-limit" limitLabel="hard limit" notification={{at:75,label:"Email notification"}} consequence="At the hard limit, workloads pause until the next billing period." formatAmount={amount => `$${amount}`} />
notes: Use UsageLimit when an allowance, soft budget or hard limit has a consequence the user needs to read next to the measurement. Use CapacityMeter when the exact quota is enough.

Pass nonnegative finite usage and a positive finite limit in the same units. An optional notification must be strictly inside that range. The exact readout still shows actual usage when the fill has reached its end.

Use allowance for included usage, soft-budget for a tracked budget, and hard-limit for an enforced boundary. Supply the actual host consequence as one short sentence. The application owns notifications, billing, enforcement and recovery.
Localize label, limitLabel, consequence and notification.label. Use formatAmount to preserve units and currency in the meter and notification threshold.

name: ContextWindowMeter
description: Inspect used and remaining tokens, optional compaction state, and the known parts of a context window.
code: <ContextWindowMeter used={96500} limit={128000} compactionAt={100000} parts={[{id:"messages",label:"Conversation",tokens:58420},{id:"tools",label:"Tool results",tokens:37080}]} />
notes: Use for the current context window of one session. Pass host-provided counts on the same token basis and the currently effective limit. Pass compactionAt only when a threshold is known and compacting only when the runtime is compacting.

Include parts only when their token counts help explain what occupies the window. The breakdown can be partial and always stays separate from the total. Supply unique stable IDs and avoid overlapping categories.

The visual meter ends at the limit. The readout preserves the actual usage and overage. Use lang and labels for localized numbers and copy. Token counting, pruning, billing and model settings belong to the host.

name: TokenUsageBreakdown
description: Inspect recorded token totals with cached input and reasoning output shown as subsets.
code: <TokenUsageBreakdown usage={{input:5000,output:900,cachedInput:1500,reasoningOutput:200}} />
notes: Use on a run or turn detail to explain recorded token consumption. Pass input and output totals from the same record and use cached and reasoning counts as subsets of those totals.
The component adds input and output once. Omit subset counts that were not reported. Use zero when it was reported, and null for an unavailable usage record.
Use ContextWindowMeter for context occupancy against a limit. The host owns accounting, pricing, cache rates, data refresh and any running estimate.

name: UsageForecast
description: Compare recorded usage, period-end estimates and a budget boundary on one scale.
code:
<UsageForecast label="Recorded spend" used={72} limit={100} limitLabel="Budget"
  projection={{amount:118,label:"Estimate by Nov 30"}} scaleMax={135}
  formatAmount={amount => `$${amount}`} />
notes: Use for cumulative usage within one period, where people need to see if the host forecast crosses a named boundary. The solid fill shows recorded use, the striped extension shows the estimate, and the marker shows the limit.
Pass a projection at or above recorded usage and include the forecast horizon in its label. Omit it when no forecast is available. The host owns estimation, resets, budget policy and enforcement.
Supply scaleMax for comparable rows or a stable scale during refresh. It must include every amount. Use UsageLimit for the consequences of crossing a threshold.

name: Alert
description: An inline message with a quiet boundary and explicit announcement priority.
code:
<Alert tone="warning" title="Storage is almost full">
  Free some space before your next upload.
</Alert>
notes: announcement defaults off: a static message does not automatically interrupt a screen reader. Polite uses role=status; assertive uses role=alert.
Use assertive for newly inserted urgent messages, and verify with actual assistive technology. No focus movement, timeout or automatic dismissal is implemented.
Title is optional. Icons are original decorative glyphs; pass icon={null} to omit or supply noninteractive artwork. Meaning must remain in the text.
Use action for a named recovery or next step. The slot sits beside the message when there is room, then moves below it. Announcements apply to the message.
Use appearance=inline for a short contextual caution inside a timeline entry or another constrained surface. Use the banner for longer messages, titles and primary recovery actions.
Native div props and ref target the message root. Available in 0.2.4.

name: NotificationSubscription
description: A scoped notification preference with a controlled current mode.
code: <NotificationSubscription label="Notifications for this issue" value={mode} onValueChange={setMode} />
notes: Use for the viewer's notifications on one record, discussion, or channel. All updates, Mentions & replies, and Muted are distinct options; localize their labels to match the host's actual rules.
onValueChange requests a mode. Keep value at the last accepted preference while saving, and change it after the host accepts the request. Keep errors and retries in the host.
Use FollowButton for a follow relationship and NotificationTrigger to open the inbox. The mode picker does not configure delivery channels or modify the roster.

name: NotificationChannelSettings
