description: Enable a delivery channel and choose which events it sends.
exampleState:
const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(true);
  const [mentions, setMentions] = useState(true);
code:
<NotificationChannelSettings label="Email notifications" enabled={enabled} onEnabledChange={setEnabled}
  events={[{id:"mentions",label:"Mentions and replies",enabled:mentions}]}
  onEventChange={(_id, next) => setMentions(next)} />
notes: Use one group per delivery channel. Turning a channel off disables its event controls and preserves the supplied selections for re-enabling.
Use stable event IDs. For a policy-fixed event, pass readOnly and explain the source in description. Put alerts that always deliver outside the optional channel group.

Both callbacks propose changes to host-owned state. The app owns persistence, errors, permissions, actual delivery and any asynchronous acceptance. Use NotificationSubscription for the scope of updates on one record.

name: ReminderControl
description: Schedule, inspect or cancel a personal reminder on a record.
code: <ReminderControl label="Review export permissions" presets={[{id:"later",label:"Later today"}]} remindAt="2026-11-17T16:00:00Z" onSchedule={id => { /* Resolve and persist the preset in the host. */ }} onClear={() => { /* Cancel in the host. */ }} />
notes: Use inside a record header or detail. The accepted timestamp stays visible beside the action; scheduling a reminder keeps the record in its current collection.
Resolve presets at activation using the host clock and time zone. Pass remindAt with an explicit offset only after the host accepts it. Set timeZone and lang for display.

Use onCustom to open a host date-and-time editor and onClear when cancellation is available. The host owns pending and failed requests, delivery and persistence. Use SnoozeMenu to temporarily remove an item from a queue.

name: EstimateMenu
description: Set or clear a work estimate from a team-owned scale in a compact row or card.
exampleState:
const options = [{id:"0",label:"0 points",shortLabel:"0"},{id:"3",label:"3 points",shortLabel:"3"},{id:"5",label:"5 points",shortLabel:"5"}];
  const [id, setId] = useState<string | null>("3");
code:
<EstimateMenu label="Estimate for export review" options={options}
  value={options.find(option => option.id === id) ?? null} onValueChange={setId} />
notes: Use in a task row or card when a team works with a discrete estimate scale. Supply options in scale order with stable IDs, full spoken labels and optional short visible values.
Null clears the estimate. Supply zero as its own option when the team permits it. When the scale changes, retain the accepted value until the host accepts a different estimate.
The host owns scale settings, estimate conversions, permissions and persistence. Use NumberField when the user can enter any number in a range.

name: SnoozeMenu
description: Schedule when an item returns to an inbox or queue, with quick choices and an optional end action.
code: <SnoozeMenu label="Snooze export notification" presets={[{id:"hour",label:"In an hour"},{id:"tomorrow",label:"Tomorrow morning"}]} onSnooze={presetId => { /* Resolve the preset and submit it in the host. */ }} />
notes: Use for temporarily removing one item from an inbox or queue. Use NotificationSubscription when deciding which future updates arrive for a record.

Resolve preset IDs against the host clock and time zone at activation. Supply snoozedUntil only after the schedule is accepted and show the exact return time alongside the item when it affects the next decision.

Optional onCustom requests a separate date-and-time editor. End snooze appears when there is an accepted schedule and onClear is provided. The host owns persistence, failures and the process that returns the item to the queue.
Keep preset IDs unique and labels distinct. If acceptance removes the opener from an inbox, use getFallbackFocus to move focus to the next retained action.

name: IdentityVerificationBadge
description: A compact identity marker that opens the list of organizations that verified the identity.
code: <Inline gap="1" align="center"><Text>Maya Chen</Text><IdentityVerificationBadge label="Maya Chen’s verified identity" issuers={[{id:"press",name:"Independent Press Guild",detail:"Active member"}]} /></Inline>
notes: Place beside a person or organization name with an independent trigger. In a clickable row, keep it outside the row link or button.
Supply only confirmed, active evidence the viewer may inspect. An empty list omits the mark. Authorization, expiration, and renewal belong to the host.
Give repeated badges a subject-specific label. Link an issuer only when there is an authorized verification record or issuer destination. Use Badge for ordinary labels such as roles or plan names.

name: ParticipantPopover
description: A compact opener that reveals everyone in a scoped roster.
code: <ParticipantPopover label="Subscribers" participants={[{id:"maya",name:"Maya Chen",detail:"Issue owner"},{id:"sam",name:"Sam Rivera",detail:"Reviewer"}]} emptyLabel="No subscribers" />
notes: Use a scope-specific label such as Subscribers or Reviewers. Pass everyone the viewer can inspect, in the intended order. Use detail for an actual role or relationship.
Use AvatarGroup when people should remain visible in the layout and only overflow names need disclosure. Use ParticipantPopover when the full roster belongs behind a single opener.

Supply a localized emptyLabel and closeLabel. Put eligible host-owned management actions in actions. Use a dedicated searchable people view when finding or editing individual memberships is the main task.

Use triggerAppearance=inline beside metadata. It keeps focus on the opener and leaves the roster reachable with Tab. A custom trigger renders one accessible control with the supplied props. Use description for context shared by the entire roster.
Use GroupReadReceipt for the confirmed readers of one message and CollaboratorPresence for activity in the current document.

name: ReplyAudience
description: Choose and disclose who can reply to a post from the composer or post settings.
code: <ReplyAudience value={audience} onValueChange={setAudience} options={[{id:"anyone",label:"Anyone can reply"},{id:"members",label:"Workspace members only"},{id:"closed",label:"Replies off"}]} />
notes: Use near Send or Publish when the selected rule changes who can participate. Put it in MessageComposer leadingActions in an existing composer.
Supply the workspace's actual policies as complete short labels. Pass one accepted value. Set disabled for policies the current user may inspect but cannot choose.

Changing the policy must preserve the draft and leave submission separate. The host enforces permissions and can ignore a request that fails. Use NotificationSubscription for who receives notifications.

name: CollaboratorPresence
description: A document-toolbar roster for collaborators who are viewing or editing, with explicit connection states.
code:
<CollaboratorPresence presence={{status:"live",people:[
  {id:"maya",name:"Maya Chen",activity:"editing"},
  {id:"sam",name:"Sam Rivera",activity:"viewing"},
]}} />
notes: Place in a shared document or record toolbar. One button opens the full roster. Supply visible other collaborators in stable host order and use activity for observed document activity, independent of edit permissions.

Use live with an empty list when the host confirms nobody else is present. Use reconnecting with the last authorized snapshot, or unavailable when there is no reliable roster. Do not preserve identities if the viewer's access changes.

The host owns transport, expiry, current activity and disclosure. Use labels to localize the status, count and activity. Use AvatarGroup for identities displayed independently of live document presence.

name: GroupReadReceipt
description: A compact message action that opens the list of confirmed readers.
code: <GroupReadReceipt readers={[{id:"sam",name:"Sam Rivera",detail:"10:31"},{id:"lee",name:"Lee Park",detail:"10:42"}]} />
notes: Place beside the timestamp for one outgoing group message. Supply only confirmed readers the current viewer is allowed to see. Use the record detail for a localized read time when available.
An empty list renders no trigger. Use MessageReceipt separately for delivery status when no read roster is available. Do not infer that the entire group has read the message from the visible count.
Localize label for the roster and formatTriggerLabel to change the complete button label. The host owns receipt visibility, arrival order and privacy.

name: MessageReceipt
description: Sending, delivery and read state for one outgoing message.
code: <MessageReceipt state="delivered" />
notes: Place beside a message timestamp or under the outgoing message. Pass the strongest state confirmed by the host. Sent, delivered and read are separate facts.
Honor the host's read-receipt privacy settings. If read receipts are unavailable, show the last confirmed state. Use label to localize the visible text.

Keep polite announcements off in message history. Set announce for one outgoing message when a state update needs feedback. In a failure state, offer a separate retry control when the host supports retry.

name: TypingIndicator
description: Quiet typing presence above a message composer.
code: <TypingIndicator label="Maya Chen is typing" />
notes: Supply a short localized label from the host's current typing presence. Omit the label when nobody is typing. Network events, expiration, privacy and identity are host-owned.
Keep the default reserved line when the indicator sits beside a composer or other control that should stay stationary. Use reserveSpace={false} when the empty row can collapse.
The dots briefly pulse and then settle. Reduced motion displays static dots. The text is passive and updates without a live announcement.

name: GenerationPreview
description: A stable media frame for queued, partial, final and unsuccessful generated results.
code: <GenerationPreview title="Weekly visits chart" ratio={2} result={{state: "generating"}} announce />
notes: Set the requested aspect ratio before generation so the media frame stays stable. Use Image with an explicit alternative text for images.
Pass a partial result as generating media and the assembled result as ready media. Keep partial content passive and reserve download or publication actions for ready.
Set queued, failed or cancelled from the host's accepted state. Supply a concise message to explain a failure and use actions for an available retry or stop. The host owns the operation and recovery.
Use announce for a short status when no parent region announces the same operation. Use progress percentages only when the backend supplies measurable progress.

name: FeedAttribution
description: A quiet context line that tells readers why an entry appears in a feed.
code:
<Stack gap="2">
  <FeedAttribution label="Reposted by Maya Chen" href="/people/maya" avatarSize="md" />
  <Comment author={{name:"Sam Rivera"}}>The source export is ready.</Comment>
</Stack>
notes: Place above the entry identity when a repost, pin or collection membership explains why the user sees the entry. Keep the original author in the entry itself.
Supply the full localized reason as label. Add href only when it opens the person, collection or source named in that reason. Keep the original entry and its actions separate.
Optional icons are decorative. Keep the reason available as text and allow it to wrap in a narrow feed without shifting the icon to the middle of the paragraph.
Match avatarSize to the entry when the attribution text should align with the author's name. The leading space stays steady if the icon is omitted.

name: FeedUpdate
description: A floating action that loads buffered feed items without shifting the reading position on arrival.
code:
Activity { /* Apply buffered items in the host feed. */ }} />
Earlier updates
notes: Use the default header placement in a positioned feed heading with room at the logical end. Use placement="overlay" over a positioned feed frame beside its ScrollArea when that leaves the reading area clear.
Use count=0 when caught up, a positive count when known, and unknown when only availability is known. Format the action with a localized verb and noun.
Keep the action mounted with pending while applying changes. The host owns the buffer, scroll and focus after success, and error recovery. Keep the count when an apply attempt fails.
Use announcement to opt into a short, stable live message. Use UnreadMarker to mark a boundary inside an existing sequence.

name: UnreadMarker
description: A quiet marker at the beginning of unread messages or events.
code: <UnreadMarker label="New messages" />
notes: Use once at the boundary where previously read records end and unread records begin. Use CommentThread.unreadBoundary in a chronological thread to place it before a top-level message.

The marker is read in sequence with the messages and has no action. For a jump link, use the target message's persistent anchorId. Use your application's localized count only when the count adds context.
The host owns the read position. Clear the marker when the host accepts a read update, and skip the boundary if the targeted message is not in the current view.

name: QuotedPost
description: An attributed excerpt with an optional original source, for a discussion or record.
code: <QuotedPost post={{author:{name:"Maya Chen"},content:"The source export is ready for review.",href:"/posts/review-ready"}} />
notes: Use when the quoted post itself should remain readable in the current discussion. Supply one authorized excerpt with the original author and an optional destination.

Use appearance="embedded" when a card or details panel already groups the excerpt. The author, author metadata and source link share the identity header. Use a specific source label such as Support conversation.

Use media for authorized attachments from the same post. Actions inside an attachment remain independent from the link to the original. Localize openLabel to distinguish several quoted posts in one feed.

When the source is removed, detached or private, omit post and supply a localized unavailableLabel. Use ReplyReference for a compact pointer to a parent message and LinkPreview for an external webpage card.

name: ThreadTrigger
description: A message action that opens its replies, with optional participants, recency and unread context.
code: <Popover title="Replies" trigger={(props) => <ThreadTrigger {...props} replyCount={1} unread participants={[{id:"maya",name:"Maya Chen"}]} latestReply={{dateTime:"2026-11-16T10:42:00Z"}} />}><CommentThread aria-label="Replies" items={[{id:"reply",author:{name:"Maya Chen"},body:"I attached the original export."}]} /></Popover>
notes: Use below the parent message when replies open a hosted thread. Forward an overlay trigger or supply the host panel's aria-expanded, aria-controls and onClick.

Pass the full reply count and optionally preview up to two eligible participants. These avatars are decorative and the thread is the place to inspect their identities. Zero replies shows Reply and omits reply metadata.
Include unread only when the host has confirmed unseen replies. Put the full replies in CommentThread and use ReplyReference to point from a published reply back to its original message.

name: ReplyReference
description: A short excerpt and a route to the original message above a published reply.
code: <ReplyReference label="In reply to Maya Chen" excerpt="Could you include the original attachment?" href="#review-request" />
notes: Use in Comment.replyReference or CommentThreadItem.replyReference when the original message would be difficult to find beside the reply. Omit it when the parent is already apparent from the thread.

Use a document-unique anchorId on a CommentThreadItem for same-page links, or supply an application route. Give the link a localized label identifying the original message. Provide a short excerpt when it helps recognition.

When the viewer cannot reach the original, omit href and display a clear unavailable label. Supply an excerpt only when the viewer has permission to read it. Use CommentComposer.replyContext for the context of an unsent draft.

name: Mention
description: An account reference that sits in running text and can link to a resolved profile.
code: <Text as="p">Ask <Mention handle="bsky.app" href="https://bsky.app/profile/bsky.app" /> about the update.</Text>
notes: Use inside structured text when the host already knows which account is referenced. Pass a handle with or without @. Supply href for a real destination or omit it to show plain text.
Use label for a reader-facing name. The accessible name of a linked alias includes its full handle. Long names wrap in the surrounding sentence and mixed-direction names are isolated.
A mention does not resolve the handle, verify ownership, parse messages or send notifications. Use AuthorMeta for the person who wrote the message and TextAnnotation for an anchor to a discussion.

name: ImageAnnotations
description: Numbered review points anchored to physical image coordinates, with a host-controlled selection.
code: <ImageAnnotations label="Chart review" image={{src:"/comparison-area.png",alt:"An area chart showing weekly visits",width:801,height:403}} annotations={[{id:"count",label:"Visit count",x:0.105,y:0.18},{id:"peak",label:"Weekend peak",x:0.81,y:0.39}]} activeId={point} onAnnotationSelect={setPoint} />
notes: Pass the exact dimensions of the annotated image. Coordinates are fractions from its physical left and top edges and retain their positions in RTL. Preserve proportions across responsive sources.

Give each point a stable ID and an accessible name that identifies its target. Points follow the supplied order. Leave room between targets; provide an independent discussion list when a dense set cannot be inspected spatially.
The host owns selection, the associated thread and annotation placement. Compose ReviewThread next to the image or return focus to the selected point after dismissing an overlay.

name: ImageFocalPoint
description: Choose which part of an image to keep in frame when an asset is cropped.
code: <ImageFocalPoint label="Preview focal point" horizontalLabel="Horizontal" verticalLabel="Vertical" image={{src:"/comparison-area.png",alt:"Weekly visits chart",width:801,height:403}} value={point} onValueChange={setPoint} />
notes: Pass the exact source dimensions. Coordinates are fractions measured from the physical left and top edges. The image accepts click or tap; the two sliders offer one-percent adjustments with the keyboard.
Store the point in the host and apply it to a cover preview or the host's image delivery API. The component emits coordinates with one-percent precision and leaves the source asset intact.
Use ImageAnnotations for several points that refer to discussions. Use ImageFocalPoint to edit one point that drives a crop preview.

name: TextAnnotation
description: Mark a phrase in prose and link it to its discussion in the same document.
code:
<Stack gap="4">
  <Text as="p">Keep the source file until <TextAnnotation discussionId="retention-review">the next release</TextAnnotation>.</Text>
  <Section id="retention-review" tabIndex={-1} title="Source file retention">
    <Comment author={{name:"Sam Rivera"}}>Keep it in the shared project folder.</Comment>
  </Section>
</Stack>
notes: Use for a discussion attached to the existing words. Use TextRevision for a proposed edit and Citation for the evidence supporting a claim.
Give the discussion a stable ID and tabIndex=-1 so a native fragment link can move focus there. Link back to the annotation by its own ID when readers need to return.

Use resolved to quiet a closed discussion while keeping it reachable. Use active when the host selects its discussion. The host owns text ranges, thread status, and recovery after an anchor is removed.

name: ChangeRegion
description: A leading-edge marker for changes to a document block with stable reading geometry.
code: <ChangeRegion label="Launch check edited by Maya Chen"><Text as="p">Verify the default permissions before publishing.</Text></ChangeRegion>
notes: Use for paragraph, table or section-level edits in a document review. The marker follows the logical leading edge in left-to-right and right-to-left layouts.
Use active for the current block and unmarked to clear the marker without shifting the shared text track. Apply unmarked wrappers to neighboring blocks when they need the same start edge.
Give the change an accessible label. A host-owned review control can focus the wrapper by using a ref and tabIndex={-1}. The marker itself adds no tab stop.
Use TextRevision to expose exact inline insertions and deletions, and VersionHistory to browse saved versions.

name: TextRevision
description: An inline insertion, deletion or replacement with an externally owned decision.
code: <Text>Share the notes <TextRevision before="with the project lead" after="with the project team" />.</Text>
notes: Provide only before for a deletion or only after for an insertion. Both values show a replacement while pending.
Use accepted or rejected to display the applicable text in the document. The host owns revision IDs, ranges, persistence and decisions.
Keep review actions beside the document and use the inline mark as a named focus destination when jumping from the discussion.

name: ValueChange
description: Previous and current values for a recorded change.
code: <ValueChange before="Draft" after="In review" />
notes: Use beside a named field or event. Pass both values for a replacement or supply only the applicable side for an addition or removal.
Use the inline arrow for short values, including existing status chips. Use layout=stacked to compare longer values with visible Before and After labels. Localize the labels where needed.

Use layout=adaptive when the same content appears at different widths. Above 18rem, values wrap on their own side of the arrow. At 18rem or less, the pair uses labeled rows. At 13rem or less, adaptive and stacked layouts give each label and value their own line.
Values may contain Flood controls or rich content. The host owns data comparison and formatting. Zero remains a value.

name: AgentHandoff
description: Inspect who handed off a task, the intended recipient and the recorded transfer outcome.
code: <AgentHandoff from={{label:"Support triage"}} to={{label:"Billing review"}} state="transferred" detail="Review the refund against the original charge." />
notes: Use in a trace, event detail or audit record for a transfer of responsibility. Keep the intended recipient visible when the transfer fails. Use transferred only when the runtime confirms the handoff.
A transferred task can still fail later. Display the enclosing run’s outcome separately. Use unknown when the recorded outcome is unavailable, and supply only detail safe for the viewer.
Use TraceWaterfall for span timing and ToolCall for one tool invocation. The host supplies timing, access and links.

name: EnvironmentSyncReview
description: Review a one-way environment sync, including which changes will remove values from the destination.
code: <EnvironmentSyncReview source={{id:"production",label:"Production"}} destination={{id:"staging",label:"Staging"}} groups={[{id:"worker",label:"Queue worker",changes:[{id:"queue",label:"Legacy queue",before:"exports-v1"}]}]} />
notes: Use after choosing two environments and before applying a one-way sync. Source supplies the plan; only Destination is changed. Supply distinct stable IDs and labels that identify the environments in context.

Group changes by resource. Supply display-safe current and planned destination values. Omit before for an addition and after for a removal. The removal indicator counts individual changes, which can include fields as well as resources.

Pass null while there is no usable plan, including a stale plan invalidated by a source or destination change. Pass an empty array after a successful comparison with no changes. The host owns refresh, permissions, confirmation and apply, and only offers Apply for an actionable plan.

name: StagedChanges
description: Review proposed changes by resource, with optional per-change discard actions.
code: <StagedChanges label="Proposed changes" groups={[{id:"api",label:"API service",changes:[{id:"region",label:"Region",before:"US East",after:"EU West"}]}]} />
notes: Use for a pre-apply review with independently identified changes across resources. Use ChangeList for a read-only comparison on a single compact surface.
Supply safe display values through before and after. Omit before for an addition and after for a removal. Keep secrets and raw infrastructure plan data outside the displayed model.

Use renderDiscard for a small, named action when individually dropping a change is supported. The host updates groups after acceptance and moves focus to a surviving control before a focused row disappears. Use SaveBar or form actions outside the review when applying the draft.

name: ChangeList
description: A definition list of fields changed in a single event.
code: <ChangeList aria-label="Project changes" items={[{id:"owner",label:"Owner",before:"Maya Chen",after:"Sam Rivera"},{id:"due",label:"Due date",after:"21 Nov"}]} />
notes: Use for multiple changes from the same recorded event. Give each field a stable ID and name the list when its context needs a label.
Inherits DescriptionList alignment and density. Keep values inline for short changes, or use valueLayout=stacked when each side needs a clear label and room to wrap.
Use valueLayout=adaptive if the history appears in both a page and a narrow drawer. The comparison responds to the value column, whether the term is above or beside it.
Use Timeline for the chronology. Put ChangeList inside the event's content when the field-level detail helps the reader.

name: VersionHistory
description: Select a saved checkpoint and preview it alongside its history.
code:
<VersionHistory label="Launch notes versions" currentId="v2" versions={[
  {id:"v2",label:"Handoff confirmed",description:"Maya Chen · Nov 16"},
  {id:"v1",label:"Support review",description:"Sam Rivera · Nov 15"},
]} renderPreview={version => <Text as="p">{version.id === "v2" ? "The beta opens Friday." : "Invite the first cohort after the dry run."}</Text>} />
notes: Use for saved versions of one artefact with an inspection pane. Use Timeline for an event chronology and ChangeList or CodeDiff to display a chosen comparison in the preview.

Supply checkpoints in reading order with stable IDs and currentId when known. Selection uses value or defaultValue, then falls back to the current version or first available entry. Arrow keys move within the list; Enter or Space previews a version.

Selecting a checkpoint only changes the preview. Provide renderRestore only when the viewer can restore a historical checkpoint. The host owns permissions, confirmation, writes, outcome feedback and focus after a restore changes the available actions.
On narrow panels the version list comes before the preview. Compact metadata and a short label keep each checkpoint discoverable. Localize currentLabel and emptyContent for translated interfaces.

name: ExpenseAllocationForm
description: Split a single expense across named destinations and reconcile the allocation with the original total.
code:
<ExpenseAllocationForm aria-label="Split expense" currency="USD" total="100.00" lines={lines}
  onAmountChange={(id, amount) => setLines(current => current.map(line => line.id === id ? {...line,amount} : line))}
  onSubmit={split => { /* Validate destination codes and save the split in the host. */ }} />
notes: Supply the expense total and allocations in one currency as nonnegative decimal strings. Blank fields count as zero in the arithmetic and remain null in the submitted data.
The form shows the difference from the latest total and only submits a balanced split. If the expense settles at a different amount, update total and retain the user's allocations for correction.
The host owns destination selection, permissions, accounting validation and saving. Use pending during a save and keep amounts on failure. Use AmountBreakdown for the accepted read-only detail.

name: ExpenseAllocationReview
description: Review recorded expense allocations and show any difference from the current expense total.
code: <ExpenseAllocationReview currency="USD" total="100.01" lines={[{id:"ops",label:"Operations",amount:"60.15"},{id:"growth",label:"Growth",amount:"39.85"}]} />
notes: Use after a split is saved or imported. Supply its recorded lines and the latest expense total in the same currency, as canonical nonnegative decimal strings. Use an empty array if no split is recorded.
The component compares the amounts in integer minor units and shows the difference only when a recorded split is out of balance. Keep the original line amounts visible when the total changes.

Use ExpenseAllocationForm when users can correct the split and AmountBreakdown when the host supplies an ordinary itemized amount. The host resolves changes to the underlying expense, permissions and saving.

name: AmountBreakdown
description: Itemized monetary amounts with a shared end axis and one emphasized total.
code: <AmountBreakdown aria-label="Invoice amounts" rows={[{id:"subtotal",label:"Subtotal",amount:"$12,000.00"},{id:"tax",label:"Tax",amount:"$960.00"},{id:"credit",label:"Account credit",amount:"−$1,250.00"}]} total={{label:"Amount due",amount:"$11,710.00"}} />
notes: Use after invoice, billing or approval detail when intermediate amounts explain the final amount. Only show a summary total once in the surrounding workflow.

Pass localized, display-ready strings from the host, including signs and currency where needed. The component renders the supplied order, retains zero values and emphasizes the supplied total. Calculations and rounding belong to the host.
Use short row labels with stable IDs. An empty rows array shows the total alone. Use MoneyField to edit amounts and Table for line items with multiple comparable fields.

name: RefundLinkSummary
description: Show an individual refund and the purchase it is linked to.
code: <RefundLinkSummary refund={{amount:"42.00",currency:"USD"}} original={{merchant:"Northstar Supply",amount:{amount:"186.40",currency:"USD"},dateTime:"2026-11-12",href:"/transactions/42"}} />
notes: Use next to one refund. Pass the original charge and this refund independently. Several partial refunds can point to the same purchase.
Pass null only for a confirmed unlinked refund. Omit original when the link details could not be inspected. Use href for the accepted original purchase, and action to open the host’s editing flow.

When the host forbids editing, pass lockedReason to show the reason in place of the edit action. Matching, ledger policy, candidate selection and persistence belong to the host. Use ReceiptMatchReview for comparing a receipt with a charge.

name: BillPaymentSchedule
description: Review partial payments and the outstanding balance of one bill.
code:
<BillPaymentSchedule total="$2,400.00" remaining="$1,600.00" unscheduled="$400.00"
  payments={[{id:"p-1",label:"First payment",amount:"$800.00",status:"paid",date:{dateTime:"2026-11-12"}},
    {id:"p-2",label:"Second payment",amount:"$1,200.00",status:"scheduled",date:{dateTime:"2026-11-24"}}]} />
notes: Use within one bill. Pass precise display-ready amounts in the bill currency. The remaining balance includes scheduled payments that have not settled. If known, supply the unscheduled portion separately.

Report each payment’s accepted lifecycle state independently. A scheduled, awaiting-release or processing payment is still unpaid. Pass a recorded date for paid rows and the planned date when it is known for future rows.

Pass a zero balance explicitly. Omit remaining if unknown. An empty payments array means no payments were recorded; omit it when payment details are unavailable. The host owns currency arithmetic, adjustments, actions and authorization.

name: ExpenseSettlement
description: Show who pays whom, the amount and the payment status for one expense settlement.
code: <ExpenseSettlement kind="reimbursement" employee="Maya Chen" company="Studio North" amount={{amount:"186.40",currency:"USD"}} state={{status:"settled",channel:"external",dateTime:"2026-11-16"}} />
notes: Use in a reimbursement or repayment detail view after a transfer is recorded or expected. Reimbursement runs from company to employee and repayment runs from employee to company.

Pass the amount of this payment, including only the transferred portion for a partial payment. The host formats and supplies the exact display amount and ISO currency code. Use CurrencyConversion separately if statement currency differs.

Use external only for a payment recorded as completed outside the application. Approval and processing alone do not establish payment. Add a known date only after settlement and a useful cause if payment fails.
This is a read-only summary. Keep identity, authorization, payment processing and any retry actions in the host.

name: CurrencyConversion
description: Original and statement amounts for a cross-currency transaction, with an optional reported exchange rate.
code:
<CurrencyConversion aria-label="Card transaction conversion"
  original={{amount:"240.00",currency:"CAD"}}
  target={{state:"settled",amount:"175.87",currency:"USD",rate:"0.7328"}} />
notes: Use in a transaction, reimbursement or payout detail when the original and statement currencies differ. Keep both currency codes visible, even when both currencies share a symbol. Use AmountBreakdown for fees, credits or amounts in one currency.

Use target.state pending when the statement amount is unavailable, estimated for a provisional amount, and settled for the posted amount. A known zero is a normal amount. Supply localized numbers without currency symbols or codes, and localize visible labels through labels.

Pass the original and target amounts from the host. If available, pass the provider's reported rate as target units per one original unit. The component displays these values without calculating a rate, rounding amounts or inferring fees.

name: DescriptionList
description: Related terms and descriptions with native list semantics and responsive grouping.
code:
<DescriptionList items={[
  {id:"project",term:"Project",description:"Flood"},
  {id:"version",term:"Version",description:"0.2.4"},
]} />
notes: Use DescriptionList for labeled facts about one object. Keep the same term and value alignment across peer groups. A status is valid as a value for a named field. Put editing commands in a separate action area.
At the actual panel width, check the longest term and value and make sure the stacked layout preserves the pairing.
Renders native dl/dt/dd groups. IDs are stable React keys, not generated DOM anchors; require unique nonempty IDs.
Inline layout becomes stacked when the component container is narrow. Stacked layout is always one column.

Use layout=columns to retain two shared tracks for compact facts such as owner, status and date in a narrow inspector. Columns stack at 10rem or less. Prefer inline or stacked when translated terms or values need more room sooner.
Use layout=grid for independent overview facts. Each value stays beneath its term and the grid fits as many groups as the available width supports.

Set layout=stacked on an individual item to give a long readable value the full width while the other items keep their shared columns or grid tracks. Reserve this for values whose full content matters.
Density and dividers affect presentation. Values may contain React content; the host owns formatting and missing-value text.

Set item.valueOverflow=truncate for a recognizable plain value, such as an identifier or URL. The full text stays available on hover and keyboard focus. Leave values that require reading in full able to wrap.
Set item.action for a compact utility tied to the value, such as a named CopyButton. Actions align at the trailing edge and can move below the value in narrow panels.
Native dl props, className/style and HTMLDListElement ref target the list. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Table
description: A native data table with caption, density and a protected horizontal scroll area.
code:
ProjectMembers
Flood12
notes: Caption is required and remains the accessible table name with hideCaption. Supply table sections and correct native header/cell associations.
Native table props, className/style and HTMLTableElement ref target the actual table. Set style.minWidth when horizontal overflow is preferable to compressed columns.

Flood ScrollArea owns horizontal scrolling and keyboard access. Set maxViewportHeight for bounded vertical scrolling with stable clearance for the overlay rail. scrollLabel names the viewport independently.
Use data-numeric on headers/cells for end alignment and tabular figures; data-align=start/center/end gives logical alignment. No automatic sorting, selection, pagination or data access.
Striped and compact/comfortable density are opt-in presentation. Available in 0.2.4.

name: ComparisonTable
description: Compare the same criteria across options, with the criterion column pinned on scroll.
code:
<ComparisonTable caption="Backup plans" criterionLabel="Criterion"
  columns={[{id:"current",label:"Current plan"},{id:"proposed",label:"Proposed plan"}]}
  rows={[{id:"retention",label:"Retention (days)",numeric:true,cells:{current:7,proposed:30}}]} />
notes: Use for a decision based on the same criteria across several actual options. Use ChangeList for a record of edits and DataTable for working with a collection.
Each option and criterion needs a stable unique ID. Use the same unit across the numeric cells in a criterion and put the unit in its label.
A missing cell shows unavailableLabel. Real zeroes remain visible. Give values such as Not included explicitly when they are known.
Use featuredColumnId to draw attention to an option whose column heading explains its role. Emphasis does not select an option or decide the outcome.

The table uses Flood ScrollArea. At narrow widths the criterion stays pinned while the option columns scroll. Use compact layout for short values that should remain side by side. Add detail to a row for secondary criterion context.

name: MigrationHistory
description: Compare which migrations are recorded across a repository and database environments.
code: <MigrationHistory caption="Migration history" sources={[{id:"git",label:"Repository"},{id:"prod",label:"Production"}]} migrations={[{version:"20261116091500",name:"Add invoice index",history:{git:"recorded",prod:"missing"}}]} />
notes: Use when inspecting a versioned migration history. Supply stable source IDs and exact versions in the intended reading order. Include the recorded name when available.
Report missing only when a readable source confirms absence. Omitted source states appear as Unknown. Recorded describes history membership; it does not certify the live schema or executed SQL.

Prefer short source labels for narrow panels. Use the pinned migration column when more sources require horizontal scrolling. Pass labels for translated states and the empty row. Keep writes and reconciliation in the host.

name: Menu
description: An action and preference menu with keyboard navigation and controlled checkbox/radio items.
code:
<Menu label="Project actions"
  trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Project actions</Button>}
  items={[{id:"rename",label:"Rename…"},{id:"divider",type:"separator"},{id:"delete",label:"Delete project",tone:"danger"}]}
  onAction={id => console.log(id)}
/>
notes: Forward all supplied trigger props and ref to one native button or Flood Button/IconButton. Label names the menu; action labels remain visible.
Enter/Space and ArrowDown open at the first item; ArrowUp opens at the last. Inside use arrows, Home/End and label-prefix typeahead.
Disabled items stay keyboard-focusable with aria-disabled but cannot activate. Separators are noninteractive; action IDs must be unique and nonempty. At least one action is required.
Escape closes and restores trigger focus. Tab moves to the next control after the trigger; Shift+Tab returns to the trigger. Outside interaction dismisses without stealing deliberately moved focus.
Use getFallbackFocus when an action can remove or disable its opener. Resolve the surviving control from the committed interface.

Shortcut text is a visual hint, not an implemented key binding. No href or asynchronous task manager is included. Nested items use type="submenu" and a nonempty items array. Checkbox/radio items are controlled preferences, available in 0.2.7.
Controlled open needs host updates; onAction requests closure before calling the host. Modern native Popover API required. Native div props/ref target the popup. Available in 0.2.4.

Checkbox items take checked (boolean or mixed) and onCheckedChange. Radio items take a nonempty group label, checked and onCheckedChange; the host keeps one selected item per group. Keep each radio group contiguous. Preference items stay open by default; closeOnSelect opts into dismissal. They do not call onAction or submit form values.

Submenus open by logical arrow, click/tap or cancellable mouse hover intent. Escape closes one level; Tab leaves the entire tree through the root trigger. IDs are unique across the tree and nested keyboard searches stay inside their own menu.

name: Toolbar
description: A compact action panel with one Tab entry and directional keyboard navigation.
code:
<Toolbar label="Editor actions">
  <Button variant="ghost">Undo</Button>
  <Toggle variant="ghost">Bold</Toggle>
  <Button variant="ghost">Share</Button>
</Toolbar>
notes: Use Button, IconButton, Toggle, native buttons/links and Menu triggers. Keep inputs, Select, Tabs and ToggleGroup outside this action-only toolbar.

Arrows move focus without activation; Home/End jump to the ends. Disabled and hidden actions are skipped. One Tab entry is established after hydration; before JavaScript native child tab order remains.
Horizontal arrows follow writing direction. Vertical arrows move between actions; open a vertical toolbar Menu with Enter/Space. Horizontal menus retain ArrowUp/Down opening.
A vertical pill centers its controls on one axis. Use consistently sized icon-only actions with accessible names. Use the rounded shape for a vertical group of labeled actions.
loop defaults to true. Native div props/ref target the toolbar; preserve a meaningful label. Available in 0.2.4.
shape defaults to rounded; pill uses the action radius and a horizontal single scrollable rail.
variant="plain" removes the material and outer inset for grouping peer controls; contained remains the default. Keyboard ownership is unchanged.

name: Kbd
description: A quiet native keyboard-input label for keys and shortcut hints.
code: <Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
notes: Native kbd markup, not a button or a shortcut handler. The application implements and documents actual bindings.
Use KeyboardShortcut for a combination of keys or a platform-specific spoken label.
Sizes sm/md/lg use relative keycap tokens. Native props/ref target the kbd element. Available in 0.2.4.

name: KeyboardShortcut
description: A group of keycaps for a keyboard shortcut.
code: <KeyboardShortcut keys={["Ctrl", "Shift", "K"]} />
notes: Pass keys in the intended reading order. Use presentation=compact to fit the combination in one keycap, or pass a preformatted string.
Pass nested arrays for successive chords, such as keys={[["G"], ["D"]]}. Localize sequenceSeparator or supply label when the spoken order needs different wording.
Use label to supply a localized spoken form for glyphs such as Command and Shift. The surrounding action owns the actual binding and aria-keyshortcuts.

name: ShortcutRecorder
description: Record and confirm a keyboard shortcut in settings.
code: <ShortcutRecorder label="Command palette shortcut" defaultValue={{key:"k",code:"KeyK",modifiers:["Control"]}} />
notes: Use for editing one chord. The host owns persistence, dispatch, and whether matching uses logical key or physical code. The browser can only capture keys that reach the page.
Pass validate to explain a conflict beside the candidate. Save or Enter accepts it. Escape or leaving the popover discards it. Clear stages removal so it can still be cancelled.
Use requireModifier=false only when single-key bindings are intentionally supported in that context. Tab and Escape keep navigation and dismissal behavior. Bare Enter confirms a candidate.
Provide localized labels and formatKeys as needed. Use KeyboardShortcut for display and ShortcutReference for searchable help.

name: ShortcutReference
description: Searchable, grouped keyboard help for shortcuts the host supports.
code:
<ShortcutReference groups={[
  {id:"global",label:"Workspace",items:[{id:"search",label:"Open command palette",keys:["Ctrl","K"]}]},
  {id:"service",label:"Service view",items:[{id:"deploy",label:"Go to deployments",keys:[["G"],["D"]]}]},
]} />
notes: Use for a searchable keyboard guide. Group shortcuts by where they work, and omit unavailable bindings. Queries can combine terms from the group, action, keys, spoken names, and keywords. Use CommandPalette to execute commands and KeyboardShortcut for hints next to one action.

Supply actual key labels for the current platform and configuration. A flat array is one chord; nested arrays are successive chords. Use spokenKeys for glyphs such as Command and keywords for familiar alternative names.
Search matches the action, group, displayed keys, spoken keys and keywords. The component never installs or runs a binding. Use Dialog or Sheet as the host when the reference opens over a workspace.
Use stable unique group IDs and item IDs within each group. Localize searchLabel, clearLabel, sequenceSeparator and empty states, and set headingLevel to fit the host outline.

name: Card
description: A structured surface for a heading, supporting content and independent actions.
code:
<Card title="Project details" description="Release on 12 November"
  footer={<Button variant="subtle">Open project</Button>}>
  <Text as="p" size="compact">Homepage and checkout</Text>
</Card>
notes: Card composes Surface with optional title, description, header actions, children and footer. Missing slots add no empty wrapper or reserved space.
Use media for top-aligned artwork in a gallery. Give peers the same AspectRatio. Place imagery that follows the heading in the body.
Use Surface for unstructured containment; use Card when its header/body/footer structure is useful. Card is a noninteractive div, not a button or link. Put named actions inside.

Title uses Heading at headingLevel (2 by default). Choose the level according to the page and headingSize according to the visual hierarchy. Use group for a compact repeated card title. Supply phrasing content for the title.
Density compact/comfortable controls padding and section rhythm using existing semantic spacing. Header actions wrap naturally; content is never clipped to the radius.

Pass selection with a named checkbox when the card is a record that can participate in a bulk action. The checkbox sits in the header and the host owns selection. Keep links and commands independent. Use CheckCard for a form choice whose primary action is checking the option.
In a narrow card, wide header actions can move below the title and description. The independent selection checkbox stays at the top trailing edge.
Use footerDivider={false} when spacing is enough to separate the footer. Match that setting in CardSkeleton when loading this card.
Root HTMLDivElement ref and native div props/style/className target the surface. The title prop is content, not the native HTML tooltip attribute. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Container
description: Centered content with token widths and logical gutters.
code: <Container size="md" gutter="6"><Text as="p">Content stays within a readable width.</Text></Container>
notes: Max width includes gutters (border-box). Sizes sm/md/lg use relative semantic roles; full removes the maximum.
Native div props/ref target the container. Gutter uses Space; it does not add vertical spacing or breakpoints.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: Grid
description: An adaptive content grid with optional fixed columns.
code: <Grid minItemWidth="16rem" gap="4"><Surface>First</Surface><Surface>Second</Surface></Grid>
notes: Default auto-fit columns clamp their minimum to available width, so narrow parents retain a single column.
Use maxColumns to cap responsive tracks while allowing fewer columns in a narrow container. A supplied columns value takes precedence.
Explicit columns retain their count; choose this deliberately. minItemWidth applies only to automatic columns and accepts a CSS length.
Cells remain ordinary content, not an ARIA grid. Use native tables for tabular relationships and host media/container queries for deliberate breakpoints.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: Masonry
description: A responsive column-first list that gives unequal-height media room to retain its proportions.
notes: Compose native li children in meaningful source order. Items are kept together and laid out down each column in the reading direction. Keyboard traversal follows that same order. Use Grid for row-first comparison or explicit tracks.

Reserve image proportions with width and height. Keep height automatic when rendering at the available column width. Use maxColumns as a cap and minColumnWidth to set the preferred minimum before the layout falls back to fewer columns.
Use ImageMosaic for a bounded set of attachments with its own preview, and FileCardGrid when equal media framing or aligned card footers is part of the collection.

name: VisuallyHidden
description: Nonvisual content with optional reveal when keyboard focus enters.
code: <Text>Project updated.</Text><VisuallyHidden>Changes save automatically.</VisuallyHidden>
notes: Content remains in the accessibility tree. Default is for noninteractive text only.
Use focusable for a skip link or another focusable descendant: the wrapper becomes visible while it contains focus. Supply visible focus styling on the actual control.
This is not aria-hidden, display:none or a conditional unmount. as accepts span/div.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: AspectRatio
description: Reserved media proportions that respond to their containing width.
code: <AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}><Image src="/flood-mark.png" alt="Flood logo" fit="contain" /></AspectRatio>
notes: ratio must be finite and positive. The root reserves media geometry before image loading.
Direct img/video/iframe children fill the reserved box. Content can overflow; the component does not clip focus, menus or arbitrarily tall text.
Host media owns alt, captions, controls and loading. Native props/ref target the outer div.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: Image
description: A native responsive image with explicit alternative text and media fitting.
code: <Image src="/flood-mark.png" alt="Flood logo" width={160} height={160} fit="contain" />
notes: alt is required; an empty string is appropriate for decorative imagery beside equivalent visible content.
Native src/srcSet/sizes/loading/decoding/dimensions, handlers and HTMLImageElement ref are preserved. Supply width/height or AspectRatio to reserve geometry.
fit cover/contain changes object-fit, not fetching, optimization or fallback behavior. Avatar composes Image with its own load/fallback lifecycle.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: List
description: Native ordered or unordered content with token spacing and optional markers.
code:
• Install the matching packages.
  • Import the stylesheet.
  • Compose with Flood.
notes: Supply native li children. ordered chooses ol; start/reversed apply only to ordered lists. start must be a safe integer.
Hiding markers retains an explicit list role for browser/assistive-technology consistency. Content may include links or controls without changing its content-list semantics.
This is not ListBox, a selection model or a keyboard-navigation engine.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: EmptyState
description: A quiet explanation and optional next action when content is absent.
code: <EmptyState title="No projects yet" actions={<Button>Create project</Button>} />
notes: Composes Stack, Heading, Text, IconSlot and Inline. Optional icon is decorative; title and description explain the missing content.
Static by default, without status/alert announcements or automatic focus. Host owns whether a result change should be announced.

Choose headingLevel for the page hierarchy. Use centered when the state occupies the destination, inline for a narrow section, and row when the message and a recovery action can share a line. The row moves actions below the message on narrow widths. Density controls padding.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: NoResults
description: A compact empty result after search or filtering, with optional reset.
code: <NoResults title="No matching projects" />
notes: Use after search or filtering excludes every item. Keep the search and filters in place. Use EmptyState for a new collection with no records.
Pass onReset only when this region owns the reset action. Name its scope with resetLabel. A clear command in the toolbar can own the whole reset.
Pass resetFocusRef to return focus to a persistent input or filter before the results change. Keep announcements in the collection's existing status region.
The default compact row puts reset at the trailing edge when it fits. At narrow widths it falls below the message.

name: ErrorState
description: A failed content region with an optional retry and supporting actions.
code: <ErrorState title="Could not load project activity" layout="inline" />
notes: Use when content is unavailable because a request failed. Leave still-usable content in place for errors that affect a single action.
Share EmptyState layout and density in related regions. The row layout keeps recovery at the trailing edge until it needs to wrap below the message.

Provide onRetry only when the host can retry the request. Use retrying to hold the focused button and its dimensions while the request runs. Restore focus to a persistent destination when the result replaces the error. Announce operation changes through the host's one status region.

name: NumberInput
description: A native numeric field with optional decrement and increment actions.
code:
<Field label="Seats">
  {(control) => <NumberInput {...control} name="seats" defaultValue={5} min={0} max={20} />}
</Field>
notes: Values are finite numbers or null for an empty field. onValueChange reports edits and button/arrow steps; native min/max/step validity remains available. Out-of-bound typed values clamp on blur; a step mismatch remains native validation.
Ref and native form attributes target the input. Controlled value stays host-owned; uncontrolled form reset restores the initial value. Buttons use explicit accessible names, which can be translated.

Use Field for labels and feedback. appearance="plain" keeps keyboard stepping and gives the value the full field width. Read-only remains selectable and prevents stepping. No currency/locale formatting or wheel interception is supplied.

name: TemporarySpendLimit
description: Review a temporary spending increase, the enforced limit and its reset.
code:
<TemporarySpendLimit title="Events card" baseLimit="$3,000.00" requestedIncrease="$1,500.00"
  state={{status:"active",effectiveLimit:"$4,500.00",resetsAt:"2026-12-01T05:00:00Z"}}
  reason="Deposit for the team offsite" timeZone="America/New_York" />
notes: Use on a card or fund detail to review a temporary increase. Pass localized display amounts with the same currency. The requested increase and the effective spending limit are independent values.

Use the host's recorded state. Only active carries the effective limit and confirmed reset time. For a request, supply an expected reset only when known. A declined request may carry the approver’s reason.

Use explicit-offset instants and the appropriate display time zone. The host determines approval, the reset date, the enforced limit and expiration. Use SpendLimitForm when editing permanent thresholds.

name: SpendLimitForm
description: Edit a notification threshold and a hard spending limit for one known scope.
code: <SpendLimitForm currency="USD" value={limits} onValueChange={setLimits} onSubmit={saveLimits} capEffect="Pauses compute workloads when spending reaches this amount." />
notes: Use for a known account, workspace, or resource group with both controls. Place the scope and billing period in the surrounding settings UI when users can edit several.

Describe the real enforcement consequence next to Hard limit. The alert and the cap are independent optional amounts. Null means unset and zero is an explicit amount. The notification threshold must be below a configured cap.
Pass exact decimal strings at the currency’s precision. Use pending during the request and keep the draft visible on failure.

Your application owns authorization, any minimum thresholds or non-removable limits, and confirmation when saving could immediately interrupt service. Use UsageLimit to show recorded consumption against an existing limit.

name: MoneyField
description: An exact decimal amount with a currency, locale-aware editing and canonical form submission.
code:
<Field label="Refund amount">
  {field => <MoneyField {...field} name="amount" currency="USD" locale="en-US"
    defaultValue="1299.50" min="0" max="2000" />}
</Field>
notes: Use MoneyField for a monetary amount with an explicit currency. Choose NumberInput for counts and other ordinary quantities.

Keep accepted monetary amounts as decimal strings. A named field submits the canonical amount without grouping or currency text. Supply the currency separately if the form supports multiple currencies.
Keep product rules such as the refundable balance in the host. Pass exact min and max bounds to the field when they are known.

name: NumberRangeField
description: Two numeric fields for entering exact lower and upper bounds.
code: <NumberRangeField label="Budget (USD)" min={0} start={{ label: "Minimum", name: "budgetMin", defaultValue: 1200 }} end={{ label: "Maximum", name: "budgetMax", defaultValue: 5000 }} />
notes: Use for exact typed values with a shared unit. Name both endpoints. Two equal tracks stack when the fields no longer fit their container.

Each endpoint submits separately with its own name and supports controlled value/onValueChange or an uncontrolled defaultValue. Empty endpoints default to null. required applies to both inputs; disabled follows native fieldset behavior.
The host owns cross-field validation and may show one shared error. Values remain editable in either order so a correction never silently changes the other endpoint.

name: Slider
description: One value or an ordered range with native keyboard controls on a shared rail.
code: <Slider label="Price range" name="price" defaultValue={[25, 75]} min={0} max={100} />
notes: value/defaultValue contain one number or an ordered pair. onValueChange returns a new array. Values snap to min-based steps and thumbs cannot cross; Tab order stays stable. Supply thumbLabels to translate or explain each handle.

Horizontal only. Direction follows the host, including RTL. Native range inputs retain keyboard behavior; pointer selection chooses the nearest handle. Names submit one or two entries; uncontrolled reset restores defaults.
On touch, a tap commits on release and a horizontal drag starts after a small movement. A vertical gesture on the rail leaves the selection unchanged so the surrounding surface can scroll.

hideLabel preserves the accessible legend; showValue only controls the visible numeric readout. Read-only prevents edits while keeping focus. Use hint/message/error for meaning beyond color. Touch assistive technology needs device testing. Available in 0.2.5.

Use valuePlacement="inline" to show the readout by the visible label. Use the same placement across related sliders. Use formatValue for units or locale-specific values in the readout and on each accessible thumb.

name: RolloutAllocation
description: Adjust the traffic split between a candidate version and a baseline.
code: <RolloutAllocation label="Traffic allocation" candidateLabel="New checkout" baselineLabel="Current checkout" value={candidate} onValueChange={setCandidate} />
notes: Use for a binary rollout. Pass the candidate share as a number from 0 to 100. The baseline displays the complement. Traffic bucketing, eligibility, scheduling and publication belong to the host.
Choose precision to match the rollout system's accepted percentage step. The default uses whole percentages. Set precision=3 for allocations such as 0.125 percent.
Without onValueChange the slider is read-only. disabled removes it from keyboard operation and form submission. Use name and form to submit the candidate percentage with native form data.

name: Combobox
description: Search a defined collection and commit one option while focus stays in the input.
code:
<Field label="Framework">
  {(control) => <Combobox {...control} name="framework" options={[{value: "react", label: "React"}, {value: "vue", label: "Vue"}, {value: "svelte", label: "Svelte"}]} placeholder="Choose a framework" />}
</Field>
notes: Typing filters labels and optional keywords; labels remain presentation and only the selected option value is submitted. Enter commits the active option. Escape/Tab/outside interaction discard an uncommitted query. Emptying the input clears selection.

Native input ref, Field associations, required validity, controlled/uncontrolled value, forms/reset, read-only/disabled and IME editing are preserved. Options need unique nonempty values and labels. Disabled options remain discoverable and cannot be chosen.
For people or team options, supply avatar data on the option. The committed value shows its avatar. While typing a query, the same space holds a search glyph. Keep the name in the option label.
Use selectedLabel for a committed value that needs group context. Keep the option label and keywords sufficient for search. The option value still determines what the form submits.

Use clearable for the visible clear action; translate clearLabel/toggleLabel/listLabel/emptyMessage/invalidSelectionMessage. The popup reuses Flood ScrollArea and layer positioning. No arbitrary text, multiple selection, async fetching or virtualization engine is supplied. Available in 0.2.5.
Only the disclosure chevron is shown by default. Set clearable to opt into the extra clear-selection action; individual MultiSelect tags retain their removal buttons.

name: Tag
description: A compact label with an optional icon or avatar and a named removal action.
code: <Tag onRemove={() => { /* Update the host collection. */ }}>Design</Tag>
notes: For an applied-filter summary, retain the property name when the value alone is ambiguous. Update the applied values on removal and keep each chip near the controls that own it.
Tag is a label, not a status Badge or a selection toggle. The host owns removal; onRemove never hides the element automatically. Use ordinary noninteractive label content.

Plain text gets a default Remove label. Rich content needs explicit removeLabel. disabled prevents removal; size and decorative icon are independent. removeButtonProps customizes the nested native action while Tag owns type, name, disabled and removal.
Use avatar for a named person or team. It takes the leading slot and stays decorative beside the visible name.

Standalone removal is an ordinary Tab stop. MultiSelect supplies its composite keyboard model. Geometry uses relative Flood sizing; long labels wrap and touch targets remain distinct. Available in 0.2.5.

name: TagGroup
description: A wrapping group of labels or removable tags with optional count disclosure.
code: <TagGroup label="Project filters" items={[{id:"status",label:"Status: Active"},{id:"owner",label:"Owner: Maya"},{id:"team",label:"Team: Design"}]} maxVisibleTags={2} />
notes: Use for accepted labels or filter summaries. Use TagInput to create values and MultiSelect to choose values.

Provide a group label and stable unique item IDs. Pass onRemove to request removal by ID. Update items after acceptance. Supply removeLabel for localized removal and disabled on individual protected tags.
maxVisibleTags keeps a short preview with an expandable count. Localize moreTagsLabel and fewerTagsLabel. A disabled group displays every label and blocks removal.
Choose the same size as nearby tags. The group wraps between tags and keeps long labels readable at narrow widths.
For identity groups, provide each item's avatar data and keep the name as its visible label.

name: MetadataList
description: A compact list of supporting facts with optional decorative icons.
code: <MetadataList label="Project details" items={[{id:"team",value:"Design team"},{id:"updated",value:<time dateTime="2026-11-14">Updated Nov 14</time>}]} />
notes: Use for short facts such as team, timestamp or counts. In DataListItem, put them in details to keep them with the title and description.
Use value for text or inline content such as time. Icons are decorative, so write the fact with enough context to read without the icon.
Each item has a stable unique ID. Empty values are omitted. Facts wrap with their icons intact; long localized words may wrap within one item.
Keep state and triage signals in StatusIndicator or Badge where their meaning calls for emphasis. Use DescriptionList for explicit term and value pairs.

name: MultiSelect
description: Search a collection, choose multiple values and manage them as removable tags.
code:
<Field label="Frameworks">
  {control => <MultiSelect {...control} name="frameworks" options={[{value:"react",label:"React"},{value:"vue",label:"Vue"},{value:"svelte",label:"Svelte"}]} defaultValue={["react"]} placeholder="Search frameworks" />}
</Field>
notes: value/defaultValue are arrays of unique nonempty option IDs; onValueChange returns a new array. Native forms submit repeated entries with the same name, never typed query text. Uncontrolled reset restores initial values.

The shared Combobox search/layer model keeps focus in the input. Enter toggles the active option and the list stays open. Backspace in an empty input removes the last visible editable tag; a logical backward arrow at the start enters tag actions. Tag arrows, Delete/Backspace, Enter and Escape support keyboard editing.

Use maxVisibleTags to limit display in dense filters. A keyboard-accessible count opens the rest. The complete selection remains in FormData and in the field's accessible description. Localize moreTagsLabel and fewerTagsLabel where needed.
Option avatar data appears in the list and the corresponding selected tag. When results are remote, retain avatar data in selectedOptions along with the selected names.

Disabled selected options cannot be individually removed or cleared globally. Read-only permits copying but blocks selection and removal. Required means at least one valid selected ID. Translate removeItemLabel and the shared action/empty/validation messages.
No freeform values, remote fetching, virtualization or arbitrary tag selection engine is supplied. Available in 0.2.5.
Only the disclosure chevron is shown by default. Set clearable to opt into the extra clear-selection action; individual MultiSelect tags retain their removal buttons.

name: SearchInput
description: A native search field with a leading search icon and one clear action.
code:
<Field label="Search">
  {control => <SearchInput {...control} name="search-input" />}
</Field>
notes: Native onChange, name, form, reset, ref and Field associations are preserved. clearable defaults to true; read-only hides the clear action. Translate clearLabel. Enter keeps native form submission; filtering belongs to the host.
Composes Flood InputGroup, IconSlot and IconButton using existing semantic geometry and feedback states. Available in 0.2.5.

name: VisualSearchForm
description: Send a text query, a reference image, or both through one search form.
code: <VisualSearchForm label="Find visual references" value={{text,image}} onTextChange={setText} onChooseImage={openImageChooser} onRemoveImage={() => setImage(null)} onSearch={runSearch} pending={searching} />
notes: Use when a reference image is part of the search query. Use SearchInput for a text-only search and QueryInput for typed field constraints.

The host owns image selection, preparation, search and results. Provide an identified image and a short label the user can recognize. A display thumbnail may also be supplied. onChooseImage requests the same chooser for adding and replacing.

Either a nonempty trimmed text value or a reference image can submit. Removing the image preserves the search text and returns focus to it. While pending, the form blocks another submission and the current draft can be edited.
Localize labels and placeholder. The host reports search failures and keeps the accepted results visible when a request is refused.

name: PasswordInput
description: A password field with one named visibility action.
code:
<Field label="Password">
  {control => <PasswordInput {...control} name="password-input" />}
</Field>
notes: Use visible/onVisibleChange for controlled visibility or defaultVisible for an initial reveal. Translate showPasswordLabel/hidePasswordLabel. Read-only still permits inspection; disabled blocks actions. Native value/onChange, autocomplete, form and ref are preserved. Visibility does not change the value.
Composes Flood InputGroup, IconSlot and IconButton using existing semantic geometry and feedback states. Available in 0.2.5.

name: FieldChecklist
description: A compact list of requirements with pending, met and unmet states.
code: <FieldChecklist label="Upload requirements" items={[{id:"format",label:"PDF file",status:"met"},{id:"size",label:"Under 10 MB",status:"pending"}]} />
notes: Use for independent requirements the host can evaluate. Supply a list name and stable, unique item IDs. Omitted status is pending.
The list gives each state a distinct mark and readable status text for assistive technologies. Localize statusLabels where needed.
Keep the actual input, its validity and the announcement policy in the host form.

name: PasswordStrength
description: A compact password assessment with a named meter and optional requirements.
code: <PasswordStrength assessment={{value:2,max:4,valueText:"Fair",tone:"warning"}} />
notes: Place near a new-password field. Pass a host-owned assessment and an honest localized valueText. The component receives the assessment rather than the password.
Omit assessment until a result is available; requirements can still show independently. Provide requirements only for constraints that apply to the form.
Composes Meter and FieldChecklist. Assessment, validation and any deliberate announcements belong to the host.

name: FileTrigger
description: A button or icon action that hands newly picked files to the application.
code: <FileTrigger label="Attach files" multiple onFilesSelect={(files) => appendAttachments(files)} />
notes: Use for a host-owned attachment queue, import action or image picker. FileInput is the corresponding field for native FormData submission.
Each nonempty pick sends a fresh File array. Cancel is quiet and repeated picks of the same file work. The hidden native input is cleared after each pick.
Use trigger to compose a named Button or IconButton with the supplied props. accept and capture configure the browser chooser. The host checks the selected content and owns processing.

name: AvatarPicker
description: A profile image with connected choose, replace and remove actions.
code: <AvatarPicker name="Alex Morgan" src={storedPhotoUrl} file={photo} onFileSelect={setPhoto} onRemove={removePhoto} />
notes: Pass the current stored image as src and an accepted local replacement as file. The component manages the local preview URL for that File.

The application owns validation, draft state, upload and persistence. Pass error for visible rejection and busy while processing a change. A filename extension or accept hint alone cannot validate image contents.
Localize the group and choose/replace/remove labels. Remove appears when an image and onRemove are available. If a focused Remove action disappears, focus returns to the chooser.

name: FileInput
description: A native file picker with a compact selection summary and one clear action.
code:
<Field label="Attachments" hint="Choose files from your device.">
  {control => <FileInput {...control} name="attachments" multiple />}
</Field>
notes: The browser owns FileList, native name/form/required/accept/multiple/capture behavior and the input ref. onChange retains the native event; onFilesChange receives a fresh array after selection or clear. No controlled value/defaultValue or readOnly mode is supplied.

clearable defaults to true. Localize placeholder and clearLabel. Clear restores input focus and empties the native selection; form reset clears the summary without emitting a change. Disabled includes inherited fieldset behavior. Cancelling the chooser preserves selection.

File names are shown as text, shortened visually when needed. This component only selects files; the host owns upload, progress and validation. accept is a chooser hint, not file validation. Available in 0.2.5.

Multiple selection shows a compact count and a collapsible list with full file names and localized sizes. Removing one file updates the native FileList and preserves keyboard focus; clearable=false hides both individual and global removal. Translate selectionLabel/removeFileLabel. In multiple mode, choosing again appends files. Repeated files are deduplicated by name, size, type, lastModified and relative path. Single mode replaces its selection.

name: CollectionImportReview
description: Review where a collection will be imported and which items the importer will skip.
code: <CollectionImportReview source="Editorial references" destination="Studio archive" assessment={{state:"checked",eligible:48,exclusions:[{id:"video",reason:"Unsupported videos",count:8}]}} />
notes: Use before importing a collection. Give the source and destination distinct, recognizable names. Supply an assessed eligible count and mutually exclusive groups for items that will be skipped.
Zero eligible describes a checked import. Use unavailable when the source could not be assessed. The optional confirmation action appears only when the assessment finds eligible items.
The host owns eligibility, permissions, import and confirmation state. Use BatchResult for the recorded outcomes after an import runs.

name: BatchResult
description: A completed batch summary with record-level reasons and an exact subset for retry.
code:
<BatchResult title="Purchase order import" items={[
  {id:"PO-186",label:"PO-186 · Field equipment",status:"succeeded"},
  {id:"PO-189",label:"PO-189 · Shipping supplies",status:"failed",retryable:true,reason:"The accounting connection timed out."},
  {id:"PO-190",label:"PO-190 · Monitor stands",status:"failed",reason:"Create the vendor before importing this order."}
]} onRetry={ids => retryOrders(ids)} />
notes: Use for a completed batch with independent item results where people need to examine or resolve exceptions. Use Toast for routine success, Progress while the batch runs, and a filtered DataTable when server-side paging is needed.

Pass the complete terminal outcomes for this batch to derive exact counts. The default shows only failed and skipped records; use showSucceeded for a small full audit. Supply the reason needed to fix an exception and href when a record can be opened.

Set retryable only for failed items the host can safely reattempt. The callback receives those stable IDs exclusively. Keep accepted results visible, set retryPending during the request, and replace outcomes when the host confirms them.
Use labels to localize outcome text, pluralized counts, recovery and the empty result. Put longer recovery actions in the surrounding workflow.

name: PendingInvitationList
description: Review outstanding email invitations, their roles and delivery or acceptance state.
code: <PendingInvitationList label="Outstanding invitations" invitations={[{id:"invite-1",email:"alex@example.test",role:"Contributor",state:"awaiting-acceptance"}]} renderActions={renderInviteActions} />
notes: Use after sending an invite and before acceptance. Use a member list or an audit history for accepted and revoked entries.
Key each row by its stable invitation ID. Read the state from the host, and show the resource only when the list spans multiple scopes.
Render only allowed actions per row. Name them for the recipient. Confirm revocation when it invalidates an already shared invitation, and preserve or restore focus after the row leaves the list.
Resend and revoke are host operations. Keep the row during the request, disable duplicate actions, and update it when the host confirms the result. Announce results outside the collection.

name: SessionList
description: Account sessions with current-device identity and a scoped sign-out action.
code:
<SessionList label="Active sessions" currentId="browser" sessions={[
  {id:"browser",label:"Chrome on Windows",location:"London, UK"},
  {id:"phone",label:"iPhone",lastActive:{dateTime:"2026-11-16T12:15:00Z",label:"Nov 16, 12:15 UTC"}},
]} />
notes: Use in account security when users need to recognize active sessions. Provide the device or application name, available location and labeled time. Preserve any qualifiers for approximate facts.

Supply currentId once known. Leaving it undefined suppresses every sign-out action. Use null only when no listed session can be the viewer's current session, for example when an administrator reviews another account.

The current session and any unavailable session never receive renderEndAction. The host decides whether a known remote session can be ended, names the target in confirmation and controls completion, errors and focus recovery.
Use AccessSummary for resource permissions. Keep a global sign-out action outside SessionList so it can explain the scope of signing out everywhere.

name: ConnectedAccountList
description: Provider identities and current connection states with one host-owned action per account.
code:
<ConnectedAccountList label="Connected accounts" accounts={[
  {id:"github-work",provider:"GitHub",account:"maya-work",state:"connected"},
  {id:"github-personal",provider:"GitHub",account:"maya-personal",state:"reconnect"},
]} />
notes: Use in account settings to show which provider account is connected and what needs attention. Multiple accounts from the same provider need distinct stable IDs and visible account identities when disclosure is allowed.

Use reconnect for a known connection requiring fresh authorization. Use disconnected for an available setup with no connection, and unavailable when setup or its status is unavailable. Supply a specific reason only when the host knows it.

Render one contextual action by default. Include the relevant account or provider in its accessible name. Keep the accepted state while authorization runs and update it from the provider result. Use AccessSummary for permissions, and SessionList for active sign-ins.

name: VariableReferencePicker
