description: Choose a configuration reference by source and key without using the resolved value.
code:
<Field label="Source variable">
  {control => <VariableReferencePicker {...control} name="reference" references={[{id:"db-url",source:"Postgres",key:"DATABASE_URL"},{id:"cache-url",source:"Redis",key:"CACHE_URL"}]} />}
</Field>
notes: Use to choose one declared reference. Collocate the option group with its source and show the source again in the committed value so repeated keys are distinguishable. The picker submits the stable reference ID.

Pass only source names, keys, safe descriptions and opaque IDs. Omit entries a viewer cannot discover. Use disabled for known references that are visible but unavailable to select. Resolve, authorize and serialize the chosen reference in the host.
For remote results pass the controlled query, optionsQuery and selectedReferences as needed. Use EnvironmentVariableList for published configuration and Autocomplete for editable free text.

name: TemporaryAccessLink
description: Copy an issued time-limited link with the resource, access scope and exact expiration in view.
code: <TemporaryAccessLink resource="Account export.csv" access="download" state={{status:"issued",url:"https://files.example/export?token=example",expiresAt:"2026-11-17T09:30:00Z"}} now="2026-11-17T09:00:00Z" />
notes: Use once the host has issued a temporary link for a named download or upload. Render only for users permitted to copy it. The full address is copied without displaying it.
Supply UTC-offset timestamps from the host. Update now at expiration and on resume so a stale address cannot be copied from the UI. Expired and unavailable states keep the copy control inactive.

The host issues and enforces the link, and owns authorization, renewal and confirmed revocation. Use state=unavailable when no issued link can be used. Offer renewal only when supported, using a separate host action.

name: VolumeMountSummary
description: Inspect a persistent volume’s attachment, copy its exact mount path and review recorded capacity.
code: <VolumeMountSummary title="Database volume" attachment={{state:"mounted",service:"Postgres",path:"/var/lib/postgresql/data"}} usage={{used:4.2,capacity:5,warningAt:4,unit:"GB"}} />
notes: Use in service or volume details. Use pending for a configured path that the host has yet to observe mounted, detached for a confirmed absence, and unknown when attachment data is unavailable.
Supply the exact path. Capacity is independent of attachment, so a detached volume can still show recorded usage. Supply observed values in one shared unit and omit usage for unavailable metrics.
The host owns observation, thresholds, attach and resize actions. Use CapacityMeter alone when placement and mount state are already visible.

name: StorageBucketPolicy
description: Inspect effective read access, the per-file upload limit and allowed MIME types for one storage bucket.
code: <StorageBucketPolicy aria-label="Brand assets policy" readAccess="public" uploadLimit={{source:"bucket",bytes:8000000}} contentTypes={["image/png","image/webp"]} />
notes: Use next to a bucket's details or file picker. Supply the effective permissions and limits from the host. Public refers to reading objects; uploading and managing objects use their own permissions.

Use source=project when the effective maximum inherits the project limit. Use source=unknown rather than implying there is no limit. Pass an empty contentTypes array for a confirmed unrestricted policy or null for unknown.
Supply exact MIME patterns the provider accepts. The host owns upload validation, access checks, loading and editing. Localize labels or supply formatSize when the host uses another unit convention.

name: EnvironmentVariableList
description: Configuration inventory with readable values, named references and sealed entries.
code: <EnvironmentVariableList label="Production variables" variables={[{id:"url",name:"PUBLIC_APP_URL",kind:"plain",value:"https://app.studio.example"},{id:"db",name:"DATABASE_URL",kind:"reference",source:"Postgres / PRIVATE_URL"},{id:"key",name:"SIGNING_KEY",kind:"sealed"}]} />
notes: Supply a stable ID and name for each variable. Pass only display-safe values as plain. Sealed entries carry no value and have no built-in copy or reveal action.
A reference shows the named source and links to it when href is supplied. Pass the source name without resolving the referenced value.
A nonempty plain value copies in full, including when clipped. An empty string displays an empty-value label.
Use renderActions for authorized management flows owned by the host. Use KeyValueEditor for an editable draft and StagedChanges for pending changes.

name: ApiKeyList
description: Scan API credentials by scope, last use and lifecycle state, with copy for explicitly public keys.
code: <ApiKeyList label="Project API keys" keys={[{id:"sync",label:"Warehouse sync",kind:"secret",status:"active",scope:"Production",fingerprint:"•••• 7f2a"}]} />
notes: Use ApiKeyList for the inventory in project or account settings. Pass safe fingerprints and host-reported scope, status and last-used time. Keep full secret values out of the inventory payload.

Supply getPublishableValue only for values intended for public clients. It and the Copy action are available for active publishable keys. Show a newly created secret in a separate, authorized creation flow.

renderActions is called for active keys. Name the key and relevant scope in confirmation before revoking it. Update status after the host confirms success and move focus to a stable destination if the action disappears.
Use AccessSummary for the capabilities of a connection and SessionList for signed-in devices. Localize status, kind, empty-state and copy labels with labels.

name: PasskeyList
description: Recognize registered passkeys by name, provider and sign-in history.
code: <PasskeyList label="Registered passkeys" passkeys={[{id:"work",label:"Work laptop",provider:"Windows Hello",added:{dateTime:"2026-11-10",label:"Nov 10"}}]} />
notes: Use in account security settings for registered sign-in keys. Keep registration, rename, and permissions in the host. Use SessionList to manage signed-in sessions.
Supply an opaque record ID and display-safe metadata. Show the provider only when known. Pass null for lastUsed only when confirmed unused, and omit it when usage is unknown.

Use renderActions for eligible row actions. Name the exact passkey in removal confirmation, preserve it if the request fails, and recover focus to a stable control when the row disappears. The host determines whether removing a key is allowed.
Localize the empty state and labels with labels, and pass localized date text together with a machine-readable date.

name: KeyRotationSummary
description: Review which credential takes over and when the previous key stops working.
code: <KeyRotationSummary current={{label:"Warehouse sync", fingerprint:"7f2a"}} replacement={{label:"Warehouse sync v2", fingerprint:"a4c8"}} retirement={{mode:"scheduled", dateTime:"2026-11-19T16:45:00Z"}} />
notes: Place in a review step once the host knows the replacement and retirement policy. Use immediate if the previous key stops working on rotation, scheduled for a known cutoff, and manual if it remains accepted until revoked.
Supply display-safe names and optional fingerprints only. The application owns authorization, confirmation and execution. Use ApiKeyList for the settings inventory.

Use an ISO timestamp with an explicit offset for scheduled retirement. Pass the display timeZone and lang to show a localized cutoff with an explicit offset. Localize the row and state names through labels.

name: AccessSummary
description: The acting identity, scope and resource permissions for a connection or delegated operation.
code:
<AccessSummary actor="Expense assistant" actingFor="Maya Chen" scope="Finance workspace" permissions={[
  {id:"receipts",resource:"Receipts",access:"read",description:"Open receipts attached to expense reports."},
  {id:"notes",resource:"Review notes",access:"read-write",description:"Read and add notes to expense reports."},
  {id:"payments",resource:"Payments",access:"none"},
]} />
notes: Use for an effective or proposed access summary. Name the account, service or agent performing the action and the workspace, project or environment it can reach. Add actingFor when a different identity delegates access.
Pass read, write or read-write as granted by the host. Use none only for a known restriction worth explaining. An unavailable permission result is a separate loading or error state.

Describe consequential capabilities in plain language. Use labels to localize terms and badge text. Narrow rows move explanations below the resource and its access label; at very small widths, all three stack.
For consent, place the summary in the evidence slot of ApprovalRequest or in the relevant confirmation. Keep the actual authorization, saving, revocation and requests in the host.

name: AccessRequestForm
description: Request access to a restricted resource from the current account, with pending and unavailable states.
code: <AccessRequestForm resource={{id:"roadmap",label:"Release roadmap"}} account="maya@example.test" state={requestState} onSubmit={requestAccess} />
notes: Use on a restricted resource the signed-in user may discover. Supply only metadata the current account is authorized to see. The displayed account receives access if the host approves the request.

Provide message only when the reviewer can use it. Keep the draft controlled and preserve it on failure. Set sending in flight and requested after the host accepts the request, so a refresh can show the same state.
Use unavailable when policy disallows requests. Give a specific reason and offer an eligible next step such as switching accounts when available.
The host validates the account and resource, deduplicates requests, and owns approval. Use AccessInviteForm when an administrator sends an invitation to someone else.

name: SharingPanel
description: Review direct access and stage a change to the general sharing scope.
exampleState:
const [scope, setScope] = useState("restricted");
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(scope);
code:
<SharingPanel title="Share collection"
  scopes={[{id:"restricted",label:"Restricted",description:"Only invited people can open this collection."},{id:"public",label:"Public",description:"Anyone can find and view this collection."}]}
  effectiveScope={scope} draftScope={draft} onDraftScopeChange={setDraft} onApply={setScope}
  members={[{id:"maya",name:"Maya Chen",role:"Owner"}]} />
notes: Use for one resource. Write who can find or open the resource for each available general scope. List direct grants separately so a restricted resource still shows its invited members.
Treat effectiveScope as the policy accepted by the service. Choosing a draft scope requires Apply access. Set pending while saving; preserve the draft and show an error if the request fails.

Supply shareUrl only for the enforced scope and for a link the viewer can copy. Use the header action slot for an authorized invitation entry point. The host applies permissions and publishes or revokes links.

name: AccessInviteForm
description: Invite one person to a named workspace, team, or project with an explicit role.
code: <AccessInviteForm scope={{id:"app",label:"Customer portal"}} roles={[{id:"viewer",label:"Viewer",description:"Can view this project and its reports."}]} value={invite} onValueChange={setInvite} onSubmit={sendInvite} />
notes: Choose the resource upstream and display its name in the form. Pass only roles the host can offer for this scope, each with a stable nonempty ID and one consequence-oriented description.
Use an empty roleId to require active selection. The form also requires a valid email and blocks submission when the selected ID is no longer available.

The draft is controlled. Reset or reconcile it when the resource changes. onSubmit receives the email, the chosen role ID and the fixed scope ID. The host authorizes this combination again before sending.
Use pending while sending, emailError for an address-specific rejection, and error for request-level failure. Keep the draft on failure and show success after the host accepts the invitation.
Use PermissionEditor to modify a role definition and AccessSummary to review the effective capabilities of an existing grant.

name: PermissionEditor
description: Edit grouped role permissions and see the role or policy behind fixed access.
code: <PermissionEditor label="Release operator" groups={[{id:"deploy",label:"Deployments",permissions:[{id:"read",label:"View deployments",granted:true,inheritedFrom:"Member"},{id:"start",label:"Start deployments",granted:false}]}]} />
notes: Use in role settings when people can grant individual capabilities. Group related actions by resource and identify the affected role in the fieldset label.
Supply granted and inheritedFrom from the host. An inherited row shows its resolved state and the named source. Use onGrantChange to update a draft and commit it through the enclosing form.
Omit onGrantChange for a read-only review. Set disabled while an editable draft is unavailable or saving. The host validates and authorizes the submitted permissions.
Use AccessSummary to explain effective consent for a connected app and ComparisonTable to compare several fixed roles.

name: CidrField
description: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 range with a prefix length and native form validation.
code: <CidrField name="range" label="IP range" value={range} onValueChange={setRange} placeholder="203.0.113.0/24" required />
notes: Use for one address and explicit prefix length. Omit family when both IPv4 and IPv6 are allowed. Pass an example for the permitted family.

Keep the value as typed. The field checks syntax and prefix bounds and does not normalize host bits, infer a missing prefix, authorize an address or compare ranges. The host owns those policy decisions and revalidates before saving.
Pass error for a host rejection. Compose NetworkAllowlist to display the submitted or applied ranges and make the draft scope clear.

name: NetworkAllowlist
description: See which networks can reach a connection endpoint and copy exact allowed ranges.
code: <NetworkAllowlist title="Database connections" access={{mode:"allowlist",entries:[{id:"office",label:"Studio VPN",family:"IPv4",cidr:"203.0.113.24/29"},{id:"runner",label:"Build runners",family:"IPv6",cidr:"2001:db8:abcd::/48"}]}} />
notes: Name the connection scope. Pass the mode reported by the host. Use unrestricted or blocked only when the effective network policy is known. An empty allowlist renders its own empty state and does not imply either mode.
Pass display-ready CIDRs and IP families. Long IPv6 values wrap while copy preserves every character, including the prefix length. Use labels to localize the mode and clipboard feedback.

Use renderRuleAction to place an authorized host action beside a range when needed. The host owns validation, confirmation, editing and policy enforcement. Use RestrictionSummary for general restrictions unrelated to network endpoints.

name: ContentReportForm
description: Collect a reason and supporting details for a report about a specific record.
code:
<ContentReportForm aria-label="Report post" draft={draft} onDraftChange={setDraft}
  reasons={[{id:"spam",label:"Spam"},{id:"other",label:"Something else",requiresDetails:true}]}
  onSubmit={report => { /* Submit to the host moderation service. */ }} />
notes: Identify the reported post or record in the host's heading or subject slot. Supply reasons from the applicable policy. Mark details required only for reasons that need specific context.

The component submits a selected, available reason and trimmed details within maxDetails. The host owns the recipient, submission, policy validation and confirmation. Use pending while sending and preserve the draft on error.
Use ContentAdvisory to reveal a content warning, and MutedWordForm for a personal visibility preference. Reporting initiates moderation review.

name: ContentReportStatus
description: Show the current review state and any published outcome of a submitted content report.
code:
<ContentReportStatus title="Comment by @jules.example" reason="Spam"
  submittedAt={{dateTime:"2026-11-14"}}
  review={{phase:"action-taken",summary:"The comment was removed for spam."}} />
notes: Render one accepted report in a reporting history or detail panel. Use a display-safe subject and pass the recorded reason and submission date when they help identify it.
Use submitted after acceptance. Use in-review only when the service exposes that state. Supply action-taken or no-action and an optional reporter-visible summary from the published decision.
Use ContentReportForm for collecting a report. The host owns status retrieval, disclosure decisions and any follow-up actions. Use ServiceIncident for public operational updates over time.

name: AccountStanding
description: Show overall account standing, the confirmed active strike count and the next known expiry.
code: <AccountStanding title="Account standing" standing="at-risk" activeStrikes={2} nextExpiry={{dateTime:"2026-12-01"}} description="Further violations may temporarily restrict posting." historyAction={<Link href="/moderation/history">Moderation history</Link>} />
notes: Use in the affected person's moderation inbox or account settings. The host supplies account standing and permissions independently of the active strike count. Never calculate an enforcement level or appeal eligibility from a count in the component.
Pass zero for a confirmed clear strike count and omit the count if unknown. Show the next expiry only when the service reports it. Use unknown standing if the standing itself is unavailable.

Use historyAction to open permitted overall history and ModerationNotice for the effect and appeal path of a specific decision. Keep reports filed by the viewer separate from enforcement on that viewer's account.
Use description only for a concrete impact or next step that the standing label does not convey. Localize the state and fact labels.

name: ModerationNotice
description: Explain an account or content restriction and show its current effect and appeal path.
code:
<ModerationNotice title="Posting restriction" reason="We found unsolicited promotions in several of your comments." effect="active"
  endsAt={{dateTime:"2026-11-17T12:00:00Z",timeZone:"UTC"}}
  appeal={{state:"available",action:<Link href="/moderation/appeals/new">Appeal decision</Link>}} />
notes: Describe the affected capability or content in the title and explain the published reason. Pass the effective restriction state from the host.
Show the end of a temporary restriction and any appeal deadline as distinct dates. Supply the viewer's time zone or a display-ready label when time precision matters.

Pass an action only while an appeal is available. Once accepted by the service, show the submitted or resolved appeal state without its original action. The host owns eligibility, deadlines, submission, and enforcement.

Use ContentReportStatus to show a report to the person who filed it. This notice is for the person whose account or content was affected. Use ModerationAppealForm to request reconsideration of the named decision.

name: ModerationAppealForm
description: Write and submit an appeal for a specific moderation decision while keeping the original reason in view.
code:
<ModerationAppealForm aria-label="Appeal decision"
  decision={{id:"restriction-38",title:"Posting restriction",reason:"We found unsolicited promotions in your comments."}}
  value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft}
  onSubmit={appeal => { /* Send the appeal and preserve the draft if refused. */ }} />
notes: Mount as its own form inside the appropriate page or overlay. Pass the actual decision ID and a display-safe title and reason. Keep a separate draft per decision if the same editor can change records.

The component keeps over-limit text editable, blocks blank or over-limit submission, and submits the trimmed explanation with the decision ID. Use pending to retain the visible draft while the service processes it.

Pass an actionable error on refusal and keep the draft. The host verifies eligibility and owns submitting, cancellation and transition to the accepted state. Show the accepted status in ModerationNotice after the service confirms it.

name: ContentLabelSettings
description: Choose how labels from one moderation provider affect visible content.
code:
<ContentLabelSettings title="Community Moderation"
  preferences={[{id:"spoilers",label:"Spoilers",description:"Reveals a story or result.",visibility}]}
  onVisibilityChange={(_id, next) => setVisibility(next)} />
notes: Group labels by their named provider. Supply the accepted preference for each label. Show, Warn and Hide apply to content carrying that label. The host maps these choices to its policy.
Pass lockedReason with the effective visibility if a policy fixes a choice. The row shows the value and the reason without an editable control.
The host owns persistence, policy resolution and what a warning or hide means in the feed. Use ContentAdvisory for a warning with deliberate reveal in the affected view.

name: MutedWordForm
description: Draft a word, phrase or tag mute with a match scope, duration and optional exception.
code:
<MutedWordForm value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft}
  onSubmit={rule => { /* Validate the term and resolve the duration when saving. */ }} />
notes: Mount as its own form. The component trims outer whitespace on submission. The host defines matching, normalization, duplicate checks and permissions.
Keep the draft while pending or after refusal. Use termError for a problem tied to the word and error for a save failure. Reset the draft after the host accepts the rule.
Resolve timed durations to an absolute expiry at save time. Pass the accepted rule to MutedWordList with its expiry and exception.

name: MutedWordList
description: Read active personal word and tag mutes with their match scope, exceptions and expiry.
code: <MutedWordList rules={[{id:"finale",term:"season finale",scope:"text-and-tags",excludeFollowing:true,expiration:{dateTime:"2026-11-30T16:00:00Z"}},{id:"giveaway",term:"#giveaway",scope:"tags-only"}]} />
notes: Pass only active rules. A rule without expiration remains active until removed. The host owns matching, policy, the viewer's relationships and expiry.
Use localized scope labels and pass timeZone for the intended display context. Use expiration.label when the host already supplies the displayed time.

Use renderRuleAction for host-owned edits or removal. Keep focus on a nearby action or the section when the last rule goes away. Use ContentAdvisory where the user can deliberately reveal filtered content.

name: RestrictionSummary
description: Read which items a policy allows or blocks and see where each rule applies.
code: <RestrictionSummary label="Spending restrictions" groups={[{id:"card", label:"Merchants", source:"This card", mode:"allow-list", entries:[{id:"linear", label:"Linear"}]}, {id:"company", label:"Merchants", source:"Company policy", mode:"block-list", entries:[{id:"parcel", label:"ParcelPoint"}]}]} />
notes: Use to read configured restrictions in settings or a review panel. Keep each rule grouped with its policy source when several scopes apply.
Pass entries for an allow list or block list. Use unrestricted for an explicitly known unrestricted scope. Keep unavailable or still-loading policy data in the host's loading or error state.
The host owns ordering, precedence and enforcement. Use PolicyEvaluation for the decision and evidence from a specific attempt. Translate mode labels through modeLabels.

name: RecordMergeReview
description: Review which record will be merged and which will remain canonical before confirming.
code: <RecordMergeReview source={{id:"source",title:"Invoice search fails after refresh",reference:"SUP-238"}} destination={{id:"target",title:"Invoice search drops the active query",reference:"ENG-814"}} consequence="Comments and attachments move to ENG-814." onMerge={(sourceId, destinationId) => console.log(sourceId, destinationId)} onCancel={() => console.log("Cancelled")} />
notes: Use after a host-owned destination search or match selection. Pass distinct stable IDs and supply a human-readable reference when names can be similar.
Describe the actual effect on comments, attachments, references or history. The host controls authorization, reversibility and the commit request. A review does not compute or mutate a merge.
Place inside a Dialog when the review needs its own confirmation step. Let the surrounding header name the task. In an inline review, supply its title in the surrounding layout.
Drive pending and error with the request state. Keep the chosen records present if the request fails. Confirm receives sourceId first and destinationId second.

name: ScheduledTaskList
description: Review scheduled and event-triggered tasks, their current state and confirmed next run.
code: <ScheduledTaskList label="Scheduled tasks" tasks={[{id:"digest",label:"Weekly release digest",state:"active",trigger:{kind:"schedule",label:"Mondays at 09:00 UTC",nextRun:{dateTime:"2026-11-23T09:00:00Z",timeZone:"UTC"}}},{id:"build",label:"Summarize failed builds",state:"paused",trigger:{kind:"event",label:"When a build fails"}}]} />
notes: Use for registered tasks with host-owned triggers. Show a short, meaningful cadence or event label. Supply the next run only when the scheduler has confirmed its date and time.
Next run appears only for active time-based tasks. Paused tasks keep their trigger details. Event tasks retain their event without a fabricated run time.
Use renderAction for a permitted host-owned pause, resume or management control. Keep the accepted state during requests, preserve row IDs and show refusal through host feedback.
Use RecurrenceEditor to edit schedules, RetrySchedule for a delivery retry, and PipelineRun for the execution stages of one run.

name: ScheduledRunHistory
description: Inspect when a scheduled job ran, whether it was triggered manually, and why an execution was skipped.
code: <ScheduledRunHistory label="Export runs" timeZone="UTC" runs={[{id:"run-42",status:"skipped",scheduledFor:"2026-11-17T09:00:00Z",detail:"The previous run was still active."},{id:"run-41",status:"succeeded",trigger:"schedule",startedAt:"2026-11-17T08:00:04Z",durationMs:42000}]} />
notes: Use for the executions of one named scheduled job. Use ScheduledTaskList for configured tasks and their next runs, or PipelineRun to inspect stages within one execution.

Supply startedAt and the actual trigger for started executions. Supply scheduledFor for a skipped slot. Skipped rows do not report a start time or duration. A running duration is elapsed so far; omit durationMs when it is unknown.

Keep IDs and chronological order stable when the host refreshes. Include a short, display-safe failure or skip reason when known. Use href only when a run or skipped slot has its own detail destination.
Timestamps require an explicit offset and display in timeZone, UTC by default. The host owns scheduling, execution, pagination, and loading or failure before the history is available.

name: EvidenceChecklist
description: Track each supporting requirement from missing or requested to received, accepted or waived.
code: <EvidenceChecklist label="Expense evidence" requirements={[{id:"receipt",label:"Itemized receipt",state:"requested",detail:"Waiting for the cardholder."},{id:"memo",label:"Business purpose",state:"accepted"}]} />
notes: Use in the detail view for a request, expense or case when the evidence has its own review lifecycle. Supply real host states. Received means evidence arrived; accepted means a reviewer or policy accepted it. Waived means the requirement was explicitly removed.

Use href to open the material the viewer may inspect. Use renderAction for one permitted next step, such as requesting an item or opening a review. Keep mutations, permissions and focus recovery in the host.

Use FieldChecklist for live validation of input requirements, ReceiptMatchReview for comparing values, and ApprovalRequest for the overall decision. Keep evidence completion separate from the parent decision.
Place inside a visibly titled section when the surrounding record needs one. Localize stateLabels and emptyLabel. Use a compact layout without dividers unless the host needs row boundaries.

name: ReceiptMatchReview
description: Compare receipt and transaction evidence side by side and spot reported discrepancies.
code: <ReceiptMatchReview title="Receipt match" outcome="needs-review" fields={[{id:"amount", label:"Amount", receipt:"$128.40", transaction:"$182.40", differs:true}, {id:"merchant", label:"Merchant", receipt:"Northstar Print", transaction:"Northstar Print"}]} />
notes: Use in an expense review panel when people must inspect the actual values from two sources. Use PolicyEvaluation for rule checks and ApprovalRequest for submitting a decision.

The host owns the verification outcome and flags discrepancies. Supply display-ready values with currency, time zone or locale context as needed. Omit unavailable values. Preserve the source order and use stable, unique field IDs.
Localize the title and labels. Check that both columns remain readable at drawer width and that the reported outcome stays distinct from individual differences.

name: AdvisorFinding
description: Inspect a diagnostic finding with its severity, affected resource, impact and supporting evidence.
code: <AdvisorFinding title="Foreign key has no index" severity="warning" resource="public.invoice_lines" impact="Deleting an invoice can scan invoice lines for references." evidence="The invoice_id foreign key has no supporting index." rule="unindexed_foreign_key" />
notes: Use for a diagnosed finding with a known affected resource. Lead with a short diagnosis and explain its practical effect. Show only evidence the viewer may inspect.
Severity belongs to the finding and is supplied by the host. It does not imply that the current viewer can change the resource or that a repair succeeded.

Keep supporting observations in Evidence. Omit that disclosure when neither evidence nor a diagnostic rule ID exists. Show a documentation link or a host-owned action in remediation when the next step is available.
Use PolicyEvaluation for the checks that explain a policy decision and CheckRunList for run outcomes. Keep scan execution and remediation permissions in the host.

name: PolicyEvaluation
description: Explains the outcome of a policy evaluation with ordered checks and observed evidence.
code: <PolicyEvaluation title="Finance review required" checks={[{id:"amount",label:"Amount is at least $5,000",status:"matched",evidence:"Submitted amount is $8,450"}]} />
notes: Use the host-reported outcome as the title. Supply applied rule checks in evaluation order with stable, unique IDs and display-safe evidence.
Use matched and unmatched for completed conditions, skipped for a branch the evaluator intentionally did not run, and unavailable for missing data or a failed evaluation.
Localize statusLabels and checkListLabel. Keep the host as the authority for rule evaluation, authorization and any next action.
Use ApprovalChain for the actual reviewer route and ApprovalRequest for a decision the current user can submit.

name: ApprovalChain
description: Follow the reviewers and decisions in an ordered approval route.
code: <ApprovalChain label="Approval route" stages={[{id:"owner",label:"Budget owner",status:"approved",reviewers:[{id:"maya",name:"Maya Chen"}]},{id:"finance",label:"Finance",status:"pending",approvals:{received:1,required:2}}]} />
notes: Use for a read-only route, beside the request facts or in a detail surface. Use ApprovalRequest for submitting a decision.
Supply the current host-reported stages in route order. Reviewers within one stage can have independent statuses. Add a reviewer detail for identity context such as delegation.

Use approvals on a stage when the threshold helps readers track a parallel decision. Supply received and required from the host. The visible reviewer list can be partial or include people who do not count toward the requirement. Localize the count with formatApprovalCount.
Pass actual recorded times with timeLabel and dateTime. Queued stages can omit unknown reviewers. Localize statusLabels and keep authorization, parallel rules, and advancement in the host.

name: ApprovalRequest
description: An inline approval form with request evidence, decision consequences and choice-specific notes.
code: <ApprovalRequest title="Renew Northstar Analytics" evidence={<DescriptionList items={[{id:"amount",term:"Requested amount",description:"$18,400"}]} />} options={[{id:"approve",label:"Approve renewal",consequence:"Send to Finance for payment."},{id:"changes",label:"Request changes",consequence:"Return the request to the owner.",note:{label:"Changes needed",requiredMessage:"Describe the change you need."}}]} draft={draft} onDraftChange={setDraft} onDecision={submitDecision} status={status} />
notes: Use when outcomes or authorization scopes need comparison before submission. Put the request target and impact in evidence. Use AlertDialog for a single short confirmation, or the proposed action recipe when reviewers can edit structured arguments in a separate editor.

Supply a controlled draft with decisionId and note. Use stable option IDs and mark unavailable outcomes disabled. A note with requiredMessage needs non-whitespace text. The draft retains the note when switching choices, and onDecision includes the trimmed note only for the active choice's note field.

The host owns permissions, request identity and revision, submitting/error/resolved state, and execution. Keep the draft after an error and report the actual decision outcome after acceptance. Key the component and initialize the draft for a new request or revision.

Translate labels.decision, labels.submit and note text. Render outside other forms. While submitting the commit button retains focus. If resolution removes the focused form, focus moves to the result.

name: AlertDialog
description: A focused confirmation with explicit cancel and continue actions.
code: <AlertDialog title="Archive this project?" description="You can restore it from the archive." confirmLabel="Archive project" trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Archive project</Button>} onConfirm={() => { /* Archive in the host application. */ }} />
notes: Uses the original Flood Dialog modal layer with role=alertdialog, a required message and initial focus on Cancel. Tab stays inside the modal; Escape cancels and restores trigger focus. Outside clicks do not dismiss it. There is no extra close action competing with the explicit Cancel button.

onConfirm is a host callback followed by a close request. onCancel handles the Cancel button and Escape, not confirmation. Use open/onOpenChange for host-controlled state and confirmDisabled to prevent confirmation while unavailable. Async work/errors belong to the host; callbacks are not awaited.
Translate title, description, confirmLabel and cancelLabel. Use ordinary Dialog for forms and exploratory content. Available in 0.2.5.

name: DeploymentRollbackDialog
description: Confirm which deployment will replace the live build and what the rollback changes.
code:
<DeploymentRollbackDialog
  current={{id:"dep-1042",label:"Restrict export link access"}}
  target={{id:"dep-1038",label:"Stabilize preview exports"}}
  description="Production will serve the selected build with its original configuration."
  trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Review rollback</Button>}
  onConfirm={(targetId, currentId) => { /* Submit both IDs to the host. */ }}
/>
notes: Open once the user has selected a specific target. Both deployment IDs are displayed so builds with the same label can be distinguished.

Use description for the consequence in this environment. Pass unavailableReason for an ineligible target and confirmDisabled while requests are unavailable. Identical current and target IDs block confirmation.

The host owns eligibility, stale-deployment checks, the request and retry. onConfirm receives target ID first and observed live ID second. Confirmation requests close immediately; use controlled open state if the host must wait for a response.

name: Drawer
description: A modal edge panel with a steady header, scrollable body and optional footer.
code:
<Drawer title="Project settings" description="Keep the details close." trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Open settings</Button>}>
  <Field label="Project name">{control => <Input {...control} defaultValue="Flood" />}</Field>
</Drawer>
notes: Use Drawer for a bounded task alongside a collection. Use a page for a long-running task or when the record needs a shareable route. Check that the opener, or a surviving fallback, receives focus after a save removes the original row.

In a settings Drawer, give peer sections consistent heading size, body inset and spacing. Align repeated labels and controls on shared tracks, then test with a narrow viewport and dense content so the footer stays reachable.

Uses Flood native Dialog focus containment, scroll lock, background inertness, nested layers and return focus. Escape and the named close IconButton dismiss it; closeOnOutsideClick defaults to true. Controlled open/onOpenChange and initialFocusRef match Dialog.
Drawer inherits getFallbackFocus from Dialog. Use it when saving or deleting can remove the opening row from a collection.

side is logical start/end or physical top/bottom. size sets 20/26/34rem for sm/md/lg, capped to the viewport. Vertical drawers occupy the viewport height; horizontal drawers occupy its width. Entry motion respects reduced motion; closing is immediate.

Choose width against a populated record. For longer messages and several controls, compare md and lg. Use the description slot for short context and compose independent body groups with Section or Fieldset. Keep persistent actions in footer.

The body scrolls with Flood ScrollArea while the header and optional footer remain visible when space allows. Responsive padding and full-width narrow descriptions preserve the reading area at enlarged text; if the chrome cannot fit, the whole panel can scroll rather than clipping the body. Footer actions are host-owned, without implicit save or close. No swipe/drag gesture or nested navigation engine is included. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Sheet
description: A bottom-aligned modal for short tasks, navigation and touch-friendly choices.
code:
<Sheet title="Project settings" trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Open settings</Button>}>
  <Field label="Project name">{control => <Input {...control} defaultValue="Flood" />}</Field>
</Sheet>
notes: When switching the same short task between Drawer and Sheet, share the draft, wording and actions. Keep the state in the host and verify both dismissal and focus restoration at each supported width.
Sheet shares Drawer's modal semantics, dismissal, focus restoration, scrollable body and optional footer. Its scrollbar fits in the panel padding. Placement is always bottom.
The panel grows with content up to its size limit. Keep actions that must remain visible in the footer and use ListBox for selectable options.
Use a sheet for touch navigation or short choices that benefit from a wider target. Anchored popovers and selects remain useful on desktop. Available in 0.2.12.

name: CopyButton
description: A clipboard action with stable geometry and localized result feedback.
code: <CopyButton value="npm install @flood-md/react" />
notes: Copies only on a user click. Requires a secure context and Clipboard API; onCopyError receives unavailable/denied errors. The host owns any manual-copy fallback. Native button ref and disabled semantics are preserved.

Localize copyLabel/copiedLabel/errorLabel. resetDelay restores the idle state after success. Labels reserve their common width and a live status announces the result. No remote data transfer is built in. Available in 0.2.5.
Use iconOnly for a square IconButton when the nearby content makes the copy target clear. The button keeps its accessible name and success or failure feedback.

name: FollowButton
description: A subscription action with stable width across follow, following and requested states.
code: <FollowButton subject="Maya Chen" state="not-following" onAction={intent => { /* Send the intent to the host. */ }} />
notes: Use beside a recognizable account or feed identity. Keep separately configurable notifications in their own control.

Send the intent to the host and update state on acceptance. Use requested for a submitted follow request awaiting approval. Use pending for an in-flight request to suppress repeat activation and keep focus.
Keep the settled state on failure and tell the user how to retry. Localize labels and formatActionLabel together so the accessible name includes the visible label and distinguishes the next action.

name: ToastRegion
description: A host-controlled notification queue with timed, pausable messages and actions.
code: <ToastRegion items={[{id:"saved",title:"Changes saved",status:"success",duration:0}]} onDismiss={id => { /* Remove the item from host state. */ }} />
notes: The host owns items and removes them onDismiss. IDs must be unique/nonempty. limit controls visible items; queued timers start only when visible. Ordinary messages default to five seconds; error/action messages persist unless duration is explicit. duration=0 persists.

Timers pause on hover, focus and hidden documents. F8 focuses the first visible region without interrupting initial task focus; hotkey=false disables it. Use a single main region per document. Localize label/closeLabel and message/action text. Error messages announce as alerts; others use polite status.
The stack uses an overlay scrollbar when displayed messages exceed its height. Focusing a dismissal or recovery action reveals it within the stack.

placement is logical start/end. inline embeds the region in a host container; fixed mode uses ordinary document stacking, so place a contextual region inside a modal if needed. Action callbacks do not dismiss automatically. No global notification store or promise API. Available in 0.2.5.

name: AvatarGroup
description: A compact collection of avatars with a count or an optional list of additional people.
code: <AvatarGroup label="Project collaborators" items={[{id:"alex",name:"Alex Morgan"},{id:"sam",name:"Sam Lee"},{id:"june",name:"June Park"}]} max={2} />
notes: The native list composes Flood Avatar. IDs and names must be nonempty and unique IDs remain stable. max is a positive integer; the default shows four people.
The default overflow is a static count. Use overflowPresentation="popover" when readers need the remaining names. Translate overflowLabel and overflowTitle as needed.
Visible avatars retain their accessible names. The popover shows only the additional people and uses ScrollArea when the list grows. The button has clearance from the overlapping avatar row.
Supply presence on individual items when known. Visible avatars separate to give each presence mark clearance. Additional names in the popover retain their presence.
Use spacing="separated" to give each face its own space even without presence. The default auto layout overlaps avatars unless a visible presence mark needs clearance.

Use layout="fit" in a bounded toolbar, table cell or summary where the group should use one line. It shows as many faces as fit up to max, and the same overflow disclosure accounts for hidden faces. The default wrap layout shows up to max faces across lines.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: AuthorMeta
description: An avatar, a person’s name and optional secondary information on one shared axis.
code: <AuthorMeta name="Maya Chen" metadata={<Timestamp dateTime="2026-11-14">14 Nov</Timestamp>} />
notes: Use AuthorMeta for attribution in comments, activity entries and compact contributor rows. Use Avatar alone for an image-only person reference.
The avatar is decorative because the adjacent name identifies the person. Supply Timestamp for a date or concise text for a role. Optional presence adds an availability mark and its accessible label.
Use metadataPlacement="inline" for a short timestamp beside the name. Metadata can wrap onto the next line as space runs out. The default stacks metadata below the name.

Use nameOverflow="truncate" in a constrained row when the visible prefix still identifies the person. The full name is available on hover and keyboard focus when clipped. Choose one size for peer rows and keep lifecycle states and row actions in their own slots.

name: StarterPackPreview
description: Preview the curator, recommended people and sample feeds in a starter pack.
code: <StarterPackPreview title="Independent type designers" href="/packs/type-design" curator="Maya Chen" people={[{id:"sam",name:"Sam Rivera"}]} feeds={[{id:"workbench",label:"Type workbench"}]} />
notes: Use in discovery or sharing when the recommendation bundle includes people, feeds or both. The counts come from the supplied recommendations, so pass the complete lists.

The avatar group shows a sample with an overflow count. The first two named feeds help preview the subject. Provide href when the user can open the complete pack. Omit the corresponding list if that kind has no recommendations.
Supply publishable names and images. The host owns visibility, ordering, following and subscribing. Use ProfileSummary for an individual identity and CollectionCard for a collection of media.

name: ProfileSummary
description: A profile identity, short bio, contextual facts and independently actionable controls.
code: <ProfileSummary name="Maya Chen" handle="@mayachen" href="/people/maya-chen" description="Designing collaboration tools." facts={[{id:"followers",label:"followers",value:248,href:"/people/maya-chen/followers"}]} />
notes: Use in the body of a result, panel or HoverCard when identity alone is too little context. The parent supplies the surface. For a byline or a row with only secondary identity, use AuthorMeta.

Use href to link the identity and use independent links in facts when a destination exists. Place FollowButton or other profile actions in actions. Keep the surrounding row or overlay free of interactive wrappers around the entire summary.

Supply a short display-ready bio and facts that help the reader decide. Keep unknown facts absent and pass zero for a known empty count. Check a long handle in a narrow panel and make sure actions remain reachable.

name: Comment
description: An attributed message with an avatar, optional timestamp and message actions.
code: <Comment author={{name:"Maya Chen", metadata:<Timestamp dateTime="2026-11-14">14 Nov</Timestamp>}}>The export is ready for review.</Comment>
notes: Use Comment for an attributed message in a review or conversation. AuthorMeta owns the avatar, name and date. The body and actions share the author text axis.

Pass the message as children. Use named ghost IconButton or icon-only CopyButton for secondary message actions. They appear on hover or focus without shifting the message and stay visible on touch. Use actionVisibility=always when an action must be discoverable at rest.

Pass onReply to show the standard reply action, and replyLabel to localize it. The host chooses where to open and focus the editor, and restores focus when cancelling. CommentThread items support the same callback.
Use CommentThread for related messages and Timeline in activity mode for chronological system events. Keep permissions, reply state and data in the host.
Use attachments for FileList and reactions for ReactionButton. Reactions share the command row, remain visible when secondary actions are quiet, and belong to this message.
Pass a ReactionPicker to reactionPicker. Its trigger stays visible next to existing reactions. An empty comment reveals it with the secondary actions.

name: CommentThread
description: A chronological list of related comments with shared spacing and optional dividers.
code: <CommentThread aria-label="Review comments" items={[{id:"one",author:{name:"Maya Chen"},body:"Please include the original attachment."},{id:"two",author:{name:"Sam Rivera"},body:"I found the source file."}]} />
notes: Provide stable nonempty IDs that are unique within each sibling list. Pass items in reading order, and name the list using aria-label or aria-labelledby.
Each item uses Comment for the author, message and independent actions. Pass nested replies under their parent. Depth stays semantic while visual indentation is capped to preserve narrow text widths.

Spacing separates top-level messages by default. Use dividers only when peers are hard to distinguish, and repliesDisclosure for long branches. Pair with CommentComposer for drafting. The host owns reply targeting, permissions and loading.

name: ReviewThread
description: A review discussion with a visible resolution and a host-controlled resolve or reopen action.
code: <ReviewThread title="Release notes review" resolved={true} resolution="Link to the versioned accessibility guide." items={[{id:"maya",author:{name:"Maya Chen"},body:"Which version should we link in the release notes?"},{id:"sam",author:{name:"Sam Rivera"},body:"Use the versioned guide so it matches the release."}]} />
notes: Use for a discussion whose state can be open or resolved. The original conversation stays visible in both states, and the optional resolution records a concrete decision or links to it.

Pass onResolvedChange to request a new value. Supply the accepted resolved value from the host, keep it during pending or error, and omit the callback for a read-only view. Localize labels and error copy.
Set headingLevel for the host outline. Place ReviewThread on the host surface and compose a CommentComposer next to it when the workflow accepts replies. Use CommentThread for conversation alone.

name: CommentComposer
description: A compact comment editor with optional reply context and a cancel command.
code: <CommentComposer label="Reply" placeholder="Write a reply…" sendLabel="Post reply" replyContext="Replying to Maya Chen" value="" onValueChange={() => {}} onSend={() => {}} />
notes: Use next to a CommentThread for a comment or reply. Supply localized context only when the reply target should be explicit.

The reply context sits above the input surface in a compact header and describes the editor for assistive technology. The input surface is shared with MessageComposer. The send action defaults to Reply with context and Post otherwise. Localize it with sendLabel. Enter submits and Shift+Enter inserts a line break.
If replies accept files in a narrow panel, set maxVisibleAttachments to keep the draft close to the visible file tags.
When cancellation removes the editor, the host should return focus to the initiating action. Preserve the draft on submission failure.

name: ReactionButton
description: A compact reaction toggle with a count and host-controlled selection.
code: <ReactionButton label="Helpful" icon="👍" count={6} pressed={false} />
notes: The label names the reaction, pressed identifies the current user's choice and count is the aggregate number of reactions.
Update pressed and count together after a host decision. The accessible name starts with the reaction label and includes the visible count.
Use reactions in Comment to keep them visible beside secondary commands. The ghost variant suits a mixed row of small icon actions.

name: ReactionPicker
description: An anchored chooser for adding a reaction from a small set of options.
code: <ReactionPicker options={[{id:"helpful",label:"Helpful",icon:"👍"},{id:"celebrate",label:"Celebrate",icon:"🙌"}]} onSelect={id => console.log(id)} />
notes: Supply a small set of distinct, named options. Icons are decorative. Each option needs an accessible label that names the reaction.
The chooser closes after selection and returns focus to its trigger. Arrow keys move through the option toolbar. Escape dismisses it.
Pass selected on options already applied by the current user. They remain interactive and use the same accent as a pressed ReactionButton. onSelect receives the ID and requested next selection state.
Use Comment reactionPicker next to its ReactionButton elements. The host controls reaction data, counts and which options are already applied.

name: PriorityIndicator
description: A ranked urgency marker for triage lists, tables and record summaries.
code: <PriorityIndicator level="high" />
notes: Levels are none, low, medium, high and urgent. Set label for localization. The host owns priority ordering and editing.
Use the default label when the value must be immediately readable. Use icon in a named compact column when the glyphs are recognizable. Hover and keyboard focus reveal the full value.
Use chip for consistent badge-style metadata. Keep one presentation and size across comparable records. Use StatusIndicator separately for lifecycle or operation state.
Compatible addition in 0.2.14.

name: StatusIndicator
description: A named state with a decorative dot, tinted chip or compact icon.
code: <StatusIndicator tone="success" label="All systems operational" />
notes: Place the lifecycle state beside the record name or in its own named field or column. Keep it separate from record actions. Use the same presentation and size for peer statuses.

The label stays on one line and reveals its full text on hover or focus if clipped. Choose a short, meaningful state name for dense rows. Use presentation="icon" with a recognizable state glyph and keep the full label for the tooltip and assistive technology.
Use presentation="wrap" for a prose-like message that should grow with its content. The dot is decorative. Use announce to opt into a polite live region for changing messages.

Use presentation="chip" when lifecycle states need a consistent tinted silhouette, such as in a status column or a record header. Choose the same size as peer Badge metadata. Long labels retain single-line truncation and the full-label tooltip.
Static labels do not announce by default. Tone is independent of wording and size. Use Badge for categorical labels and Alert for a message requiring more explanation.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Figure
description: A native figure that keeps media and its caption together.
notes: Composes native figure and figcaption. The host supplies the image, chart, code or other self-contained content, including its own alt text or accessible name.
captionPosition controls DOM reading order as well as placement. Caption content may contain links. Native hidden, dir, lang, style and ref target the figure.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: MediaCredit
description: Show the creator, publication and date of an image or other media.
notes: Use as secondary attribution beneath an image, chart or video. Omit facts that are unknown. Preserve the asset's own alternative text or accessible name.
Pass the original source destination when known and mark a candidate source unverified when its provenance is uncertain. The application supplies and verifies the references.
Use Figure's caption to associate the credit with the asset. Use Citation for evidence attached to a claim and SourceList for several references.

name: Blockquote
description: A quoted passage with an optional compact attribution.
code: Good interfaces make room for what matters.
notes: Uses native blockquote; cite remains a source URL, while attribution is visible host-authored credit. Rich quote content and attribution are supported.
The logical leading rule follows RTL. Supply quotation punctuation as part of your actual content; the component does not invent a quotation or source.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: RevealValue
description: A masked read-only value with explicit reveal and optional copy actions.
code: <RevealValue value="flood_demo_3f089bf2" showLabel="Show token" hideLabel="Hide token" hiddenValueLabel="Token hidden" copyLabel="Copy token" copyable />
notes: Use for read-only tokens or identifiers that should start visually concealed. The mask has a fixed length and the value enters the rendered text only after reveal.
Name the show, hide and optional copy actions for their value. Enable copyable only when copying is a supported operation. Copy becomes available when revealed and writes the exact value.
In a narrow value slot, the action group moves below the value and retains touch target sizes. The mask stays on a single line.
Use visible and onVisibleChange when the host controls disclosure. Keep authorization and secret retrieval in the host. Use PasswordInput for editable passwords.

name: CopyableValue
description: A visible value with a compact copy action.
code: <CopyableValue value="https://flood.md/mcp" copyLabel="Copy server URL" />
notes: Use for a visible URL, exact identifier or short value that people need to copy. Name the action for that value and localize copiedLabel and errorLabel when needed.

Long values wrap by default. Set overflow="truncate" when a recognizable prefix is enough in a dense row. Only clipped values get a tooltip and keyboard stop. The copy action writes the full value in either mode.
In truncate mode, use preserveEnd for identifiers with a meaningful ending. For example, preserveEnd={4} keeps a four-character request suffix visible where it fits.
Choose the code appearance for identifiers and short code values. Use CodeSnippet for commands that need a larger reading surface.

name: HttpMethod
description: A neutral, case-preserving HTTP method label for tables and request metadata.
code: <HttpMethod method="PROPFIND" />
notes: Use in a dedicated method column or as request metadata. Text is the default for dense lists. Use outline when the method needs a boundary beside nearby prose or code.

Pass the recorded method verbatim, including case-sensitive extension methods. Keep protocol tokens left-to-right in either document direction. Method labels are neutral; use HttpStatus for response outcome.
Set overflow=truncate in a constrained single-line layout. The full method is available from the clipped label. EndpointLabel uses this behavior in its shared method track.

name: EndpointLabel
description: An HTTP method and a readable request path on a shared line.
code: <EndpointLabel method="GET" path="/rest/v1/projects/{project_id}" />
notes: Use for a request row or an endpoint heading. Pass the actual method in its original case and a path or route template safe to display.

In constrained rows keep truncation and use preserveEnd when the tail distinguishes endpoints. The full path is available on focus and hover when clipped. Use overflow=wrap when readers need to see the entire path immediately.
Pair with HttpStatus for the response outcome. The label does not send requests or parse URLs.

name: DataFreshness
description: Show the update status and when the displayed data was last successfully refreshed.
code: <DataFreshness state="delayed" updatedAt="2026-11-16T08:10:00Z" relativeTo="2026-11-16T09:00:00Z" />
notes: Place beside a report or collection when the age of its data can change a decision. The host supplies the state using the availability of data and its update policy.

Use updatedAt for the last snapshot actually shown, including during an in-flight or failed update. Omit it if no update has succeeded. Pass relativeTo for relative time with an exact timestamp on hover and focus.
Place retry or connection controls alongside it using existing actions. Use StatusIndicator alone when there is no freshness information to convey.

name: RecoveryWindow
description: Show the bounds of a recovery window and where a selected restore point falls.
notes: Use for a continuous range of recoverable instants. Supply the actual earliest and latest restorable timestamps with explicit ISO offsets. Equal bounds represent one restore point.
Pass selected from the host form to show its position. A candidate outside the inclusive bounds receives a warning and no marker. The display does not validate availability or authorize a restore.

Use the same display timeZone as the restore form and pass a short timeZoneLabel where useful. All timestamps show seconds. Use BackupPicker for discrete backups, or Timeline for a history of restore operations.

name: DeploymentRegionPicker
description: Choose an available deployment region while keeping the current location visible.
code: <DeploymentRegionPicker label="Deployment region" name="region" value={region} onValueChange={setRegion} currentRegionId="frankfurt" recommendedRegionId="europe" regions={[{id:"europe",label:"Europe",scope:"automatic",location:"Automatic placement within Europe"},{id:"frankfurt",label:"Frankfurt",scope:"specific",location:"Germany",code:"eu-central-1"}]} />
notes: Supply eligible targets and provider codes from the host. Distinguish automatic placement within an area from a specific location. Disable ineligible rows with a visible reason.
Keep currentRegionId separate from the selected draft. Show a recommended region only when the host has a recommendation. A missing or unavailable draft does not submit a value.
Validate eligibility again when applying the draft. The host owns provisioning, migration impact and any confirmation needed before moving an existing service.

name: PaymentMethodPicker
description: Compare the estimated arrival and fee of available payment methods before choosing one.
code:
<PaymentMethodPicker label="Payment method" name="method" value={method} onValueChange={setMethod}
  methods={[{id:"standard",label:"Standard transfer",arrival:"Arrives in 2–4 business days",fee:"$0.00"},
    {id:"priority",label:"Priority transfer",arrival:"Estimated tomorrow",fee:"$8.00"}]} />
notes: Use before scheduling or reviewing a payment. Supply host-derived delivery estimates and fees in the displayed currency. An omitted fee is unavailable; supply zero explicitly for a fee-free method.
Show a restriction as unavailableReason. An unavailable or missing selected method does not substitute another method or submit a stale choice.
Choosing a card updates the draft. The host quotes, revalidates availability and fees, and applies any review or confirmation before initiating payment.

name: BackupPicker
description: Choose a discrete backup with its capture time and any reason it cannot be restored.
code: <BackupPicker name="backup" label="Choose a backup" required value={backupId} onValueChange={setBackupId} backups={[{id:"daily",label:"Daily backup",capturedAt:{dateTime:"2026-11-16T06:00:00Z",label:"Nov 16, 06:00 UTC"}},{id:"manual",label:"Before schema migration",capturedAt:{dateTime:"2026-11-15T18:45:00Z",label:"Nov 15, 18:45 UTC"}}]} />
notes: Use for a short list of actual snapshots. Supply stable IDs, localized capture labels with a time zone, and a concise reason when a backup is unavailable. The list follows the supplied order. Use RecoveryWindow for continuous point-in-time recovery.
Pass the accepted draft selection. An empty, absent or unavailable ID leaves the group unselected. When the selection disappears, the host reconciles its draft with the refreshed backups.

Review and confirm the restore separately. The host validates availability before submission and owns restoration, permissions and feedback. In an empty state the host can hide or disable the next step.

name: BackupRestoreDialog
description: Confirm the exact recovery point and where the restored database will be written.
code: <BackupRestoreDialog source={{project:"Billing production",kind:"snapshot",dateTime:"2026-11-16T06:00:00Z"}} destination={{kind:"new", project:"Billing recovery"}} timeZone="UTC" trigger={trigger => <Button {...trigger}>Review restore</Button>} onConfirm={requestRestore} />
notes: Use after selecting a snapshot with BackupPicker or validating a candidate against RecoveryWindow. Identify the source project, exact timestamp and destination before asking the user to commit.

Use replace for a database that will be overwritten and new for a separate restored copy. Add only the known operational impact, such as downtime or excluded storage objects. Supply an ISO timestamp with an explicit offset and a display time zone.

Keep source and destination stable during review. Revalidate permissions and point availability in the host before performing a restore. Supply unavailableReason when a refreshed selection is invalid. The component disables confirmation and describes the reason.
onConfirm requests a restore. Reflect the host's accepted, completed or failed result in the surrounding workflow.

name: ReviewRevision
description: Show whether an existing review covers the current revision and link to the relevant changes.
code: <ReviewRevision state="stale" reviewedRevision="7c00a18" revision="e709326" compareHref="/review/compare" />
notes: Use beside the review or approval evidence when the revision determines whether a previous decision still applies.
Pass the host's state separately from the revision identifiers. Rules may require or waive a new review. Include the earlier reviewed commit only when it is known and appropriate to show.
Use compareHref for the current diff or a comparison with the reviewed revision. Label the link to match that destination. Use CheckRunList for verification results on the current revision.

name: GitRef
description: An inline branch, tag or commit identifier for change and deployment records.
code: <GitRef kind="branch" value="feature/import-preview" preserveEnd={14} />
notes: Use for a Git identifier in an existing record. Supply the displayed value and the actual kind; localize kindLabel for assistive technology.
Use preserveEnd when the tail distinguishes branches with a shared prefix. A clipped identifier exposes the full displayed value on hover and keyboard focus.

Choose a host-supplied abbreviated commit ID only when it can identify the commit in context. Pass the complete hash when users need to inspect the full value. Use a separate Link or CopyButton for navigation or copying, and EnvironmentSwitcher for changing workspace scope.

name: CommitList
description: Commit messages, authors, dates and revision identifiers in a repository history.
code: <CommitList label="Release commits" copy commits={[{sha:"e7093261f30b80803d02f686d58cdefe040b3bc3",shortSha:"e709326",message:"Track file export retries",author:"Maya Chen",dateTime:"2026-11-16"}]} />
notes: Use for a Git commit history or the changes included in a release. Supply messages, full unique hashes and the order in which users should read them.
Pass href on records with a commit details destination. Pass shortSha only if the host has computed a sufficiently unique abbreviation in this repository.

Enable copy when users need the full hash for investigation or scripting. The copy action uses sha even if shortSha is displayed; localize copyLabels and commitKindLabel as needed. Supply an empty state when no records may be returned.

name: HttpExchangeDetails
description: Inspect request and response captures with a shared endpoint and outcome.
code: <HttpExchangeDetails method="POST" path="/api/v2/exports" outcome={{kind:"response",code:201}} duration="242 ms" request={{headers:[{id:"content-type",name:"content-type",value:"application/json"}]}} />
notes: Use in the detail pane for a selected request. Use HttpRequestRow in the list that opens it.

Pass authorized, redacted paths, headers and bodies. Use unique occurrence IDs to retain repeated headers in their original order. Treat an omitted body as uncaptured and an empty string as a captured empty body.

Keep Request and Response available while the selected record updates. Pending and no-response states show why response capture is unavailable. For a recorded HTTP response without a capture, give the known reason or use the neutral empty state.
The host owns selection, authorization, redaction, retrieval and transport. Compose a separate trace view from TraceWaterfall when users need per-service timing.

name: RowChangeDetails
description: Inspect the captured row snapshots from a database insert, update or delete.
code: <RowChangeDetails table="public.exports" event={{operation:"update",before:{coverage:"partial",row:{id:"exp_1042"}},after:{coverage:"complete",row:{id:"exp_1042",status:"ready"}}}} />
notes: Use in the inspector for a selected row event. For updates, switch between Before and After. Inserts and deletes expose only the applicable side.
Omit a capture when it is unavailable. Mark a capture partial when only some columns are present. Preserve captured null values. Missing columns do not establish a field change.

Supply only authorized, redacted row data. The host owns subscription, permissions and record selection. Enable searchable for larger captures or use ChangeList when you already know which fields changed.
Use labels and inspectorLabels to localize the two navigation levels. Key the view by event ID when switching between unrelated events should reset inspection.

name: HttpRequestRow
description: An HTTP request’s method, path, outcome and elapsed time in a diagnostic list.
code: <DataList aria-label="Recent requests"><HttpRequestRow method="POST" path="/api/v2/exports" outcome={{kind:"response",code:201}} duration="242 ms" source="api" /></DataList>
notes: Use a DataList for request inspection, or place EndpointLabel and HttpStatus in separate DataTable columns when users must sort by each attribute.
Pass only display-safe paths or route templates. Use preservePathEnd if different routes share a long prefix. Truncated paths can be inspected by hover or keyboard.
Use response with the actual status code. Use pending or no-response for requests without a response. Show elapsed time only when observed and pass a localized value with a unit.
Use the action slot for a named inspect or navigation command. Fetch payloads, handle filtering and apply redaction in the host.

name: HttpStatus
description: An HTTP response code with an optional readable reason.
code: <HttpStatus code={429} reason="Too many requests" />
notes: Use only when an HTTP response was received. Pass its actual code and supply a localized reason when the number needs explanation.
Codes remain visible regardless of their tone. For transport failure or a request that has not returned, use the actual state with StatusIndicator or nearby text.

name: InlineCode
description: A small monospace code fragment that participates in running text.
code: <Text as="p">Import <InlineCode>@/ui/button</InlineCode> in your project.</Text>
notes: Native code semantics, bundled monospace stack and a quiet inline surface. Content is text; no HTML parsing or syntax highlighting is performed.
wrap defaults to true for long identifiers. wrap=false preserves the fragment on one line and the host must manage overflow. Use CodeSnippet for blocks of code and Kbd for keyboard input.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Metric
description: A labeled value with optional contextual trend and supporting text.
code: <Metric label="Monthly revenue" value="$24,580" trend={{direction:"up",label:"12.8% higher",tone:"success"}} hint="Compared with the previous month." />
notes: Native definition-list semantics associate the label with its value, trend and hint. Values may be rich content; the host owns currency, number and locale formatting.

Keep the metric name short and recognizable at a glance. The label takes one line and reveals its full text on hover or keyboard focus when clipped. Use the unit, trend context or hint for supporting detail.
Pass unit for a quieter trailing unit on the same baseline, such as ms or GB. Keep prefixes and placement-sensitive symbols in the formatted value.

Use state=loading for a pending value and state=unavailable for a missing value. Pass value={null} when the application has no accepted value. The label stays visible and a localized loadingLabel or unavailableLabel is available to assistive technology.
Pass trend.context for the baseline or comparison period that belongs beside the change. It keeps the supporting text neutral even when the change has a semantic tone.

Trend direction and semantic tone are independent: a decreasing failure rate can be good. Its label must communicate the change without relying on the decorative arrow or color. No automatic percentage calculation is performed.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: MetricDelta
description: A compact directional comparison with an optional period or baseline.
code: <MetricDelta label="8% lower" direction="down" tone="success" context="vs last week" variant="chip" />
notes: Use for a change displayed on its own in a row or table cell. Inside Metric, MetricCard and MetricGroup use the trend object, which renders the same comparison.
Pass a localized label that says what changed. Direction describes the movement; tone describes its meaning for this measure. A drop in errors can be success.
Use plain when the value above already owns the emphasis. Use chip when the change needs a tint to stand out among adjacent values. Keep the period outside the tint.

name: MetricCard
description: A compact surface for a labeled measure, its comparison and optional history.
code: <MetricCard metric={{label:"Monthly revenue", value:"$24,580", trend:{direction:"up", label:"12.8% higher", context:"vs last month", tone:"success"}}} chart={<Sparkline label="Revenue dipped twice before reaching a six-month high" values={[19940, 22650, 21180, 23140, 21800, 24580]} />} />
notes: Use for a prominent metric in an overview or dashboard. Metric owns the label, value, unit and comparison. The card uses the existing Surface padding and elevation.

The label stays visible while the value, comparison and supplied chart render skeletons. Leave chartLoading unset for a shared request. Use chartLoading=true for pending history, including before a chart node exists, or false to keep valid history visible during an independent value request. An unavailable current value can still show available history.
Set chartMinHeight to the expected block size for a taller plot, including any visible caption, so the loading placeholder reserves the same space.
The default md value is the focal point. Use size sm in dense grids. The comparison period stays secondary and the chart reads after the value.
The inline layout moves the sparkline below the metric as available width decreases. Use stacked for a wide plot below the value. Omit the chart when there is no meaningful historical series.
Use a named Sparkline for the same measure. The displayed value, trend baseline and chart interval should agree with the data.

name: MetricGroup
description: Related measures with aligned values and an optional shared surface.
code: <MetricGroup label="API performance" appearance="panel" items={[{id:"requests",label:"Requests",value:"1.2M"},{id:"latency",label:"Response time",value:186,unit:"ms"},{id:"availability",label:"Availability",value:"99.98%"}]} />
notes: Use for related measures users read together. The items use Metric for labels, values, units and comparisons. Labels stay on one line. Use a short name with a recognizable start, and put the scope or period in supporting content. Clipped labels reveal the full name on hover and keyboard focus.

Use layout=rows in a drawer, sidebar or summary column. Labels share the start edge and values share the end edge. In very narrow containers, each value moves under its own label. Choose the layout independently of appearance.
Summary rows give longer values more width and scale the lg value down in compact containers. Check the longest localized number and unit at the actual panel width before selecting a size.
Each item can independently be ready, loading or unavailable. Keep real zero values visible and localize state labels when needed.
Use plain inside an existing section and panel for a shared standalone surface. Set minItemWidth when the localized values or units need more room. Tracks reflow based on available space.
Choose MetricCard for a measure that needs its own chart and surface. Supply stable item IDs and the group's accessible name.

name: Sparkline
description: A compact line or area chart for trends in a table cell, list or metric.
code: <Sparkline label="Revenue rose from $8,000 to $12,000" values={[8000, 8200, null, 9500, 11000, 12000]} domain={[0, 15000]} />
notes: Give the graphic a label that communicates the metric and the trend. Set showLabel to make that label visible.
Use a shared domain for comparing magnitudes across rows. Null and nonfinite samples leave gaps in both the stroke and area.
The default area uses an accent stroke with a gradient below it. Choose variant line for stroke only and use semantic tones only when the data has a known interpretation.

name: LineChart
description: A line or area chart for comparing trends on a shared scale.
code:
<LineChart label="Daily visits" categories={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"]}
  series={[{id:"this-week", label:"This week", values:[38, 55, 48]}]}
  domain={[0, 60]} variant="area" />
notes: The chart shows dates and a quiet dot grid by default. Enable showYAxis when numeric levels need to be visible at a glance.
Series names appear in the inspection readout. Set showLegend when the key needs to be visible before interaction.
Supply equally spaced categories in reading order and up to four named series with the same number of values. Null and nonfinite values leave gaps. Zero is an observation.

Use a shared domain containing all observations when comparing separate charts. Area shading belongs to the first series. Line styles distinguish the series independently of color. Set curve to linear for straight segments.
Explore values by hovering, tapping, or using arrow keys, Home and End. The default number format is English; supply formatValue and translated empty, missing and navigation labels for other locales.

name: BarChart
description: Grouped or stacked columns for comparing values across categories on a shared zero baseline.
code:
<BarChart label="Hours by team" categories={["Product", "Design", "Growth"]}
  series={[
    {id:"actual", label:"Actual", values:[38, 29, 46]},
    {id:"plan", label:"Plan", values:[32, 36, 40]}
  ]} />
notes: Use layout stacked for additive series. Positive and negative values accumulate independently on either side of zero. A custom domain must contain the cumulative bounds.

Use layout percent for nonnegative shares on a fixed 0–100% scale. The readout shows each share of the observed total and its raw value. A zero total leaves the column empty and shows raw zeros. Supply formatShare to localize percentages.
Series names appear in the inspection readout. Set showLegend when the key needs to be visible before interaction.
Pass up to four series in display order with one value per category. Put the primary series first to give it the accent fill. Comparison series use outline and dash styling as well as color.

Grouped columns start at zero and reserve empty slots for missing observations. In stacks, zero and missing observations take no space and remain distinguishable in the readout. Use the same domain to compare separate charts.
