code: <FilePath path="packages/workspace/src/views/export/ReviewPanel.tsx" />
notes: Use for a single path in a changed-file row, log or resource header. The directory shortens from the leading edge before the file name. A clipped value reveals the full path on hover or keyboard focus.

Pass a display-safe path. The slash is the default separator. Supply a backslash for Windows paths, including UNC paths. The component displays the path you give it without resolving filesystem segments.
Supply href if the complete path opens a single destination. Use Breadcrumb when users can navigate individual segments, and FileName for a bare name with its extension.

name: FileThumbnail
description: Decorative file artwork in an inline or tile frame with a stable fallback.
code: <Inline gap="2"><FileThumbnail src="/flood-mark.png" fit="contain" /><FileName name="Flood mark.png" /></Inline>
notes: Use inline presentation beside a filename and tile in a gallery or asset card. Keep a common tile ratio for comparable assets.
A generic file glyph remains visible when the image is missing, pending or unavailable. The reserved frame keeps its dimensions.
The frame is decorative and adds no focus stop. Render the file identity next to it. FileItem, UploadItem and FileCard use the same underlying component when given a thumbnail URL.

name: FileCard
description: A visual file gallery card with a stable thumbnail frame, file details and independent actions.
code: <FileCardGrid><FileCard name="Flood mark.png" thumbnailSrc="/flood-mark.png" thumbnailFit="contain" href="/flood-mark.png" size={1454337} /><FileCard name="Asset usage notes.pdf" size={27400} /></FileCardGrid>
notes: Use FileCard in a gallery when a visual thumbnail helps people recognize an asset. Use the same thumbnailRatio across peers and contain when the whole artwork must remain visible.
Thumbnails are top-aligned by default so wrapping titles and descriptions do not move the artwork. Use thumbnailPlacement=body when the file name should come first.
Use FileCardSkeleton when the record itself has yet to load. Match the intended thumbnail, selection and footer layout.
Missing, pending and unavailable images keep the same dimensions with a decorative file glyph. The host supplies thumbnail URLs and can use ImagePreview for a full inspection surface.

Use renderPreview to pass the card's named trigger to DocumentPreview, ImagePreview or ImageGallery. Set previewPlacement=thumbnail to place the same action in the artwork's top trailing corner. The default places it beside the footer commands. Keep the filename link, download and selection independent.
FileName preserves the extension when truncating. FileMeta owns the displayed format and size. Supply href for opening the file and downloadHref only for a separate download.
Pass the page locale through lang or provide formatSize when prerendering, so file sizes use the same formatting in the browser and on the server.
Pass selection for host-owned multi-selection. The checkbox, filename link and commands stay independent. Card owns the surface and heading level.

name: FileCardGrid
description: A responsive file gallery with aligned artwork and action rows.
code: <FileCardGrid><FileCard name="Flood mark.png" thumbnailSrc="/flood-mark.png" thumbnailPlacement="body" description="Website artwork" /><FileCard name="Usage notes.pdf" thumbnailPlacement="body" /></FileCardGrid>
notes: Pass FileCard and FileCardSkeleton as direct children. Use the same density, thumbnailPlacement and thumbnailRatio across peers.
The grid aligns headers, artwork and footers within each row. Use minItemWidth for the responsive minimum. At smaller widths, peer cards move to the next row in source order.
Set preserveColumns to retain responsive column widths as filtering or archiving leaves fewer cards. Explicit columns takes precedence.
Match the loading shapes to the expected cards and mark the gallery busy while it loads. Keep accepted cards visible during background refreshes.

name: FileItem
description: A named file row with size, type, thumbnail and independent actions.
code:
<FileList label="Attachments">
  <FileItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" size={2400000} mimeType="PDF" />
</FileList>
notes: Render inside FileList or another native list.
Pass thumbnailSrc for decorative artwork with a stable fallback. A caller-supplied thumbnail takes precedence.
Use nameOverflow="truncate" for dense rows with identifiable file names. FileName preserves the extension and reveals the full name when clipped.
Set metadataVariant=plain when the containing row already provides a surface. Pass format=null to omit the format when the filename already identifies it.
Set downloadHref for a separate download action when the filename or preview opens the record. Avoid exposing the same download twice.

Use renderPreview and pass its trigger directly to DocumentPreview, ImagePreview or ImageGallery. The overlay uses the row's named preview button. renderPreview takes precedence over onPreview. Return null from the callback to omit the preview action.
No file reading, object URL creation or uploading is performed.

name: FileList
description: A named native list of file rows.
code:
<FileList label="Attachments">
  <FileItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" size={2400000} mimeType="PDF" />
  <FileItem name="Logo.svg" size={18400} mimeType="SVG" />
</FileList>
notes: List contents and file identities are host owned. Narrow lists keep the thumbnail beside the filename. An individual command can stay alongside the name. Multiple actions move below the copy when space is limited.
Use stable host IDs for React keys; a name is not a unique file identity.

Use appearance=embedded in a message or activity entry for compact individual attachments. Use plain inside an existing surface and panel for a standalone group. All appearances preserve the same row behavior.

name: UploadItem
description: A host-controlled upload row with explicit progress and applicable actions.
code:
<UploadList label="Uploads">
  <UploadItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" size={2400000} state="uploading" progress={45} />
</UploadList>
notes: Queued, uploading, paused and processing can expose cancel. Failed or cancelled rows can expose retry. Settled rows can expose remove. Cancel and retry share a focusable action slot when both callbacks are present.

Supply onPause and onResume only when the transfer can pause and resume. The shared button keeps focus while changing its action. Known paused progress stays still. Unknown paused progress shows the status alone.
Use processing after the transfer finishes when scanning or processing is still pending. It has indeterminate progress and does not expose file preview or download.
A separate downloadHref and the preview supplied through renderPreview or onPreview become available when state is success.
The same nameOverflow option as FileItem controls the file name. The status and progress keep their own row.

Unknown progress is indeterminate. StatusIndicator and Progress share a line when the track has enough room. The track moves below a long status when space runs out. No network or upload queue is built in.

name: UploadList
description: A named native list of host-controlled upload rows.
code:
<UploadList label="Uploads">
  <UploadItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" state="uploading" progress={45} />
  <UploadItem name="Logo.svg" state="success" />
  <UploadItem name="Cover.png" state="error" error="Connection interrupted" />
</UploadList>
notes: Each row has its own state and stable host identity.
Use appearance=plain inside a drawer or panel that already has its own surface.
Cancellation, retry and removal callbacks are intents for the application.

name: UploadQueue
description: File intake, transfer states and actions in one scrollable queue.
code: <UploadQueue title="Uploads" listLabel="Files in queue" entries={uploads} picker={{label:"Add files", onFilesSelect:addFiles}} />
notes: Use for a visible queue with a heading and optional file intake. Entries use UploadItem and require a stable host ID even when two files have the same name.
Keep upload execution, validation, order and status in the host. Row callbacks request changes; the UI reflects the entries the host accepts.
Only the rows scroll when the list reaches maxListHeight. The heading and picker stay available. Removing a focused command moves focus to the nearest available row action or the picker.
When the picker is the next useful step, leave the empty list out. Pass emptyContent when users need a distinct empty-state message.

name: ImagePreview
description: A single-image preview in Flood Dialog with loading and failure feedback.
code:
<ImagePreview title="Flood mark" src="/flood-mark.png" alt="Pink Flood mark" zoomable
  trigger={props => <Button {...props} variant="subtle">Preview image</Button>} />
notes: Loads the image only while its dialog content is mounted.
The image fits without cropping by default. Enable zoomable when users need to inspect detail at the intrinsic size. The viewport scrolls independently. Localize actualSizeLabel and viewportLabel.
The host owns trusted URLs, object URL lifetime and download permissions.

name: ImageComparison
description: Compare two aligned image versions in one frame using a draggable divider or an opacity slider.
code: <ImageComparison label="Line version, visible percentage" ratio={2} before={{src:"/comparison-line.png",alt:"Weekly visits with straight line segments",label:"Line"}} after={{src:"/comparison-area.png",alt:"Weekly visits with a smooth area plot",label:"Area"}} />
notes: Use for the same subject rendered in two versions, such as an original screenshot and a proposed revision. Use crops with the same framing and aspect ratio.
Use swipe for comparing regions and mode=overlay to spot small shifts in alignment. In overlay mode the opacity slider sits below the images and the version labels identify its endpoints.
Both versions retain their alternative text. Give each a short visible name and label the slider for its mode, for example Original opacity in overlay mode.
On touch, drag horizontally to move the divider or tap to reposition it. A vertical gesture over the frame preserves the split.

The value describes how much of the before image to show. Home shows the after image and End shows the before image in full. The default is 50 percent. Use value and onValueChange when the host owns it. fit=contain preserves the whole frame.

name: CollectionCover
description: A passive cover with up to three images for a collection, folder or board.
code: <CollectionCover images={[{id:"trend",src:"/comparison-area.png"},{id:"overview",src:"/charts-share.png"}]} />
notes: Use this cover beside a visible collection name. Supply representative artwork in display order with stable IDs. The first image leads a three-image composition.
Artwork stays decorative. Use fit="contain" on an image when its full bounds matter. Zero images preserves the frame with a folder mark. Failed loads retain their tile geometry.
Use CollectionCard for a destination, or ImageMosaic when individual images must be independently inspectable.

name: CollectionCard
description: A card linking to a named collection with a stable visual cover and optional actions.
code: <CollectionCard title="Chart studies" href="/docs/charts" countLabel="2 images" artwork={[{id:"trend",src:"/comparison-area.png"},{id:"overview",src:"/charts-share.png"}]} />
notes: Use one native destination for the whole card. Give it the collection name and supply optional localized countLabel. Avoid text that repeats what the title or cover communicates.
Supply actions only for operations associated with the collection. They remain independently focusable and do not navigate.
Keep cover ratios and heading levels consistent across peer cards. Use CollectionCover alone inside an existing record or picker row.

name: ImageMosaic
description: Preview several images in a compact attachment grid and open any tile in one shared gallery.
code: <ImageMosaic label="Release screenshots" items={[{id:"overview",src:"/charts-share.png",alt:"Chart overview"},{id:"trend",src:"/comparison-line.png",alt:"Trend comparison"}]} />
notes: Use for related images attached to one message or record. Up to four tiles stay visible and the last tile shows the remaining count. Every source remains available in one ImageGallery.

Supply stable IDs, explicit alt text and small thumbnailSrc values when available. The original is used as a fallback thumbnail. For a single attachment, aspectRatio preserves useful framing within a bounded range.
Each tile opens its own source, including the last tile with a count. Closing the gallery restores focus to the opening tile. Use FileCardGrid when each asset needs independent metadata or commands.

name: ZoomControl
description: Step through viewport scales with a stable percentage readout and optional Fit action.
code: <ZoomControl value={zoom} onValueChange={setZoom} onFit={() => setZoom(1)} />
notes: Use beside a canvas or preview whose zoom is owned by the host. Pass scale factors, where 1 displays as 100%.
Pass increasing levels when the host has its own zoom stops. A fitting scale may fall between stops. The actions choose the next lower or higher allowed value and remain focused at an endpoint.
Use onFit only when the host calculates or already knows the fitting scale. Pass aria-controls for the associated viewport and supply a specific label when several zoom controls share a screen.

name: ThumbnailStrip
description: Choose the active image from a keyboard-accessible, scrolling strip of thumbnails.
code: <ThumbnailStrip label="Release screenshots" value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected} items={[{id:"trend",label:"Weekly trend",src:"/comparison-line.png"},{id:"overview",label:"Chart overview",src:"/charts-share.png"}]} />
notes: Use beside an existing inline preview or detail pane. The host owns the selection and preview content. Use ImageGallery when inspection belongs in a dialog.
Pass thumbnail-sized sources and short labels. Missing images keep the same tile dimensions. Omit value when no item is selected.
Arrow keys, Home and End move focus. Enter and Space request selection. The strip reveals the selected thumbnail without moving focus and its horizontal scrollbar overlays the content.

name: ImageGallery
description: Inspect a set of images in one dialog with a stable preview frame.
code: <ImageGallery title="Flood assets" items={[{id:"mark",src:"/flood-mark.png",alt:"Pink Flood mark"},{id:"charts",src:"/charts-share.png",alt:"Flood chart examples"}]} trigger={props => <Button {...props}>View images</Button>} />
notes: Use for related images that someone needs to inspect in sequence. Supply stable IDs, a trusted source and explicit alt text for each item.
Previous and next cycle through the set. Arrow keys work from gallery navigation and follow reading direction. Focus remains on the navigation control while the active image changes.

Use navigation=thumbnails when the artwork helps people jump to an image. Pass small thumbnailSrc files separately. Use thumbnailLabel if the image alt text is too long for a short control name. Arrow keys move thumbnail focus; Enter or Space opens it.
Only the active image is mounted. Loading, failure, fitted and intrinsic-size views reuse ImagePreview anatomy. Switching images resets zoom.
Use currentId and onCurrentIdChange for a host-controlled image. Default selection falls back to the first available item.
Localize the navigation labels and getPositionLabel when needed. Position receives a one-based index and the total image count.

name: ImageAltTextEditor
description: A controlled alt-text field with a bounded preview and an optional publishing limit.
code:
<ImageAltTextEditor image={{src:"/comparison-area.png",width:801,height:403,alt:"Weekly visits chart"}}
  name="alt" value={alt} onValueChange={setAlt} maxCharacters={160} />
notes: Use in a form or editor for a single image. Give the preview an independent accessible name or accepted description. The draft does not replace the preview's text alternative.
Pass value and onValueChange for the current image. Key or reset the draft when the host switches images. Use required if publishing requires a description, and reflect host validation through error.

Show maxCharacters only when the host has a limit measured in Unicode code points. The counter and invalid state share that unit. Text stays editable over the limit so the author can recover after pasting. The host validates, saves and decides whether an empty alternative is appropriate.
Use AltTextDisclosure to show an already-authored description.

name: AltTextDisclosure
description: An ALT action beside an image that opens its authored description in a dialog.
notes: Pass the same authored description to the image's native alt and to the disclosure. Empty or whitespace-only alt produces no control. Compose the action as a sibling of a preview trigger so the two actions remain independently reachable.
The dialog preserves paragraphs and uses the shared ScrollArea for long text. Escape and Close return focus to the action.
Localize title, triggerText, triggerLabel and closeLabel when needed. Include the visible triggerText in the accessible triggerLabel. Use Figure for a caption that should be visible to everyone.

name: DocumentPreview
description: Inspect a multipage document in one dialog with a scrolling page and finite navigation.
code:
<DocumentPreview title="Statement of work" pageCount={3}
  trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Preview document</Button>}
  renderPage={page => ({state:"ready", content:<Text as="p">{["Scope and delivery", "Schedule and milestones", "Acceptance criteria"][page - 1]}</Text>})} />
notes: Supply a known page count and a pure renderPage callback for the accepted one-based page. The host owns decoding, text layers, access, requests and cancellation.
Only the current page mounts while the viewer is open. Start page fetching in the host or in the mounted page component. Return loading or error with an optional page-local retry.
Previous and Next stop at document boundaries. Enter a page number and choose Go or press Enter for a direct jump. One page omits navigation and a zero count shows an empty state.
Use page and onPageChange for a host-managed page. Changing the accepted page resets the page viewport. Changing documents requires a new component key or a new controlled page.
The action slot can hold a named Link for downloading the whole document. Add localized navigation and state text through labels.

name: ImageMeta
description: Original pixel dimensions, with optional format and file size.
code: <ImageMeta dimensions={{width:1920,height:1080}} format="PNG" size={245760} />
notes: Use in a preview caption or asset details when pixel dimensions affect the decision. Pass the original image dimensions, not the dimensions of the thumbnail or displayed frame.
Supply format and bytes only when they describe that same asset. Use FileMeta when dimensions are unknown. Use variant=chip when the same metadata needs a quiet supporting surface in a compact row.
Use lang for number formatting and formatDimensions when the locale or product needs different wording. ImageMeta displays supplied facts and does not inspect the source image.

name: FileMeta
description: Compact file format and size, as a chip or plain secondary text.
code: <FileMeta format="PDF" size={2400000} />
notes: The format label is display metadata, not validated MIME detection.
Size uses SI units; formatSize customizes the text. Use plain when the surrounding attachment surface already provides separation. Missing values leave no empty slots.

name: TimePicker
description: A segmented time field with an anchored, keyboard-accessible list of clock times.
code: <TimePicker label="Start time" name="time" defaultValue="09:30" min="08:00" max="18:00" interval={1800} />
notes: Interval and step use seconds; the list contains at most 1000 entries.
Manual entry remains available; this is wall-clock time without timezone conversion.
One flat list, with selected-time visibility and a trailing action aligned with DatePicker.

name: DateTimeRangePicker
description: An ordered civil date/time range with four atomic form values.
code:
<DateTimeRangePicker label="Booking" startDateName="startDate" startTimeName="startTime" endDateName="endDate" endTimeName="endTime"
  defaultValue={{start:{date:"2026-10-27",time:"09:00"},end:{date:"2026-10-27",time:"18:00"}}} required />
notes: Incomplete and reversed ranges do not contribute accepted values.
No timezone or timestamp inference. Server availability remains host owned.
Only range and endpoint headings are visible; individual field names remain accessible.

name: Autocomplete
description: A free text field with optional suggestions; accepts values outside the list.
code: <Field label="Team">{control => <Autocomplete {...control} name="team" options={[{value:"design",label:"Design",group:"Product"},{value:"engineering",label:"Engineering",group:"Product"},{value:"operations",label:"Operations",group:"Business"}]} />}</Field>
notes: The submitted value is text, not an option ID. Use Combobox for fixed choices.
Manual suggestions use controlled value and optionsQuery; stale results cannot be chosen. Network ownership remains with the host.
Optional avatar data identifies a suggestion while its text label remains the value and accessible name source.

name: HoldToConfirm
description: A confirmation button with a hold-and-release shortcut and a dialog for ordinary activation.
code: <HoldToConfirm label="Discard draft" title="Discard this draft?" description="Your unsaved edits will be removed." confirmLabel="Discard draft" tone="danger" onConfirm={discardDraft} />
notes: Use for a known target with a short, predictable consequence. Use AlertDialog alone when the user must review a target, dependencies, or consequences before committing.
A primary pointer press fills the button in place. Release inside after holdMs to confirm once. Leaving the button, pointer cancellation, blur and Escape cancel the attempt.
A click or tap without holding and Enter or Space open AlertDialog with initial focus on Cancel. Localize the action labels, description, and visible hint.
The component calls onConfirm synchronously and exposes the dialog element through its ref. The host owns eligibility, in-flight disablement, outcome and recovery.

name: SwipeActions
description: A record row with contextual commands revealed by a horizontal swipe or a visible disclosure.
code: <SwipeActions label="Actions for Design review" actions={<Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onClick={() => console.log("archive")}>Archive</Button>}><TruncatedText>Design review</TruncatedText></SwipeActions>
notes: Place one or two secondary commands in the actions slot. Use named IconButtons where width is limited and match the action size to the disclosure.
Swipe toward inline start to reveal commands or press the visible disclosure by mouse, touch or keyboard. Escape closes the rail and returns focus to the disclosure.
A swipe only opens or closes the rail. The host owns each command, including confirmation or undo for destructive actions.
Keep record labels on stable lines and preserve enough width for them when open. Use a Menu for a longer action list, or set swipe=false when the parent already owns a horizontal gesture.
Use open and onOpenChange when a host needs to coordinate disclosure across rows.

name: OverflowActions
description: A priority-based action row that moves commands into a More menu when space is limited.
code: <OverflowActions label="Document actions" shape="pill" items={[{id:"save",label:"Save",priority:10},{id:"duplicate",label:"Duplicate"},{id:"archive",label:"Archive"}]} />
notes: Compose commands rather than links. Higher priority remains visible longer; source order is preserved.
Uses existing Toolbar, Button, IconSlot and Menu; hidden measurements are inert and excluded from the accessibility tree.
shape defaults to pill; rounded restores the field-radius Toolbar shell. Available width excludes Toolbar padding.

Use morePresentation=auto when shortening the More trigger can keep additional commands directly visible. The label remains when it fits the same commands. Use icon for a consistently icon-led rail. The trigger keeps its accessible moreLabel and keyboard behavior.
containerVariant="plain" delegates a surface-free rail to Toolbar, keeping peer control heights aligned; contained is the default. variant still styles the actions themselves.

name: BulkActionBar
description: A single-row selection command capsule with adaptive overflow.
code:
<BulkActionBar label="Selected projects" selectionCount={2}
  items={[{id:"archive",label:"Archive",priority:10},{id:"pause",label:"Pause"},{id:"activate",label:"Set active"}]}
  onAction={(id) => console.log(id)} onClear={() => console.log("clear")} />
notes: The default is a pill-shaped single row with at most two visible commands. maxVisibleActions accepts 1, 2 or 3; available space can reduce that number further.
Lower-priority commands move to More. selectionLabel, clearLabel and moreLabel support localized content; selectionCount=0 renders nothing.
The pill hugs the visible controls. Use morePresentation=auto to preserve visible commands under width pressure, or icon for an icon-led rail. The clear action uses a named ghost icon.
pending disables commands and clearing. The host owns selected IDs, accepted updates, confirmation and focus after removal.

Use placement=viewport for a fixed bar at the bottom center with safe-area insets. Mount outside transformed ancestors that would constrain fixed positioning. Reserve any needed scroll clearance in the base layout. The default placement is inline.

counter accepts label (default), number or none. Visible counters reserve a stable width across digit changes; counterWidth adapts that reservation to a localized label. Numeric mode retains the complete accessible selectionLabel. Hidden mode removes the slot.

name: Menubar
description: Coordinated desktop application command menus with roving triggers and shared open state.
code: <Menubar label="Editor commands" menus={[{id:"file",label:"File",items:[{id:"new",label:"New document"},{id:"export",label:"Export"}]},{id:"edit",label:"Edit",items:[{id:"undo",label:"Undo"},{id:"redo",label:"Redo",disabled:true}]}]} />
notes: Arrow keys coordinate enabled menu triggers; child menus reuse Menu focus and dismissal.
Use native links and NavigationList for destinations, not Menubar. Controlled openValue may refuse transitions.

name: FilterCondition
description: One controlled predicate for a choice, text, number or date operand.
code:
<FilterCondition label="Condition 1"
  properties={[{id:"status",label:"Status",options:[{value:"active",label:"Active"},{value:"paused",label:"Paused"}]}]}
  value={{property:"status",operator:"is",values:["active"]}}
  onValueChange={(condition) => console.log(condition)} />
notes: Compose one finite-choice condition from Fieldset, Field, Grid, Select, MultiSelect and IconButton. sm is the default; all controls share controlSize.

value and onValueChange are controlled. Changing the property proposes an empty values array; changing the operator preserves selected values. Empty values are an incomplete draft, never an instruction to match every record.
The host owns query evaluation, duplicate-property policy, Apply/Cancel, validation and focus after removing the row. onRemove is optional; no removal slot is reserved when omitted.

label names the condition group. hideLabel defaults to true; property/operator/value controls retain their accessible names. labels customizes control names, operator text, placeholder and removal text.
A wide host uses one row with a wider value track. Container-based reflow follows the space available to this row, including inside a popup or drawer. No extra background or border is added.
This version supports finite enumerated values and is/is-not predicates. Date, text, numeric operators, nested groups, remote fetching and query execution are not part of this component.

Use mode="typed" for text, number or date operands alongside optional choice properties. Each operator belongs to its operand kind. A property change creates a fresh operand, while an operator change preserves the existing value.

name: FilterGroup
description: An editable flat group of choice or typed filter conditions with All and Any matching.
code:
<FilterGroup label="Project conditions"
  properties={[{id:"status",label:"Status",options:[{value:"active",label:"Active"},{value:"paused",label:"Paused"}]}]}
  value={{match:"all",conditions:[]}} onValueChange={(filters) => console.log(filters)} />
notes: Composes FilterCondition, SegmentedControl, Fieldset, Stack, Inline, Button and IconSlot. The group adds no separate material or decorative nested container.
value and onValueChange are controlled. Stable condition IDs survive row edits and removals; new rows propose an enabled available property and empty values. Empty values remain an incomplete draft.
All/any is shown only with at least two conditions. Removing rows preserves the selected match value. An empty group offers Add condition; it does not invent an onboarding message.

Duplicate properties are prevented for new choices by default. allowDuplicateProperties enables them; maxConditions optionally limits additions. Existing accepted rows are never silently deleted when constraints change. Add remains visible and disabled when no additions are available.

Accepted additions focus the new property control. Accepted removal focuses a surviving neighbour or Add. Refused controlled proposals do not move focus or mutate accepted conditions; delayed acceptance must not steal focus from a different target.
label names the group, hideLabel defaults to true, labels localizes group controls, and conditionLabels localizes each row. controlSize defaults to sm; disabled blocks all edits.
The host owns Apply/Cancel, accepted query evaluation, persistence, validation and server semantics. This is a flat finite-choice editor, not a nested query engine.
Use mode="typed" on the group for mixed choice, text, number and date conditions. Keep condition IDs when editing a draft.

name: CollectionToolbar
description: Search, applied filter summaries and filter disclosure in one collection query row.
code:
<CollectionToolbar label="Project collection" searchValue="" onSearchValueChange={(search) => console.log(search)}
  searchLabel="Search projects" appliedFilters={[{id:"status",label:"Status: Active"}]}
  onRemoveFilter={(id) => console.log(id)} onClear={() => console.log("clear")} />
notes: Composes Fieldset, Field, SearchInput, Inline, TagGroup, Popover, Button and IconSlot. Uses normal Tab order rather than the action-only Toolbar roving model. No additional material, title or result count is invented.

Use appliedFilterDisplay.maxVisibleTags when many accepted conditions compete for the query row. Localize moreTagsLabel and fewerTagsLabel in the same object. Expanding the count leaves the accepted query intact.

searchValue and accepted appliedFilters are host-owned. onSearchValueChange, onRemoveFilter and onClear request changes; callbacks do not imply acceptance. Summaries need meaningful labels and unique IDs.

filterContent supplies the existing filter editor, including FilterGroup or a project-specific form. The host retains draft validation, Apply/Cancel, query evaluation, persistence and saved views. filtersOpen/onFiltersOpenChange optionally control the existing Popover; filterPanelRef and filterPanelClassName support real panel focus and sizing.

Clear keeps its space immediately before the right-anchored Filters trigger while inactive. Removing a summary or clearing returns focus to Filters, or Search when no panel exists. Filter disclosure is omitted when no filterContent is supplied.

quickFilters is an optional slot for at most two task-important properties; larger property sets belong inside filterContent. The host owns the threshold and slot behavior. Supply canClear when active state is not represented by searchValue/appliedFilters, such as controls in that slot.

Search, accepted summaries and commands share a responsive row. The actions slot places table commands, such as Columns, next to Filters. Saved-view selectors and save/rename actions stay outside this query row.

Use align="end" when a sibling such as a view selector or status switcher occupies the start of the row. Search, quick filters, summaries and commands form an end-aligned group and wrap in their original order as space runs out.

Use align="split" when search leads a wide collection and secondary filters and commands form the trailing group. On narrow widths the search takes its own row and the other controls follow in reading order.

controlSize defaults to sm and sizes the built-in controls. For a compact desktop query row, match host Select controlSize and Button size to that scale explicitly. Choose a larger size when the task and input need it. disabled applies to the complete fieldset, including native quick-filter controls and panel descendants. Labels and summaries remain host-localizable.

name: CollectionViewSwitcher
description: A controlled view selector with adaptive commands, separate from the active filter query.
code: <CollectionViewSwitcher label="Project view" views={[{id:"all",name:"All projects"},{id:"active",name:"Active projects"}]} value="all" onValueChange={(id) => console.log(id)} actions={[{id:"create",label:"Save as new view"}]} onAction={(id) => console.log(id)} />
notes: Compose Field, Select, Button, IconSlot, Inline and OverflowActions. controlSize defaults to sm; no extra surface surrounds the selector and commands.

value and onValueChange represent the accepted view ID. Commands request onAction(id); the component does not create, rename, delete, persist or execute queries. Keep application errors and confirmation in their existing host owners.

The host supplies only applicable actions: save a new definition, update an editable changed definition, reset a dirty query, rename or delete an editable definition. A dirty working query does not silently modify the selected definition.

One action uses Button directly. Multiple actions use priority-based OverflowActions with View actions disclosure at constrained widths. Source order remains meaningful; destructive actions belong last.

label names the hidden Field label. actionsLabel and moreLabel localize command names; views supply localized names. selectRef exposes the Select focus target for host-owned dialogs. disabled blocks selection and commands; per-view and per-action disabled flags remain supported.
Keep this row outside CollectionToolbar. Changing the selected view may reset the host query and selection, but saving or renaming a definition must not reset unrelated result selection.
The command rail uses the shared plain Toolbar variant so its outer height matches the adjacent Select, without a second container around the actions.

name: Sidebar
description: A bounded workspace sidebar with grouped destinations, a compact rail and nested navigation flyouts.
notes: Composes NavigationTree, ScrollArea, IconButton, Stack and Text. Host controls height; header/footer remain fixed while the navigation body scrolls with reserved scrollbar clearance.

collapsed/defaultCollapsed/onCollapsedChange control the full-width versus compact rail. Controlled refusals preserve accepted geometry. side supports logical start/end; width affects expanded mode only. collapsible=false omits the toggle.
groups need unique IDs and globally unique item values. Destinations retain real links; expansion and currentValue are independent. Disabled items cannot navigate or open a branch.
Expanded destinations default to labelOverflow=truncate and reveal clipped names from the existing links or buttons. Set labelOverflow=wrap where labels need to remain fully visible.

expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues/onExpandedValuesChange retain branch disclosure across width changes. In compact mode a top-level branch opens a Popover with full navigation; choosing a destination closes that flyout. No route is inferred or persisted.

header/footer accept content or a ({collapsed}) render function. Adapt meaningful content using that state, rather than hiding arbitrary descendants with CSS. The host owns workspace/account menus and their actions.
The inline headerLayout puts the expanded identity and toggle on one row. The stacked default keeps the toggle in its original place across states. Enable branchGuides per group for dense nesting.

Item icons use IconSlot; trailing content can compose Badge or other meaningful metadata in expanded mode. Compact destinations retain accessible names and native title labels; missing icons have a neutral fallback glyph.

No automatic mobile drawer, routing, resizing, keyboard shortcut or preference storage is added. Check the bounded host, enlarged text, RTL, final scroll item, real destinations and focus across collapse/flyout transitions.

groups can hide a redundant visual label with hideLabel while preserving the navigation name. currentKind="location" marks a global module; page is the default contextual destination. The workspace playground composes Sidebar profiles into GlobalRail plus ContextBar without duplicate flyouts.

variant defaults to quiet in the 0.2.11 candidate: muted inactive content, normal control weight and restrained rectangular selection through existing semantic roles. standard retains the stronger pill recipe. Both compose the same primitive anatomy and behavior; inspect them in the full-width navigation workspace.

name: KeyValueRow
description: One editable key and value with optional enablement and local validation.
code:
<KeyValueRow value={{id:"accept",key:"Accept",value:"application/json"}}
  onValueChange={pair => console.log(pair)} />
notes: Use KeyValueRow when a host already owns the list and row actions.
Use a stable id and provide row-specific labels when several pairs share the same form.

name: KeyValueEditor
description: A controlled editor for request headers, variables and other keyed values.
code:
<KeyValueEditor label="Request headers"
  value={[{id:"accept",key:"Accept",value:"application/json",enabled:true}]}
  onValueChange={pairs => console.log(pairs)} showEnabled />
notes: Use KeyValueEditor when people add or remove several key–value pairs. Keep host IDs stable across updates, including when keys are edited.
Pass validation errors by row id. The host owns duplicate-key policy, persistence and secret handling.
Set valueMode to multiline for values such as certificates or multi-line variables.

name: ServiceLevelTargets
description: Track independent service-level deadlines and outcomes for one record.
code:
<ServiceLevelTargets label="Support targets" now="2026-11-16T11:49:00Z" timeZone="UTC" targets={[
  {id:"reply",label:"First response",state:{phase:"met",completedAt:"2026-11-16T10:42:00Z"}},
  {id:"resolve",label:"Resolution",state:{phase:"running",deadline:"2026-11-16T12:00:00Z",warningWithinMinutes:30}},
]} />
notes: Name one target per row and supply a shared clock and effective zoned deadlines. The host calculates schedules, business hours and pause rules. A paused target shows the reason when known.
Use met or missed for the recorded outcome. A missed target can have a completion time when the work happened after its deadline. Keep the missed status when adding that time.
Use DeadlineStatus alone for one running deadline in a compact record cell. Use Timestamp for ordinary dates without a timing state.

name: DeadlineStatus
description: Time remaining, due soon, overdue and paused states with an exact due date.
code:
<DeadlineStatus deadline="2026-11-16T12:00:00Z"
  now="2026-11-16T11:49:00Z" warningWithinMinutes={30} />
notes: Use DeadlineStatus for urgency around a due time. Use Timestamp for an ordinary date in a record.
Supply an explicit offset for deadline and now. The host owns updates, working calendars and pause semantics.
Keep the exact deadline visible unless the same information appears next to this status.

name: IncompleteResponseNotice
description: Explain why a response stopped early and keep any available output in context.
code: <IncompleteResponseNotice output="partial" reason="output-limit" />
notes: Use inside the response region when an attempt has reached a terminal incomplete state. Keep partial output in place. Use output=none when the attempt stopped before producing usable visible text.
Map the host reason to output-limit, message-limit, filtered or unknown. Keep normal streaming, user cancellation, request errors and automatic continuation in their own states.

Pass one applicable host action, such as Continue, Review limits or Edit request. Keep action authority, pending state and request configuration in the host. Use the shared announcement prop only when a parent does not announce the same outcome.

name: DeprecationNotice
description: A persistent notice with an affected feature’s lifecycle state, published cutoff and replacement.
code: <DeprecationNotice state="deprecated" cutoff={{dateTime:"2026-12-01",label:"Dec 1, 2026"}} replacement={{label:"/v2/exports",href:"/docs/exports-v2"}}>The v1 endpoint accepts requests until the cutoff.</DeprecationNotice>
notes: Place next to the affected feature so users can act on the cutoff and replacement. Use a short title when surrounding context does not identify the feature. Use children for concrete effects or next steps.

Pass the service’s accepted lifecycle state and published cutoff. Use an ISO civil date or zoned date-time with a localized visible label. Omit cutoff or replacement when the service has not published them.

Supply a destination when the replacement has documentation. The link opens information about the replacement. When switching affects stored configuration, provide the appropriate host-owned action or form separately.

Use inline appearance in a compact existing surface. A banner suits a persistent warning at the point of use. Leave announcements off for static content and choose a live policy only when the notice actually changes.

name: RelativeTimeRangePicker
description: Switch between a rolling window and a pair of absolute date-time endpoints.
code:
<RelativeTimeRangePicker label="Time range"
  value={{mode:"relative",relative:{amount:24,unit:"hour"},absolute:{start:{date:"2026-11-15",time:"12:00"},end:{date:"2026-11-16",time:"12:00"}},timeZone:"UTC"}}
  onValueChange={range => console.log(range)} />
notes: Keep the relative window as an amount and unit when saving a rolling filter. Resolve it against the host clock only when applying the query.
Use DateTimeRangePicker when a product accepts an absolute civil interval only.
The host owns time-zone conversion, daylight saving ambiguity and query submission.

name: ToolCall
description: Show a tool invocation and its status, with independently inspectable request and result details.
code: <ToolCall title="Search workspace files" state="succeeded" input="Export policy" output="3 documents found." />
notes: Use for a named invocation in a conversation or execution log. Keep state on the same mounted call and pass the host's actual queued, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled value.
The default flush variant shares the surrounding surface. Use framed for an isolated call on a flat canvas.

Pass display-safe input and output as text or a Flood inspector. If state is failed, output is presented as error detail. Omit inspection details when the viewer has no useful detail to inspect; the status is still shown.

Use open and onOpenChange for controlled disclosure. Use announce for individual calls only when the host has no separate progress announcement. Execution, retry, authorization and redaction belong to the host.

name: ToolCallGroup
description: A compact activity summary with an independently inspectable list of tool calls.
code: <ToolCallGroup title="Workspace search" calls={[{id:"search",title:"Search files",state:"succeeded",output:"3 documents found."},{id:"read",title:"Read export policy",state:"running"}]} />
notes: Group calls from one visible step in an agent workflow. Use stable invocation IDs in host order. Use ToolCall for an individual invocation and ActivityTimeline for broader record history.
The collapsed summary names active and failed counts when present. Use formatSummary for localized counts or to show a distinction such as cancellations. Empty groups are omitted.
Keep group disclosure and each nested call independent. Provide only display-safe request and result content. Optionally enable one group announcement when host progress announcements are absent.

name: JsonInspector
description: Browse JSON values by branch, search their contents and copy a value at a known path.
code: <JsonInspector label="API response" value={{status:200,next:null,items:["Flood"]}} />
notes: Use JsonInspector for structured JSON with branch navigation. Use CodeSnippet to show raw JSON meant to be read or copied in full.
Selection returns an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer so the host can link to a nested value. Pass data or errors from the application.

name: DiffStat
description: Compact counts of added and removed lines in a file or patch.
code: <DiffStat additions={128} deletions={22} showDistribution />
notes: Pass nonnegative line counts for the exact file, patch, or filter scope the user is reviewing. Use zero for a known empty count.
Keep the signed counts in lists and table cells. Enable showDistribution when the ratio aids scanning and there is room. The bar shows relative composition, not total patch size.
Localize visible numbers with formatValue and the spoken summary with formatLabel. Use CodeDiff for the source lines.

name: ChangedFileList
description: An index of changed files with direct diff links, line counts and independent review state.
code:
<ChangedFileList label="Files in export review" currentId="panel" files={[{
  id: "panel", path: "src/views/export/ReviewPanel.tsx", href: "/review/files/panel",
  changes: { additions: 2, deletions: 1 }, reviewed: false,
}]} />
notes: Use as the file index for a multi-file review. Give each file a stable ID, path and route or fragment. Set currentId to the diff the host is displaying. For fragments, give the target a matching ID and tabIndex={-1}.
The path opens the diff. Review state is a separate control when onReviewedChange is supplied. Update the controlled file record when the review state is accepted.
Omit changes for files without meaningful line counts, and reviewed when review state does not apply. Use CodeDiff for the source changes.

name: CodeDiff
description: Read prepared source changes in a unified or side-by-side view with expandable unchanged lines.
code:
<CodeDiff label="projects.ts" hunks={[{id:"route",lines:[
  {id:"before",kind:"removed",oldLine:9,text:"return get('/projects');"},
  {id:"after",kind:"added",newLine:9,text:"return get('/v2/projects');"}
]}]} />
notes: Use CodeDiff for prepared source lines with their original numbers. Use ValueChange or ChangeList when reviewing named record fields.
Keep each source line as one entry without its line terminator. The host owns parsing, file navigation and publication of comments.
Use a single view in a narrow panel. Choose split when both versions have room or when horizontal scrolling is appropriate. The context toggle preserves focus and lines keep their source numbers.
For a line-specific action, render an explicitly named action and use the supplied before or after side to attach it to the correct source.

name: FindBar
description: Navigate and optionally replace matches within a document or editor.
code:
<FindBar query="project" matchCount={3} activeMatch={2}
  onQueryChange={query => console.log(query)}
  onPreviousMatch={() => console.log("Previous")}
  onNextMatch={() => console.log("Next")} />
notes: Use FindBar when the user needs to move among matches in existing content. Use SearchInput when they filter a collection or start a search.
Pass the match count and one-based active position from the host. The host applies flags, manages document mutations and keeps the active match in view.
Enter and Shift+Enter in the query field navigate results. Supply a queryError for an invalid expression, and check recovery when the query becomes valid again.

name: RecordRelationSuggestion
description: Review a proposed relationship with its target record, reason, and independent decisions.
code:
<DataList density="compact" aria-label="Suggested relationships">
  <RecordRelationSuggestion title="Delayed warehouse callbacks" reference="FUL-213" href="/issues/ful-213" relation="Possible related issue" reason="Both reports mention carrier callbacks timing out after a retry." onDecision={handleDecision} pendingDecision={pendingDecision} error={decisionError} />
</DataList>
notes: Place inside DataList. The title link opens the record independently of either decision. Supply a short reason grounded in evidence the person may see.

Supply pendingDecision for the submitted action. Keep the row available and pass error if the host refuses the request. Update the accepted relationship or remove the dismissed suggestion after success, moving focus to an appropriate remaining target when the row disappears.
Use RecordRelations for accepted links and RecordRelationForm for manually choosing a target. Open a separate review for operations that merge, close or transfer records.

name: RecordRelations
description: Direct relationships to other records, grouped by direction and meaning.
code:
<RecordRelations label="Relationships" groups={[
  {id:"prerequisites",label:"Blocked by",items:[{id:"carrier",reference:"FUL-212",title:"Certify the carrier feed",href:"/issues/ful-212",status:{label:"In progress",tone:"info"}}]},
  {id:"dependents",label:"Blocking",items:[{id:"pilot",reference:"FUL-241",title:"Start warehouse pilot",href:"/issues/ful-241"}]}
]} />
notes: Name each group from the viewpoint of the record the reader has open. Keep incoming and outgoing links in distinct groups, and place symmetric relationships in a group such as Related.

Use stable group IDs and item IDs unique within a group. Add reference when readers use an identifier as well as the title to recognize the linked record. Set groupHeadingLevel to fit the document outline.

Pass an href for a native link, and omit it when the record can only be shown as text. Add a named status when it helps the reader decide what to open or follow up on. The host owns ordering, data, permissions and mutations.

Empty groups collapse. Supply emptyContent when the containing section should explain that there are no relations. Use DependencyGraph when readers need to follow prerequisites through multiple records.

name: RecordRelationForm
description: Choose a relationship direction and search eligible target records.
code:
<RecordRelationForm aria-label="Add relationship"
  source={{id:"pilot",title:"Start warehouse pilot",reference:"FUL-241"}}
  kinds={[{id:"blocked-by",label:"Blocked by"},{id:"related",label:"Related"}]}
  targets={[{id:"carrier",title:"Certify the carrier feed",reference:"FUL-212"}]}
  value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft} onSubmit={relation => { /* Save this relationship in the host. */ }} />
notes: Label directions from the viewpoint of source. Use concise per-kind descriptions when direction or effects would otherwise be ambiguous. Use the record reference to disambiguate names and search by ID.
The current source is excluded. When a new kind disallows the selected target, the draft clears its target. Use kindIds to describe which kinds are eligible for each target.

Keep the draft on refusal. The host owns permissions, cycle and duplicate checks, changes to the original record, and saving. Use RecordRelations for the accepted links and DependencyGraph for wider dependency paths.

name: DependencySchedule
description: Compare two project dates and flag a start that conflicts with its prerequisite’s finish.
code: <DependencySchedule predecessor={{label:"Carrier certification",finish:{date:"2026-11-20",kind:"forecast"}}} successor={{label:"Warehouse pilot",start:"2026-11-17"}} />
notes: Use for one finish-to-start relationship. The predecessor must finish by the successor's start. Equal dates are aligned at calendar-day granularity. For constraints with time of day, business-day calendars or buffers, use the host's schedule assessment instead.
Supply civil dates in YYYY-MM-DD, and mark a forecast finish explicitly. Omit a missing date to show an incomplete check. Do not substitute today or a guessed date.
Use RecordRelations for navigation among direct links and DependencyGraph for multi-record paths. The host owns computed forecasts, permissions and rescheduling.

name: DependencyGraph
description: A dependency map for jobs, records or assets, with an equivalent list view.
code:
<DependencyGraph label="Release jobs" nodes={[
  {id:"build",label:"Build",status:{label:"Passed",tone:"success"}},
  {id:"test",label:"Test",dependsOn:["build"]},
  {id:"publish",label:"Publish",dependsOn:["test"]}
]} />
notes: Pass a directed acyclic graph with stable IDs and known prerequisite IDs. Nodes without links or an activation handler are read-only.
Use the same IDs and dependsOn contract for CI jobs and table lineage. Choose the example in the preview to compare them.
Provide a list presentation for a tight panel or when readers need to scan exact prerequisite names. Graph connections carry the same relationships through accessible descriptions.
Keep execution, routing and graph mutations in the host. Use a native href when the node opens a destination.

name: ServiceRuntimeStatus
description: Show whether a scale-to-zero service is sleeping, waking or running, with reported startup timing.
code: <ServiceRuntimeStatus title="Export worker" state={{phase:"waking",since:"2026-11-18T09:53:00Z",elapsedMilliseconds:2100}} />
notes: Use for the reported runtime of one service that can sleep. Treat sleeping as expected idle behavior and wake-failed as a reported startup failure. Use unknown when current runtime data cannot be read.

Supply explicit-offset timestamps and measured durations. Waking may show elapsed startup time, and Running may show the completed startup measurement. Omit missing measurements and preserve an actual zero.

The host owns service state, requests and polling. Enable announce only for a monitored runtime view. Use DeploymentHealthCheck for the readiness probe of a deployment and ServiceAvailability for a public health overview.

name: DeploymentHealthCheck
description: Inspect whether a deployment passed its readiness check and what the endpoint returned.
code: <DeploymentHealthCheck state={{phase:"checking",path:"/ready",timeoutSeconds:60,elapsedSeconds:28,lastProbe:{kind:"http",code:503,reason:"Warming up"}}} />
notes: Pass the deployment phase from the host. A recent HTTP error can occur while a check is still running. A missing probe means there is no result to display; use no-response for a known attempt without an HTTP response.
Pass elapsed time only when known. The bar during checking represents time spent against the timeout, not readiness. Use not-configured only when the host reports no check configured.

Use in deployment details alongside the stage or logs. The host owns probes, timing and rollout decisions. Use ServiceIncident for published service health and DeploymentHistory for multiple deployments.

name: RestartPolicyEditor
description: Configure when a service automatically restarts and how many failure restarts it can attempt.
code:
<RestartPolicyEditor value={policy} onValueChange={setPolicy}
  modeName="restartPolicy" limitName="maxRestarts" maxAllowedRestarts={10} />
notes: Use in one service’s runtime settings. On failure restarts after an unsuccessful exit, Always handles any stop, and Never leaves the service stopped.
Retain maxRestarts in the controlled draft when switching modes. Validate and submit it only for the on-failure mode. Native forms omit the limit in the other modes.
Pass mode restrictions and the upper bound from service policy. An unavailable current mode stays visible with its reason and requires a supported replacement. The host saves and applies the policy.

name: ReplicaAllocation
description: Edit planned replica counts by region under a shared service limit.
code:
<ReplicaAllocation title="Regional replicas" regions={regions} minimum={1} maximum={4}
  onReplicaChange={(id, replicas) => setRegions(current => current.map(region => region.id === id ? {...region, replicas} : region))} />
notes: Pass all assignable regions and their whole replica counts, including zero for an available unused region. Use minimum and maximum for service-wide limits. When a policy changes and the current total is outside its bounds, steps that move the total toward the allowed range remain available.

The summary counts planned replicas, not running instances. The host owns the draft, resource permission checks and the application of a reviewed plan. Pair with StagedChanges when pending changes need review.
Use lockedReason to explain a count fixed by policy. Use DeploymentRegionPicker when the task is to choose a single region.

name: DeploymentHandoff
description: Compare the previous and replacement releases while service moves between them.
code:
<DeploymentHandoff label="Production deployment handoff"
  previous={{id:"deploy-41",label:"Stabilize preview exports",revision:{kind:"commit",value:"e709326"}}}
  replacement={{id:"deploy-42",label:"Restrict export link access",revision:{kind:"commit",value:"f5bc452"}}}
  state={{phase:"draining",expectedEnd:{dateTime:"2026-11-16T14:32:00Z",timeZone:"UTC"}}} />
notes: Keep the two named releases and their IDs stable through the handoff. Pass preparing while the previous release is serving. Use overlapping or draining only after the replacement is serving, using the phase reported by the service.

Use completed when the previous release stops and the replacement is serving. Use failed for a failed replacement with the previous release still serving. The component does not represent a failure of both releases.

Treat expectedEnd as an estimate for the current overlap or drain, and refresh state from the host. Use DeploymentHistory for a service's history, DeploymentHealthCheck for a readiness probe, and RolloutAllocation to edit a traffic split.

name: DeploymentHistory
description: Deployment records for one service or environment, with revision, outcome and optional per-record actions.
code: <DeploymentHistory label="Production deployments" deployments={[{id:"run-42",label:"Verify export permissions",status:"failed",description:"Health check timed out."},{id:"run-41",label:"Stabilize preview exports",status:"active",revision:{kind:"commit",value:"e709326"}}]} />
notes: Use for the outcomes of multiple deployments in one service or environment. Keep the record order and IDs stable while the host refreshes status.
Mark a record active when it is serving traffic. A queued, building, deploying or failed attempt can be visible alongside the active deployment. Use superseded after another deployment takes over.

Use href to open one deployment. Supply a short failure reason when it helps triage. Use PipelineRun for the stages and diagnostics of that one deployment, and CommitList for the source changes included in it.

Expose eligible actions through renderActions. The host owns authorization, confirmation, mutation and announcements for those actions. Supply emptyContent for an empty environment and statusLabels to localize phases.

name: ReleaseTargetMatrix
description: Compare a release’s rollout across targets with the version currently serving in each.
code: <ReleaseTargetMatrix caption="Rollout of v2.14.0" targets={[{id:"production",label:"Production",live:{label:"v2.13.0"},status:"failed",detail:"Readiness check timed out."},{id:"staging",label:"Staging",live:{label:"v2.14.0"},status:"released"}]} />
notes: Use for one named release across multiple environments, services or channels. Name the release in the caption. Use DeploymentHistory for multiple attempts in one target.

Supply the host-reported rollout status and live release independently. A failed attempt can leave a previous release live. Use null for a confirmed empty target, and omit live when its serving version is unknown.
A live release can link to its details. Supply a short useful reason beside a failed outcome. Keep target IDs and order stable during updates.
Use DeploymentHandoff for one service's overlap or drain. Use PipelineRun for stages within one attempt. Localize captions, column labels, and statuses.

name: EvaluationResult
description: Inspect one test verdict, its expected and actual outputs, and the supporting checks.
code: <EvaluationResult title="Route a refund request" outcome="failed" expected={<CodeSnippet code={'{"queue": "billing"}'} />} output={<CodeSnippet code={'{"queue": "general"}'} />} checks={[{id:"route",label:"Correct queue",status:"failed",detail:"Refund requests belong in Billing."}]} />
notes: Use in a test result detail view. Show expected and actual content at the same level. Their labels remain attached as the comparison stacks on narrow widths.

The host supplies the overall outcome and the independent check results. Use failed when completed checks reject the output, and error when execution fails. State the cause under the verdict when it is known.

Omit expected when there is no reference output, and omit output when unavailable. To show an intentionally empty output, supply an explicit visible representation. Pass display-safe data and use CodeSnippet for exact code or JSON.

name: CheckRunList
description: Parallel verification results with links to evidence and host-reported blockers.
code:
<CheckRunList label="Checks for this revision" blockingLabel="Blocks merge" checks={[
  {id:"types", label:"Type check", status:"passed"},
  {id:"browser", label:"Browser tests", status:"failed", blocking:true, href:"/checks/browser"},
  {id:"package", label:"Package verification", status:"not-reported", blocking:true},
]} />
notes: Use for independent verification results attached to one revision. Use PipelineRun when sequence and stage diagnostics describe a single execution.

Pass blocking from the host separately from status. An absent report, a skipped run and a neutral result are distinct. Whether a result blocks work depends on the host's policy and the revision being reviewed.
Include a link when it takes the reader to the corresponding result or log. Use the detail to show a short cause the reader needs before opening the evidence.

name: PipelineRun
description: Inspect the status, elapsed time and diagnostics of an ordered run.
code:
<PipelineRun label="Production deployment stages" stages={[
  {id:"build",label:"Build image",status:"succeeded",duration:"42 s"},
  {id:"migrate",label:"Apply migrations",status:"failed",duration:"8 s",
    description:"The database rejected a duplicate key.",
    details:{label:"Migration logs",content:"23505: duplicate key violates unique constraint"}},
  {id:"deploy",label:"Deploy service",status:"skipped"}
]} />
notes: Pass stages in execution order with stable IDs. Distinguish queued work from skipped work using the status reported by the host.
Supply localized duration strings when they are available. Keep the failure reason visible and give optional diagnostics a stage-specific disclosure label.
The host owns execution, polling, retries and live announcements. Use DependencyGraph to show prerequisites or Steps to help people navigate a task.

name: RetrySchedule
description: Show when a failed operation will be retried automatically or when its retry budget has been exhausted.
code: <RetrySchedule state="scheduled" nextAt="2026-11-16T12:06:00Z" relativeTo="2026-11-16T12:04:00Z" remaining={2} />
notes: Use beside a failure or attempt history when users need to decide whether to wait or intervene. Place the same record's manual retry action next to this status when the host permits it.
Render it when the service reports a scheduled retry or confirms retries are exhausted. Include nextAt and remaining only when known. Include the scheduled attempt in remaining.
Pass a zoned relativeTo instant for relative time and exact-time inspection. Use DeliveryAttempts for previous outcomes. The host owns clocks, execution and retry permission.

name: DeliveryAttempts
description: Review the outcome, time and receiver response of each attempt to deliver one event.
code:
<DeliveryAttempts label="Invoice webhook delivery attempts" attempts={[
  {id:"try_1",number:1,dateTime:"2026-11-16T12:00:00Z",status:"failed",response:"HTTP 503 Service Unavailable"},
  {id:"try_2",number:2,dateTime:"2026-11-16T12:01:00Z",status:"delivered",response:"HTTP 204 No Content"}
]} />
notes: Use one list for an event and destination. Pass stable attempt IDs, actual attempt numbers and a display order chosen by the host.
Use an explicit timestamp offset and display zone. Keep a short response or connection error visible and put authorized request or response details inside an optional disclosure.
Use RetrySchedule for the next automatic retry or an exhausted retry budget. Use retryAction when the host allows manual redelivery. Update attempts once the service accepts or reports a new try.

name: StackFrame
description: A call frame with its exact source location and optional surrounding code.
code: <DataList density="compact"><StackFrame frame={{id:"request",functionName:"loadProject",path:"src/projects.ts",line:19,column:8,source:[{line:19,text:"  return request(projectId);"}]}} /></DataList>
notes: Use StackFrame inside DataList when a larger diagnostics surface already owns frame order and scrolling.
Pass already resolved source lines and use one-based source locations. Source-map resolution, redaction and navigation belong to the host.
Omit source for a frame with no display-ready context. The location remains visible and the disclosure is omitted.

name: StackTrace
description: An ordered call stack with exact locations and independent context disclosure.
code: <StackTrace label="Request stack" frames={[{id:"request",functionName:"loadProject",path:"src/projects.ts",line:19,column:8},{id:"router",functionName:"handleRequest",path:"src/router.ts",line:6}]} />
notes: Provide frames in the order reported by the runtime. Retain stable IDs across updates so a frame keeps its expansion state.
Body lines share their compact text and scroll treatment with source review. Verify the marked source line and independent expansion at the actual panel width.
Use LogViewer for a stream of events, and CodeDiff for changes between two source versions.

name: LogRow
description: A log entry with severity, a precise time, and an optional payload disclosure.
code:
<DataList density="compact">
  <LogRow entry={{id:"req_95b",dateTime:"2026-11-16T12:00:09Z",severity:"error",source:"storage",message:"Upload exceeded size limit",payload:"Status 413"}} />
</DataList>
notes: Render a standalone LogRow inside DataList. Use LogViewer for a stream of several entries.
Pass a time with an explicit offset and use timeZone to display it in the intended zone.
Redact and authorize payload data in the host before passing it to a row.

name: LiveFollowControl
description: Pause or resume following an incoming stream, with an optional count of new entries.
code: <LiveFollowControl following={following} queued={unseenCount} onFollowingChange={setFollowing} />
notes: Place it beside the heading or search tools of a stream whose viewport is controlled by the host. Use LogViewer for a log stream that already manages its own viewport and follow control.
Keep following separate from the transport connection. Pausing preserves the reading position and may still allow the host to receive entries. Show a count only when it can be computed reliably.
On resume, reveal the newest entries inside the intended scroll region. Keep focus on the control, and localize the count with formatQueued and state and action text with labels.

name: LogContext
description: Inspect entries before and after a selected event while preserving its reading position.
code: <LogContext label="Logs around the selected request" anchor={selected} before={earlierEntries} after={laterEntries} earlier={{onLoad:loadEarlier,pending:loadingEarlier,exhausted:noEarlier}} />
notes: Use in a detail surface opened from search results. Keep the original query and scroll position in the host so the reader can return to the result.

Pass chronological entries on both sides with unique, stable IDs. Exclude the anchor from both arrays. Initial positioning begins at a row boundary when the anchor fits. The selected row stays marked and prepending earlier entries preserves its viewport position within the available scroll range.
Supply either boundary when it can load more. Keep an exhausted boundary mounted when it was focusable, so the reader can tell they reached the available range.
Retain environment and service constraints when fetching context. Authorization, fetching, deduplication and error recovery belong to the host.

name: LogViewer
description: A bounded event stream with pause, return to the latest log, and optional message search.
code: <LogViewer label="Runtime log" searchable entries={[{id:"req_95b",dateTime:"2026-11-16T12:00:09Z",severity:"error",source:"storage",message:"Upload exceeded size limit",payload:"Status 413"}]} />
notes: Append events in chronological display order with stable IDs. Keep transport, filtering and retention in the host.
Scrolling away from the latest entry or opening a payload pauses auto-follow. New entries remain visible via the count and the resume action.
Choose a maximum viewport height for the screen. Feed a bounded window of entries and keep the focused row in that window while it is being inspected.

Enable searchable for literal, case-insensitive search in the provided messages. Matches count rows and leave surrounding events visible. Search pauses following until the reader resumes it. Use host-side search for archived entries, sources and payloads.

name: DatabaseWebhookForm
description: Choose a database table, row events and HTTP destination for a webhook.
code:
<DatabaseWebhookForm aria-label="New database webhook" draft={draft} onDraftChange={setDraft}
  tables={[{id:"exports",label:"public.exports"}]}
  onSubmit={request => { /* Validate endpoint policy and create the webhook on the server. */ }} />
notes: Use for one source table and one or more insert, update or delete events. Use stable table IDs and qualify labels with the schema where names can repeat. A removed or disabled table cannot submit.

The editor accepts HTTP or HTTPS destination URLs without embedded login credentials. Keep secrets in host-managed authentication. The host owns endpoint allowlisting, network access, delivery method and payload policies.
Keep the controlled draft after rejection and supply the host error. Use DeliveryAttempts for inspection after a webhook has been configured.

name: EnvironmentCreationForm
description: Create an empty environment or duplicate an eligible source with its copy scope visible.
code:
<EnvironmentCreationForm aria-label="New environment" draft={draft} onDraftChange={setDraft}
  sources={[{id:"staging",label:"Staging",copyDescription:"Copies service configuration. Databases start empty."}]}
  onSubmit={request => { /* Validate and create the environment in the host. */ }} />
notes: Use for a new environment that can start empty or duplicate an eligible source. Use EnvironmentSwitcher when an existing environment changes the scope of the workspace.
Describe what each source actually copies and call out surprising exclusions such as database data or sealed values. Pass an unavailable reason for visible but restricted sources.
Keep the controlled draft when a request is rejected. Revalidate the unique name, source eligibility and copy policy in the host. Empty requests omit the dormant source ID.

name: LogExportForm
description: Choose the format and row limit for a bounded export of the current log query.
code:
<LogExportForm aria-label="Download logs" draft={draft} onDraftChange={setDraft}
  formats={[{id:"csv",label:"CSV"},{id:"json",label:"JSON"}]} rowLimits={[100,500,1000]}
  range={{kind:"fixed",label:"Nov 16 · 09:00–12:00 UTC"}}
  onSubmit={options => { /* Request an authorized export of the current query. */ }} />
notes: Place beside log search results or in a short dialog opened from their toolbar. Preserve the current source, filters and sort order when submitting the export.

Use a fixed range when the query already has time bounds. Otherwise offer recent windows supported by the service. A fixed-range request omits lookbackSeconds even if the draft retains an earlier recent choice.

Supply supported formats and positive row limits from the host. Set pending during export and keep the draft on failure. The host applies authorization, redaction and retention, and delivers the downloaded file.

name: UnitNumberField
description: A controlled quantity and measurement unit with paired editing.
code:
<UnitNumberField label="Package weight" value={{amount:500,unit:"g"}}
  units={[{value:"g",label:"g"},{value:"kg",label:"kg"}]}
  onValueChange={quantity => console.log(quantity)} amountName="weight" unitName="unit" />
notes: Use one controlled value for amount and unit. Set both name props for native submission.
The host owns conversion. Changing the selected unit leaves the entered number intact.

name: SpanRow
description: Compare an operation's start and duration on a shared numeric time axis.
code:
<DataList density="compact">
  <SpanRow span={{id:"cache",label:"Cache lookup",start:102,duration:93}} domain={[0,300]} />
</DataList>
notes: Pass milliseconds relative to one origin and the same domain for comparable spans.
A visual mark is clipped to the domain while the original start and duration remain available.
Render a standalone SpanRow inside DataList. Use TraceWaterfall for nested spans with a common axis.

name: TraceWaterfall
description: Nested operation timings with a shared axis, independent branches, and optional span zoom.
code: <TraceWaterfall label="Request trace" spans={[{id:"request",label:"GET /files",start:0,duration:640,children:[{id:"cache",label:"Cache lookup",start:102,duration:93}]}]} />
notes: Normalize start and duration to milliseconds from one trace origin. Every span retains its own measured values.
Use domain for a selected time window. The default domain includes collapsed spans so disclosure preserves the row and axis geometry.
Pass a controlled zoom ID to zoom to a duration span and restore the original domain. Keep branch collapse independent of zoom.
Use WaterfallChart for accumulated increases and decreases. For operation durations on a shared axis, use TraceWaterfall.

name: DatabaseSessionList
description: Inspect database sessions, observed lock waits and the sessions holding those locks.
code:
<DatabaseSessionList label="Database sessions" sessions={[
  {id:"sync",label:"Inventory sync",pid:1428,state:"active",lockWait:{blockers:[{id:"console",label:"Admin console"}]}},
  {id:"console",label:"Admin console",pid:1372,state:"idle-in-transaction"},
]} />
notes: Pass session state and observed lock waits separately. A confirmed wait keeps its Waiting for lock status even when the blocker is outside the visible scope. An idle session is different from a session idle in a transaction.

A blocker matching a visible session links to its row. Pass href when it has another authorized destination. A known blocker without a destination remains text. Give reused process IDs stable session IDs and a short display label that distinguishes sessions.

Pass display-safe operation summaries and durations that describe the measured interval. Use renderActions for authorized, session-specific actions. The host owns policy, confirmation, sampling, refresh and any termination request.
Use QueryPlan for execution operations and SessionList for account sessions.

name: IndexRecommendation
description: Review the estimated planner cost of a proposed index and copy its SQL.
code:
<IndexRecommendation title="Index open orders by customer"
  estimate={{total:{before:128.32,after:24.6},startup:{before:0,after:0.29}}}
  sql={"CREATE INDEX ON public.orders (customer_id) WHERE status = 'open';"} />
notes: Pass before and after estimates for the same query, collected under comparable conditions. A startup increase can coexist with a lower total. Keep both values visible when the advisor reports them.
Planner cost uses the engine's own cost scale. Use separate measured evidence if you need to report latency. Provide an exact, display-safe script and let the user copy it for review.
Use QueryPlan to inspect underlying execution operations. The host owns authorization, migration review and applying changes.

name: QueryPlan
description: Inspect a query’s operation tree, estimates and observed execution measurements.
code:
<QueryPlan label="File search execution plan" root={{
  id: "scan", label: "Index Scan", source: "files_project_idx",
  estimatedRows: 90, estimatedCost: 42.5,
  actual: { rows: 128, durationMs: 4.816, loops: 1 },
}} />
notes: Give the viewer a normalized tree with stable, unique IDs. The component selects an operation for inspection. The host owns fetching, parsing and executing queries.

For PostgreSQL, pass the operation’s total estimated cost and measured per-loop values. Estimated cost is in planner units. The inspection pane shows timing in milliseconds and keeps loop count separate.
Omit actual when only estimates are available. Keep actual zero values when a measurement exists. Use TraceWaterfall for durations on a shared timeline.

name: SuggestionTextarea
description: A text area with keyboard-operable mention and command suggestions anchored to the caret.
code:
<Field label="Reply">
  {field => <SuggestionTextarea {...field} value="@" onValueChange={draft => console.log(draft)}
    suggestions={[{trigger:"@",label:"People",items:[{id:"maya",label:"Maya Chen",insertText:"@Maya Chen"}]}]} />}
</Field>
notes: Use SuggestionTextarea for @ mentions and / commands inside an existing draft. Use CommandPalette for global navigation and commands.
Keep suggestions controlled by the host and handle selected entity IDs using onSuggestionSelect. The inserted text remains ordinary editable text.
Include a description when a handle, team or command preview helps distinguish suggestions. Plain mentions use a compact panel; richer options preserve room for both lines.
Use the same suggestions props on MessageComposer when it already owns the editing surface. Verify keyboard selection, composition input, Escape and insertion between existing text.

name: QueryInput
description: An inline search field for free text and structured conditions with suggestions at the caret.
code: <QueryInput label="Search requests" value={draft} onValueChange={setDraft} tokens={tokens} onTokenRemove={removeToken} resolveSuggestions={resolveSuggestions} />
notes: Use QueryInput when users type field constraints alongside free text or direct identifiers. Use SearchInput for plain text and FilterGroup for visible condition rows.
Keep the parser, candidate labels and values, token conversion and query execution in the host. Supply the replacement range at the caret and keep stable IDs for committed tokens.
