Expose invalid fragments with QueryToken.error. Removing a token preserves the draft and moves focus back to it. Verify completion between existing words, selection, Escape, and IME input.

name: MeetingAvailability
description: Compare one proposed meeting time against attendee availability and local time zones.
code: <MeetingAvailability label="Attendee availability" slot={{start:"2026-11-16T16:00:00Z",end:"2026-11-16T16:45:00Z"}} attendees={[{id:"maya",name:"Maya Chen",timeZone:"America/New_York",availability:"available"}]} />
notes: Use to review a proposed slot beside the controls that choose the time. Pass start and end as ISO instants with explicit offsets and specify IANA time zones from the host.
Local dates can differ for the same slot. The time range includes the date and zone. Omit the zone when it is unknown and use unknown when availability was not shared.
Supply attendance and availability from the host. Busy, outside work hours, and unknown are distinct states. Use attendee details for useful qualifiers and avoid exposing private event titles.

name: TimeZoneSelect
description: Search named time zones and see their offsets at a supplied instant.
code: <TimeZoneSelect aria-label="Time zone" name="timeZone" defaultValue="America/New_York" referenceTime="2026-11-16T12:00:00Z" options={[{value:"UTC"},{value:"America/New_York",aliases:["Eastern"]}]} />
notes: Pass a zoned referenceTime for offset display at the relevant day. Updating the reference changes the offset label without changing the accepted zone identifier.
Supply product-relevant IANA choices and optional local names or aliases. A named zone remains the submitted value.
Convert absolute or civil inputs and resolve ambiguous local times in the host.

name: TemplatePicker
description: Review the fields a template will fill or replace before applying it.
code:
<TemplatePicker value={template} onValueChange={setTemplate}
  templates={[{id:"incident",label:"Incident report",scope:"Operations",fields:[{id:"priority",label:"Priority",value:"High",replaces:true}]}]}
  onApply={id => { /* Apply this template to the host draft. */ }} />
notes: Use beside a record draft when users need to know which fields a template will fill. Name the team, workspace or other scope when it distinguishes options.
Set replaces only for fields whose existing values will change. Preserve the current draft until Apply template or Replace fields is activated and the host has accepted that intent.
Keep the selected template after a failed application. The host resolves permissions, fields and values, checks conflicts again before replacing content, and owns saving the resulting draft.

name: ModelPicker
description: Search model choices by name, provider or technical identifier.
code:
<ModelPicker aria-label="Model" name="model" defaultValue="northstar-core"
  models={[{id:"northstar-core",label:"Core",provider:"Northstar",modelId:"core-v2",description:"Text and image input"},
    {id:"meridian-core",label:"Core",provider:"Meridian",modelId:"meridian-core-2",unavailableReason:"Workspace access required"}]} />
notes: Supply stable host IDs and recognizable provider names. The committed label includes the provider. Differentiate revisions from one provider in their option labels and use modelId for the technical search term.
Use a short capability that changes the decision as the option description. Supply unavailableReason to show a blocked option and explain why it cannot be selected.
For remote search, pass selectedModels so the field keeps the chosen descriptor across result pages. The host owns provider access and validates the model again before running a request.

name: ContentLanguagePicker
description: Search and choose the languages of a post, document or other piece of content.
code:
<ContentLanguagePicker aria-label="Post languages" name="language" locale="en"
  languages={[{code:"en"},{code:"th"},{code:"ja"}]} defaultValue={["en","th"]} />
notes: Supply the locale tags accepted by the host. Localized names, endonyms and tags are searchable. The supplied tags remain the submitted values, including script or region subtags.

If language detection is available, pass its result as the initial draft and let the author correct it. One item can have several languages. Store the author’s accepted tags separately from the language of the application.

Give the picker a visible label through Field in an ordinary form. Use maxVisibleTags where many selections would crowd an editor. Removing a tag changes the language metadata; it does not alter or translate the content.

name: QuietHoursEditor
description: Edit the weekdays and local time window when notifications are paused.
code: <QuietHoursEditor timeZoneLabel="New York time" value={schedule} onValueChange={setSchedule} />
notes: Weekdays identify the start of each quiet window. With 22:00–07:00 on Monday, notifications pause Monday at 22:00 and the window ends Tuesday at 07:00. Equal endpoints are ambiguous and the editor asks for a different end time.
Use one shared window across the selected days. Turning quiet hours off disables editing while retaining the supplied draft. Use SnoozeMenu for postponing a single inbox item.

The host owns the IANA time zone, daylight-saving policy, validation of incomplete drafts, saving and actual delivery. Pass a recognizable time zone label and translate the field labels in localized interfaces.

name: HandleField
description: Edit a public handle with a fixed service domain or a full custom domain.
code: <HandleField name="handle" value={handle} onValueChange={setHandle} domain="studio.example" required />
notes: Pass domain for a fixed service suffix. The controlled value is the editable name and native form submission includes the full handle. Omit domain when users enter a full custom domain.
Supply availability results for the exact full handle. A response for an earlier draft stays hidden.
The host owns the allowed syntax, availability lookup and save validation. Use DomainVerification when users must prove domain ownership.

name: CronScheduleField
description: Edit a cron expression and inspect the scheduler’s upcoming runs.
code:
<CronScheduleField name="schedule" value={expression} onValueChange={setExpression} timeZone="UTC"
  result={{expression:"0 9 * * 1",timeZone:"UTC",state:"ready",summary:"Mondays at 9:00 AM",upcoming:["2026-11-23T09:00:00Z"]}} />
notes: Use for a scheduler that accepts a cron dialect. Supply validation for the exact draft and time zone. The field suppresses results from earlier drafts.

Pass explicit instants for upcoming runs in chronological order. Use an empty upcoming array only when the scheduler reports no occurrences in its preview window. Omit upcoming when the preview could not be computed.
The host owns cron grammar, recurrence, zone rules and save validation. Use RecurrenceEditor for ordinary schedules without expression syntax.

name: RecurrenceEditor
description: Edit a repeating daily or weekly schedule with optional end date or occurrence count.
code: <RecurrenceEditor label="Repeat" value={{frequency:"week",interval:2,weekdays:["mon","wed"],ending:"never",untilDate:"",occurrences:null}} onValueChange={value => console.log(value)} />
notes: Keep one controlled value with valid active fields and optional dormant drafts. Weekly frequency requires at least one day.
Pass names for native submission. The weekday name repeats for each selected day. Inactive end date or count fields are absent from submission.
Keep time zones, holiday exceptions and generation of actual occurrences in the host.

name: MediaTrimRange
description: Choose a contiguous clip using start and end handles over an optional waveform.
code: <MediaTrimRange label="Trim recording" labels={{start:"Start",end:"End",length:"Clip length"}} duration={42.5} minimumLength={0.5} value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />
notes: Pass the source duration and a bounded range in seconds. The handles stay at least minimumLength apart. The chronological direction stays left to right. Arrow keys move one second, and Shift plus arrow moves one millisecond.
Supply display-resolution peak samples across the whole source to help users find boundaries. Keep the accepted range in the host and use it for previewing or exporting the clip.
Use MediaSeekBar to change the playhead. Use MediaTrimRange to edit which interval will be retained.

name: MediaChapterList
description: Jump to named sections of a recording and follow the current chapter.
exampleState:
const [time, setTime] = useState(12);
  const chapters = [{id:"intro",label:"Overview",start:0},{id:"details",label:"Compare periods",start:29.5}];
code:
<Stack gap="3">
  <MediaSeekBar label="Playback position" duration={94} currentTime={time} chapterStarts={chapters.map(chapter => chapter.start)} onSeek={setTime} />
  <MediaChapterList label="Chapters" chapters={chapters} currentTime={time} onSeek={setTime} />
</Stack>
notes: Supply stable IDs, short titles and strictly increasing start times in seconds. A chapter stays active from its start until the next chapter begins. An empty list renders nothing.
Share the host's accepted currentTime and onSeek with MediaSeekBar. Use disabled until seeking is available. A seek request alone does not change the active chapter.
Add decorative thumbnails when they help distinguish chapters. Use MediaTranscript to show spoken lines or captions.

name: MediaSeekBar
description: Scrub a recording with elapsed time, duration and optional buffered intervals.
code: <MediaSeekBar label="Playback position" duration={84.5} currentTime={time} buffered={[[0,28],[45,68]]} onSeek={setTime} />
notes: Pass the accepted playback time and duration in seconds. Handle onSeek in the player and feed its time updates back to MediaSeekBar. The control follows the timeline from left to right, including in RTL interfaces.

Pass every buffered interval separately so gaps remain visible. Buffering is informational, so seeking is available across the known recording duration. Pass chapterStarts for visual landmarks and MediaChapterList for named chapter destinations.
Omit duration until it is known. The timeline is designed for finite recordings. For a transcript, pass the same currentTime and onSeek to MediaTranscript so both views stay synchronized.

name: MediaTranscript
description: A timed transcript that follows playback and seeks to the selected line.
code:
<MediaTranscript label="Transcript"
  cues={[{id:"intro",start:0,text:"Begin with the overview."}]}
  currentTime={0} onSeek={time => console.log(time)} />
notes: Keep cue IDs stable and sort cues chronologically. The host supplies playback time and seeks when a cue is activated.
Follow playback only while reading is synchronized. Offer a clear way to pause and resume as users review earlier lines. Pass a query to mark literal matches without removing context.
Use the actual player as the media owner. This component renders timed text, without loading media or parsing subtitle files.
